items.sum: Editorial reviewing the first post-war track season, Harry Churcher's and Derrick Burfitt's championship results, the Junior Section's new captain, and hopes for the 1947 Diamond Jubilee year.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial reviewing the first post-war track season, Harry Churcher's and Derrick Burfitt's championship results, the Junior Section's new captain, and hopes for the 1947 Diamond Jubilee year. The first post-war track season has been a busy one, and the results show that Belgrave can still be reckoned a major club. This is not surprising when we consider our wartime track performances, and with men coming back from the Forces we should be stronger still next year. Some of our returning men have not come up to their pre-war performances, but they all appreciate that their acclimatization to civilian life takes some time, especially those who have been overseas. A number of them were at their best right at the end of the season, and they are confident that with judicious winter training they will surpass their previous performances. In this respect the Wednesday evenings Physical Training and Lectures at Belgrave Hall should be helpful, and it is hoped that as many members, especially Juniors, will attend. A full programme of Championships was held, but none of our members gained any wins for the Club in either the Southern or A.A.A. Senior Championships. Harry Churcher was unfortunate to come up against one of the Swedish cracks in the 2 and 7 Miles' Walking Titles, both of which he won in 1939. Harry was second in the 2 and third in the 7, and we are all very pleased to see him back in his old form. Coming to the Junior Championships, we find, once again, the name of Derrick Burfitt at the head in the 1 Mile, he won both National and Southern titles. Derrick will still be eligible for these titles next year. The Club Championships and Handicaps gave us some keen racing and there were some good performances in Club Matches. There is still room for improvement in the support given to Club Handicaps. In days of old we had to have heats in a Club 880 yards Handicap to prevent overcrowding; there are plenty of gaps the Hon. Handicappers will be pleased to fill. The thoughts of the Athletic World are turned towards the next Olympic Games, to be held in London in 1948. The thoughts of those athletes who are aspiring to being selected should be there already! The peak of condition required of an Olympic athlete can only be gained by careful planning and training. The selectors no doubt have their eyes on all possible contestants, and several of our crack men are being watched and their performances noted. The European Games, recently held in Oslo, give some idea of the standards to be aimed at. At the Annual General Meeting a number of new officers were elected. One of the key positions is that of a responsible Senior to take charge of the Juniors. A great deal of thought has been given to the Junior Section. The choice of Juniors for official club posts is made difficult owing to National Service; a year ago we elected Alan Bishop as Junior Captain, and he was promptly called up! This years' Junior Captain is Eddie Short, and we hope that he will have the active support of the Juniors, and the moral support of the Seniors. The administration of the Juniors, i.e., notification of fixtures, travelling arrangements, etc., will be in the hands of the Sectional Hon. Secretaries, who will work in close touch with Frank Webb, who will be keeping a fatherly eye on them in general. We are very proud of our Junior Section, and, judging by their performances, they will be shaking the Seniors up before they are much older. The Club Officers are an extremely hard-working lot indeed. Much of their work consists of correspondence. All members can help them by replying promptly to all correspondence requiring an answer, e.g., when you have been selected for a team and cannot turn up, the sectional secretary should be notified so that substitutes can be arranged. The winter season is now in full swing and we are getting good musters at Belgrave Hall. Our runners will do their utmost to retain their many Championships, including the English and Southern titles. The walkers will strive to regain the Championships we have held in the past. Our respective captains, Bert Footer and Charlie Churcher, will have watchful eyes over their men and will be pleased to advise any member on training, etc. The year 1947 will be the Club's Diamond Jubilee, and it would be very fitting if we were to make a clean sweep of all the National Team Trophies; it would also make it a memorable year of office for our esteemed President, Harry Parker. e: London to Brighton and Back Walk
items.s: NOTES Club notes on training arrangements, badges, publicity, magazines, social plans, committee elections, the new Hon. Medical Adviser, members' health, the 24 Hours' Walk Centurions, the Brighton walk supporters' coach, the new R.W.A. 10 miles championship, Tom Carter's injury and Harry G. Churcher's letter of thanks for Life Membership. Belgrave Hall is open for training every Tuesday and Thursday evening. Tooting Bec Track is open on Wednesday evenings from 7 o'clock. Tuesday training round our pre-war course over Rotten Row, Hyde Park, will be held from The Duke of York's Territorial H.Q. Track Dressing Room, King's Road, Sloane Square, S.W.3 (nearest station, Sloane Square) at 7 o'clock, with Bert Footer, pack leader. There will also be a training pack for walkers. * * * * The question of Club Badges, normally in the hands of the Hon. Treasurer, is now being handled by his assistant, Tommy Morrell. Vests are not yet obtainable but badges (cloth and metal for buttonhole) can be obtained from him. * * * * It is most important that the Club should get publicity in the local press. We already have a number of members doing very good work in this direction, but more volunteers are needed. The President or the Hon. Secretary will be pleased to hear from anybody who can help. Club Notes already appear in the South London Press, South Western Star and Wimbledon Borough News. * * * * The new monthly magazine, Athletics, is now well established and needs no introduction to most members. For those not acquainted with Athletics, it is published by John Langdon Ltd., 40 Maida Vale, W.9, and is edited by one of our members, P. W. (Jimmy) Green; the annual subscription for twelve issues is ten shillings, post free. The walkers are still catered for by Race Walking Record, which has now been going strong since 1942. The subscription is seven shillings for twelve monthly copies (H.M. Forces, five shillings), from A. D. McSweeney, 102 East End Road, Finchley, N.3. * * * * The Club cannot yet resume its full programme of Social events, as Belgrave Hall is not in a fit state to undergo the strain of a Social Evening. When the repairs have been done our Social Secretary, Dave Shepherd, will be gettings things going. Before the war Belgrave was famed for its Socials, and Dave is confident of restoring our Social Side to its former state. With the co-operation of all we can look forward to some jolly and riotous evenings. * * * * Harry Shields has been re-elected to the Committee of the Southern Counties' Cross-Country Association. Jack Chapple, our Mitcham friend, and our Poly member, Jimmy Wood, were also elected. Ernie Duffett was re-elected to the Committee of the South of the Thames Cross-Country Association, and is now classed as the "Senior" Committeeman—well in the running for a Vice-Presidency. Syd Roberts has been elected Chairman of the Southern Committee of the Road Walking Association, whilst Alf. Harley has been elected Hon. Treasurer of the Road Walking Association. * * * * Dr. Christopher Woodard, recently demobilised from the Navy, is now on the Staff of the Middlesex Hospital, Mortimer Street, W.1. This hospital is taking a particular interest in athletes and offers sunlight treatment, gymnastics, and physical treatment, with a view to building up British athletes. Any Belgrave Harrier who sustains any injury or who has any physical weakness or disability is invited to call at the hospital any evening between 6 and 7 p.m. and ask for Dr. Woodard. In a short talk given to members before the A.G.M., Christopher emphasised the need for prompt and correct treatment for physical injuries, and he hoped that any member needing treatment would come along. He has been a Belgrave Harrier for many years past and has now graciously accepted the post of Hon. Medical Adviser. * * * * Harry Hare's many friends will be glad to hear that he is on the way to recovery. Frank Thomson is better and was a spectator at the finish of the Brighton walk, and was also at the A.G.M. Bill Fish was also at the A.G.M. and was very pleased to be amongst the lads again. Charlie Cook is recuperating and Will Inge has been ill. George Clay has been troubled by an old malady—an after-effect of being gassed in the 1914-18 war. * * * * Once again we must express our gratitude to our starter, George Fell, who has been as sprightly as ever. We are indeed fortunate in having such a competent man with the gun, for the starters' job is an important and exacting one. * * * * Our President was very much amused to receive, when he was Hon. Secretary, a communication addressed to Mr. H. Sam Reve. The address was correct, but the name, of course, is Parker. Incidentally, Harry maintains a large fan mail with Club members, especially those serving or away from home. For those seeking his address, it is: 3 Fritham Close, New Malden, Surrey. * * * * Here is a reminder to all concerned that the Club Rule is that only First Claim members are eligible to compete in Club Championships, and three months' membership immediately prior to the race is essential if a member has previously belonged to another athletic club. Where there is a Club Handicap in conjunction, those not eligible as above can compete in the Handicap only. * * * * Bert Button, writing from Sydney, New South Wales, sends greetings to the Club and all those he knew years ago. * * * * Heartiest Congratulations to Colin Sutton and Jock Martin upon their performances in the 24 Hours' Walk, held at the White City on July 14th-15th. Both covered 100 miles within the 24 hours and so qualified to become members of the famous Centurions' Club. Their times were: Sutton, 20 hours, 40 minutes, 11 seconds; Martin, 22 hours, 16 minutes, 57 seconds, and both have been presented with a suitably inscribed Certificate from the Club. Both these walkers have been prominent members of our teams in long-distance walks and they well deserve their new honour. The winner of the event was our Poly member, Percy Reading, who set up three new records, viz., 19 hours: 105 miles, 466 yards, 110 miles: 19 hours, 57 minutes, 16 seconds, and 20 hours: 110 miles, 410 yards. Percy also beat the unofficial record for a non-stop walk, covering 129 miles, 749 yards. We offer Percy our heartiest congratulations for he is very proud of his membership of the Club. The race was held in appalling weather conditions, the track was rain-soaked and the competitors had to walk several yards wide, which for four hundred laps must be a fair distance. Our veteran walker, already a Centurion, Jimmy Chalk, covered nearly 80 miles before retiring, a remarkable achievement for a man well past 60. It is interesting to note that Jimmy Belchamber gained his Centurion's Badge over 20 years ago when he was second in the London-Brighton and back walk. Our Vice-President, Mr. Ernest H. Neville, is also a well-known figure in the Centurions. * * * * George Clay has been carrying on with the good work at Motspur Park Track. In response to one or two enquiries he has asked us to point out that the training schedules given in the last Belgravian were not his, in fact some of the items were much different to his teaching and practice. * * * * Another renewal of our pre-war activities was the Supporters' Coach for the London to Brighton Walk (details elsewhere). A number of members and friends made the trip and the encouragement they gave to our walkers was much appreciated. Thanks are due to the organiser of the coach, Syd Roberts. From the walkers comes further praise for the splendid services of Charlie Poulter at the baths after the race. The competitors when they arrived after their 52 miles' walk, the last 20 being walked in the pouring rain with a wind which, apart from its slowing effects due to its sheer force, made cold bodies and limbs even colder, were heartened to see the genial and grinning Charlie all ready to bath, rub and bandage them. He used five yards of adhesive tape on blisters alone! Charlie will be at Belgrave Hall, or travelling with our teams (runners and walkers) and his services are at the disposal of any member who wants a rub down or first-aid treatment. * * * * The R.W.A. has just announced a new National Championship at 10 Miles. This will be a Senior Championship, and it is suggested that it should take place four weeks after the "Junior" 10 Miles (i.e., March 29th, 1947). Belgrave will make a strong bid to become the first holders of the title, and our chances of an individual winner are very good indeed. With Harry and Charlie Churcher, Jack Rutland, Joe Coleman, Bob McMullen, and others, we should see a number of Belgrave vests at the front. * * * * WANTED—from a Club Member with a fully-marked copy of the 1937 Track Championships programme—times of all the Junior Championships held on that day. Please forward to the Hon. Secretary. The Hon. Secretary would also be glad to have programmes, fixture cards, cuttings, etc., etc., giving details of Club activities in the pre-1914 era, for inclusion in the Club records. * * * * Tom Carter was unable to do any serious racing this summer owing to the leg injury he sustained in a road relay. He has had an operation on his leg and has started training again and we hope that he will regain the form he showed when he led the field home in last season's Southern Cross-Country Championship. Owing to Tom's inactivity we had no representatives in the 2 Miles Steeplechase Races. This is an event at which cross-country runners shine; have we any potential steeplechasers amongst our new cross-country stars? Tom put some good steeplechase performances before the war, and no doubt would have been prominent this season. * * * * We are very pleased to print the following letter:— "Having joined the Belgrave Harriers in the year 1930, I never for one moment thought I should have the great honour to be made a Life Member at the last A.G.M., for which honour, gentlemen, I really sincerely thank you. I have always enjoyed walking races and training with the Belgrave lads and I will certainly do my best to bring the teams forward in the athletic world, and more so, to endeavour to have the Belgrave Colours in the next Olympic Games. I thank you once again for the honour bestowed upon me, and I wish Belgrave Harriers every success in the coming years." HARRY G. CHURCHER. items.sum: Announcement of the Wednesday evening Winter Coaching School at Belgrave Hall, its coaches and its aim of preparing members for the 1948 Olympic Games.
items.s: WINTER COACHING SCHOOL Announcement of the Wednesday evening Winter Coaching School at Belgrave Hall, its coaches and its aim of preparing members for the 1948 Olympic Games. It was suggested to the Committee, and it has now been decided, to organise a Winter Coaching School at Belgrave Hall, which will be held every Wednesday evening from 7 p.m. to 8.30 p.m., commencing on November 6th. The programme will consist of physical training, the study of the technique and coaching of field and track events. The physical training will be under the expert tuition of Dicky Dumbrill, who was a member of the Army Physical Training Corps, assisted by Frank Simmons. The field events coaching will be under the supervision of Charlie Jones, assisted by Sid Jones, and Bill Sutton, and George Clay and others will give advice and instruction to sprinters and middle-distance runners. In addition it is hoped to be able to arrange for eminent coaches and International athletes to give lectures. One of our members, Dr. C. R. Woodard, has also promised to give talks in connection with injuries usually sustained by athletes and their treatment. The full programme is available and is exhibited on the notice boards at Tooting Bec Track and Belgrave Hall. It has also been circulated to Junior members for whom this coaching is mainly designed. It is hoped that as many as possible will come along to Belgrave Hall on Wednesday evenings so that when the Summer season comes round they will be in a position to start their training on the right lines. Now is the time to look ahead to 1948 when the Olympic Games will be held in London and we hope that this coaching will be able to set some of our members on the right lines so that they may be able to improve their performances sufficiently to be considered as candidates for the British team for the Games. Any further information can be obtained from the Field Events Hon. Sec., T. C. Jones, 6 Broomwood Road, S.W.11. items.s: NEWS OF MEMBERS Short news paragraphs about members at home and abroad, in the Forces and returning to sport. Max Quackenbos is very busy in the U.S.A.. He is working hard in research with plastics, but has found time to resume running after a year's absence from the track. He got down to 4.33 for the mile and 10 minutes flat for 2 miles. With a small band of enthusiasts, he is starting a new club, the Newark (New Jersey) Track Club. He was thrilled to read of our "National" win, and marvels at the fitness of the "old hands." Willie Nankeville has been training with a club in Hamburg, except when he has popped home to show us his heels. Amongst his many brilliant performances this season were winning his Corps championships at 800 and 1,500 metres in 2 minutes 0 seconds, and 4 minutes 9 seconds, respectively. Represented Britain at the International Meeting in Antwerp, and was third in the 800 metres in 1.58.8. Won the 1,500 metres in the Armed Forces Olympic Games, held in Berlin, in 4 minutes 1.2 second (equivalent roughly to a 4.20 mile). Has many many friends amongst Continental athletes, and we hope that he will gain a Full International vest when he returns home. Etienne Gailley, perhaps better known as "Steve," is now commissioned in the Belgian Army, and sends his best wishes to his Belgrave friends. "Steve" joined us in 1943, having escaped from occupied Europe. Johnny Johnson, our Sheffield member, is now demobbed. He has been doing some good publicity for the Club by showing the magazine to his Northern friends. George Chantler is now running again after ten years of inactivity, during which time he has been in and out of hospital. Jack Rathbone, one of our long-distance walking stalwarts of some dozen or so years ago, sends greetings to his old friends and invites any of them to call on him for a cup of tea and a yarn if they are down Herne Bay way, where he now has a place of his own. Harry Thaxter is now an official of Diss Town F.C. and is on the committee of a tennis club. Jack Bidgood gave our Brighton walkers a cheery smile as they passed through his "beat." Charlie Redgrave appeared at the Pavilion, Bognor Regis, in his famous turn, "A Ukelele, a Smile and a Song." Tommy Green hopes to be a frequent attender at walking fixtures and we all look forward to seeing him and Raymond, who is shortly coming out of the Navy. Tommy holds high hopes that Ray will go a long way in the walking world. Charlie Smart will be returning to Germany as a civilian with the Control Commission. Jim Heathfield is now a Lance-Corporal with the B.A.O.R. and is training on the track at Hamburg. Len Coleman has been home from W. Africa and has had a few spins before he goes abroad again, probably to India. John Weames has been called up and is with the R.A.F. Ron Danielson is another who has been called up, also in the R.A.F. Dick Norton is an officer cadet, and has been in hospital with scarlet fever, followed by a bruised heel, sustained on an assault course. Tony Whincup is still in India and is now a Sergeant. His first intimation of our "National" win was derived from a grimy sheet of newspaper which floated around his quarters in the monsoon breeze. An hour or so later another grimy piece of newspaper turned up describing the prowess of Jack Rutland. Hopes to be home this winter. Dennis Giles, one of our newer members, is with the R.A.F. at Weston-super-Mare. Will Lockyer, sent to us by our old friend Cecil Bailey, had a training schedule given to him in Italy by Alf. Harley. Brian Driscoll is now with the R.A.F., training to be a wireless operator. Bob Boyden is still busy at his home near Redhill, but hopes to come along and see us. John Seddon is now de-mobbed and is continuing with his studies. He has been doing a spot of training at Motspur Park. Roy Anderson is still overseas, and is looking forward to his return. Cecil Mains is another who is running again, he is concentrating on the marathon. Percy Wright is studying at the Oakley Training College (men), Cheltenham. Don Brown is home and may soon be returning to London. He hopes to try himself over 20 miles. Bill Snell is now back from overseas and has already been on the road. Alby Bird, with his wife and youngster, were welcome spectators at the Club Championship Meeting. They are living at Bolton. Bob Martin, we regret to learn, has been in hospital with a damaged ankle. We trust that it is not serious and that he will soon be on the road again. Dan Patience is now working in Scotland. Norman Graves, our friend from Wirral, sends greetings. He is now demobbed and spent part of his leave in Switzerland, enjoying some of what are to us now "luxury foods." John Brown, still at Catterick, was in the Services team v. B.A.O.R. in Dusseldorf at the end of September. Ken Cuff sends a news cutting from Palestine. The news writer says of the "Bels.": "It is their boisterous attitude that is mainly responsible for making them the power they are in the sport to-day." * * * * Our congratulations go to Fred Clay, Dick Towndrow, Rene Howell and Ron Hughes, upon becoming fathers. items.sum: Review of the Field Events Section's 1946 season: second in the S.A.A. League, Club Championships, county championships and inter-club trophies, with notes on throwers, jumpers, hurdlers and Juniors.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS REVIEW Review of the Field Events Section's 1946 season: second in the S.A.A. League, Club Championships, county championships and inter-club trophies, with notes on throwers, jumpers, hurdlers and Juniors. We welcome the return of Sid Jones and Bill Sutton from the Forces and genial Jerry Thompson, after suffering from sugar diabetes, has been one of the features of the Section's activities during the past summer. Unfortunately, neither one of them was able to help us in the first of the post-war S.A.A. League contests, but they all made their presence felt as soon as they did get back into competition. As far as can be ascertained (without the official table of results to hand) we finished second in the S.A.A. League. We were rather unfortunate in not being able to turn out our best available men in all events, which made all the difference between first and second places in the League. All who turned out are thanked for their support and next year we hope to be able to go one better and show the other clubs in the South that we are the best-equipped Club in this Section of the sport in team competition. The Junior Section of the S.A.A. League was run for the first time this year and Field Events were included therein in which our Juniors showed up very well. Charlie Melchior again, and Alan Dunn, one of our most promising younger members, were our mainstays in the Javelin, gaining maximum points in a number of matches. They were ably backed up by veteran George Powell, and our Field Events Captain. Until the entry into the competition of Sid Jones, Bill Sutton and Jerry Thompson, Charlie Melchior was our first string in the Shot. Jerry Thompson, after a long lay-off, did not show quite such good form as previously, but managed one or two good performances. Sid Jones soon started showing he had lost none of his old form and towards the end of the season was consistently showing around 38 feet. Bill Sutton was rather slower in showing his form, but was coming along nicely, and with a winter of light training should be pushing Sid Jones and Jerry Thompson next season. In the Discus, Sid Jones and Bill Sutton did not quite reach their pre-war form and George Powell and Charlie Melchior were on their heels always. Alan Dunn was also showing good form in this event, even managing to beat Sid Jones in the Club Championship with a throw of over 104 feet. With Alan's potentialities as a Javelin thrower, he might be well advised to concentrate on that event. Another member who showed up well in the Discus was Ben Lee. He did one good performance of over 100 feet in a Club Handicap, but owing to difficult working hours is unable to find time to train properly, which is a pity, as with his natural size and strength he appears capable of getting amongst the best. The Long Jump was again one of our weaknesses but Charlie Jones started doing performances which if not near championship standard were fair, and in fact he was almost never out of the first three places in match events. One of our pre-war second claim members, Frank Norman, has returned to the Club as a first claim member now, and with steady training next season should be showing some good performances. Until his return we had to rely on Juniors, or members who do not do much jumping, for our second strings in matches. In the High Jump we had to rely on Juniors almost exclusively, with the exception of Bob Wise, who is torn between this event and quarter-miling, thereby, perhaps, not showing his best in either. Guy Hendry, of whom we had great hopes this season has, owing to Service duties, been unable to turn out at all. Dick Negus and Boxall of the Juniors and Leigh have possibilities, but need to do a lot of study of technique to show their best. The Hop, Step and Jump, rather a neglected event heretofore, we have tried to popularise by including the event in matches. We also instituted a Club Championshop at this event and the entries were very satisfactory. Charlie Jones was our best performer but Bert Machell and Geoff. Freestone have possibilities, and Frank Norman has started to train for this event. This must be one of the most interesting events in the Field category and there are great possibilities in the way of International competition if anyone will only concentrate on it. It is interesting to note that we have at least two members who are trying their hand (or should I say feet) at Hurdling events. Young Briggs has shown good form in the Junior events in which he has competed and Jack Frost has taken to running 440 yards hurdles. He might well prove an excellent performer if he will concentrate on improving his style over the obstacles. He should observe Harold Abrahams' remarks about Ede in the October issue of Athletics. As for the Juniors, we have a number of very promising lads. Dennis Fleming, Peter Drew and Arthur Allen in the Shot. Dennis Fleming and Geoff. Freestone in the Discus and Dennis again and Arthur Allen for the Javelin. Dennis might be well advised to concentrate on one or other of these events as he has great possibilities in either of the three with the Javelin as the most probable. In the Jumps the performances here, as with the Seniors, have been weaker than in the throwing events, but Dick Negus and Boxall have done fairly well in the High Jump. In the Long Jump, in Dick Negus again, Davis, Dorian and Geoffrey George we have potentially good performers, but all must do more to perfect their run-up. Unfortunately Alan Fleming, our best Junior here, has joined the R.A.F. and has been unable to turn out at all for us. The first post-war Club Championships were very well supported and from the results to be found on another page, it will be seen that not one of the 1939 winners retained his title. Standard medal winners were quite numerous, especially in the Hop, Step and Jump, and no doubt the Committee will have to consider raising some of the standards. In the various County Championships which were held once again, our members showed up well. Charlie Melchior, having changed his County qualification (after a number of years in Surrey) to Hertfordshire, won their Javelin Championship with a throw of 163 feet, 10 inches. The Surrey Championships saw Ron Jeal gain second place in the Javelin with Charlie Jones third. Our Field Events Captain also gained second place in the Hop, Step and Jump with an effort of 39 feet, 8¾ inches. In the Surrey Junior events we put up a good show. Dennis Fleming was unexpectedly beaten into second place in the Javelin but made amends in the Discus by winning with a good throw of nearly 100 feet. His best performance so far. His brother Alan got second place in the Long Jump with an effort of 19 feet, 6 inches. In the Middlesex Championships Frank Cutts-Watson was third in the Javelin, but Alan Dunn had an off-day when we were expecting a good performance from him. In the major Inter-Club Competitions we showed up reasonably well. In the Kinnaird Trophy Charlie Melchior and Alan Dunn gained points in the Javelin. In the Waddilove Trophy at Birmingham we were unfortunately not too well represented owing to travel difficulties, but Charlie Jones managed second place in the Javelin and third in the Long Jump with 20 feet, 5½ inches. Charlie Jones won the Long Jump and Bob Wise was second in the High Jump in the Reynolds Garrett Trophy meeting, at Southampton. Club Handicaps have again been well supported and it is hoped to put on even more events next year. Keep it up, lads, and don't forget the Winter Coaching School, particulars of which will be found on another page. It is only by the study of technique and still more technique which will enable us to supply candidates for the 1948 Olympic Team. e: England Youths' race (National Cross Country Championships)
items.s: WITH THE RUNNERS Review of the runners' 1946 track season and preview of the 1946-47 cross-country season: captains, fixtures, championship venues and the Boxing Day track meeting. On looking back over the past Track season, I think we have every reason to be well satisfied with the progress of the Club and its members during the summer months. We won most of the Inter-Club matches, although the winning or losing is not so important, in my view, as the important point of giving our members an opportunity of testing themselves against other clubs and of encouraging the team spirit, without which any club cannot expect to make headway. Our Juniors were a good example in this direction, and we have got together a very fine lot of youngsters who should stand the Club in good stead in the years that lie ahead. Derrick Burfitt, was, of course, outstanding in his performances, and we look forward to a continuation of his successes, both on track and country. Len Herbert was our most outstanding distance runner, and it was a great pity that Tom Carter, owing to a leg injury, was unable to give of his best. Among the middle-distance men, Len Marchant and Willie Nankeville were very much to the fore, and with John Brown and Vic Blowfield showing great promise, we can look forward with confidence to next season. Among the sprinters, Teddy Read improved by leaps and bounds as the season progressed, and was given good support by Dicky Dumbrill and Jack Frost. Stan Botwright, back in civvy street, took things fairly quietly and near the end of the season Michael Broadbent made a re-appearance on the track. Alan Sexton and Dick Negus give promise of better performances to come, while Arthur Bruce was outstanding over the middle-distance races in our Junior matches. Space does not permit of my mentioning all the many very promising members, but Junior and Senior, that we have in our ranks, but I am confident that next season will see our members more outstanding than ever. So to the cross-country season, and if the gathering at Belgrave Hall for our opening race can be taken as a guide, I think we are in for a bumper season. We cannot win more races than last season, and it must be borne in mind that for several of the events complete new teams will have to be found, as the winning team each year is barred from competing again. However, with a turn-out of 55 members for the 3 miles road race handicap, I think these can be found, and it is especially pleasing to see so many old faces once again appearing at Belgrave Hall. We are holding the usual Club Championship and Handicap events, also a 3 Miles' Novices Race on November 2nd, and in addition to the various Inter-Club matches, we have arranged several matches for the Juniors, under 19 years of age. Bert Footer is our cross-country captain, and as a runner who has thrice represented England in the International Cross-Country Championship, I am sure our members, both new and old, will reap much benefit from his learned advice and experience. With Alf Taylor and Frank Webb as vice-captains, we again have two men of much experience, and the latter is giving a special eye to our Junior Section. Eddie Short is our new Junior captain, and in his first season over the country, Eddie put up a magnificent show in the England Youths' race, and is certain to give the Junior Section a good lead in this direction. Coming to our fixture list, we have again arranged runs with very old friends such as Thames Valley Harriers, Metropolitan Police, Finchley Harriers, Surrey A.C. and Mitcham A.C. Towards the end of the season we have arranged runs with the Cambridge Harriers and London University Tyrian Club. This will give those members, not in our championship teams, an incentive to keep training, and not slack off as is likely towards the end of rhe season. We again have the usual Road Relay races, and we also understand that Ilford A.C. are hoping to stage their annual race, so our road runners look to be in for a busy time. For the championship events, the Surrey County are going to Earlswood, and the South of Thames is being held in Windsor Great Park. The Southern Counties will be on Ascot Racecourse, while the English Championships will be held at Apsley, Herts. For the benefit of those who think they stand a chance, the International race is being held in Paris, so they had better "brush-up" their French! We are again holding our Annual Track Meeting at Tooting Common on Boxing Day morning, and I trust that members who intend competing will let us have their names in good time for handicapping purposes. Thus it will be seen that there is plenty of work ahead for all members and it behoves everyone to give the Club captain their best support by turning up on Saturday afternoons whether at home or away, and also by coming along and training in mid-week, so that he can sort out the various "packs" that will assist us in retaining our proud title of the premier English cross-country club. items.sum: Round-up of members' 1946 successes at open meetings, road races, the British Games, Services, London, county, Inter-Counties, Southern and A.A.A. championships, the Mitcham meeting and the Surrey medley relay.
items.s: ROUND THE MEETINGS Round-up of members' 1946 successes at open meetings, road races, the British Games, Services, London, county, Inter-Counties, Southern and A.A.A. championships, the Mitcham meeting and the Surrey medley relay. Club members have competed with success at the various "open" meetings held during the season, and among those who have been successful are E. G. Read, L. M. Marchant, A. A. Hawkins, H. A. Bishop, A. H. Bruce, L. C. Bishop, W. E. Lucas, S. R. Eales, V. S. Blowfield, while Frank Webb has been picking up "pots" in open veterans' sprints. The Club teams have also done well in winning several 2 mile team races, also open medley relays, while Tom Clinton, Bert Mitchell and (whisper it) Bert Footer have done well in open road races. Dan Patience finished third in the Kent County 20 miles road race, and Syd Ring was third in the Surrey 20, while the Club team were second in the team contest. At the British Games meeting held at the White City, Derrick Burfitt won the 880 yards Youths' Race, while Basil Walden was third in the final of the 100 yards Youths' Scratch Race. Also on the programme was a "Services" 1 Mile, which owing to the large entry, was run in two sections. In the first race J. W. Brown finished third, while in the second race Willie Nankeville was placed second. Len Herbert ran fourth in the 3 Miles, which was won by Gaston Reiff, of Belgium. Willie Nankeville was also selected to represent the A.A.A. in their match at Antwerp, and finished third in the 800 metres event, his time being 1 minute, 58.5 seconds. At the Armed Forces "Olympic" meeting, which was held in Berlin, Nankeville was the only British athlete to record a win, and his time of 4 minutes 1.5 seconds for the 1,500 metres, beat the record for the meeting. Willie will make them all go when he is demobbed and with Derrick Burfitt to keep him company, our chances of having a couple of representatives in the 1948 Olympic Games look very bright. Derrick was also picked to run for the A.A.A. at the Royal Ulster Constabulary meeting at Belfast, and as this was his first senior contest, he can be said to have done well in finishing second in the 1 Mile Race. Others to represent the A.A.A. during the season have been Len Marchant and Len Herbert. Derrick Burfitt was also selected to represent the A.T.C. against a picked French junior team in a match at the White City, and he won the 1 Mile Race in 4 minutes 25.8 seconds. Burfitt also won the Southern Junior Mile Championship, repeating his success of last year, and then went on to win the A.A.A. Junior Mile title in the record-breaking time of 4 minutes 23.2 seconds. For a lad of 19, Derrick is certainly in the world-beating class and well merits the award of the Club Honours Badge, which was bestowed upon him recently. Our Service members have also been well to the fore in their own championships, and in the R.A.F. meet, L.A.C. Scantlebury was third in the 100 Yards to McDonald Bailey. Len Marchant came second in the 880 Yards, and both these runners represented the R.A.F. in the Inter-Service Championships, where Len Marchant finished third in the 1 Mile, and was also in the winning 4 x 880 team. John Brown was second in the Army 1 Mile Championship, and also represented them in the Inter-Services meeting. The L.C.C. promoted what they termed the London Championships and several of our members gained places in the area meetings, which qualified them to appear at the finals held at the Parliament Hill track. Ted Read won the 100 Yards, while Charlie Smart won the 3 Miles, and proved how sadly we missed him during the season while he was overseas with the B.A.O.R. At the Surrey County Championships our members did well, and Len Marchant was third in the 880, while Len Herbert annexed the 3 Mile title. Jimmy Wood, a second-claim member, won the 1 Mile, and in the Senior Javelin, Ron Jeal was second and Charlie Jones third. Charlie was also second in the Hop. Step and Jump, and seems to improve with age. Our junior members also gained several award, with Dennis Fleming winning the Discus, and being second in the Javelin. His brother, Alan, was also second in the Long Jump, and G. Osmint ran well to finish third in the 220 Yards. Arthur Bruce won the 1 Mile in 4 minutes 46.8 seconds, and so proved he is the best junior miler in the county. Len Herbert won the 3 Miles race at the Inter-Counties meeting held at Hove, while Len Marchant was in the winning Surrey team in the medley relay. At the Southern Counties' Championships held at the White City, Len Herbert finished second in the 3 Miles event, and his battle with Maurice Bingham was worth seeing. Bingham led throughout but Len gradually overhauled his man and they went down the straight neck and neck. Bingham eventually triumphed by a few yards, but as Len's time was 14 minutes 36.2 seconds, it will be seen that he was very unlucky to do such a time and then not win. Fred Clay qualified for the final of the 440, but was evidently short of training, and it is a pity that Fred now lives at Leicester. In the A.A.A. Championships, Len Herbert and Bill Lucas both ran in the 3 Mile event, in which Sydney Wooderson put up such a wonderful performance, and Herbert qualified for a standard award. We had several entrants in the Marathon race and Bert Mitchell was the first Club man home in the thirteenth position, and his time of 2 hours 59 minutes 43 seconds also gained him A.A.A. standard. At the Mitcham meeting our members carried off the majority of the awards, with Ben Lulham winning the 880 "open," and Syd Jarlett gaining third place in the Mile. Len Herbert was the individual winner of the 2 Miles, his time being 9 minutes 28 seconds, and our team of Herbert, Bill Lucas and Ted Stimpson won the Team Race from Poly. In the Youths' Medley Relay, our team of Bruce, Briggs, Lewis and Sexton, ran away from the opposition and put up a really fine show for juniors. The seniors did likewise in the Surrey County Medley Relay Championships, although they had a great fight with Dorking St. Pauls. Len Marchant was behind Parlett of Dorking over the half-mile stage, but Jack Frost pulled up a little, and then Dicky Dumbrill almost caught his man over the first 220. Ted Read took the final leg and swept past his man in great style to record a win for the Club. Our time was 3 minutes 36.8 seconds, which must be very near a County record for this race. E. G. items.s: SOUTHERN AMATEUR ATHLETIC LEAGUE Report and final tables of the revived Southern Amateur Athletic League South-West Division in 1946: Belgrave headed the Senior table and the Juniors were second to Herne Hill. It was decided to revive this pre-war competition again this season, and instead of the system of divisions with promotion and relegation it was decided to have four area divisions for this season. We were placed in the South-West Division along with Herne Hill H., Dorking St. Pauls A.C., Surrey A.C., Mitcham A.C., Epsom and Ewell H., and Sutton and Cheam H. It was also decided to run a Junior League, for those under 19 on May 1st, and there were six events for the Seniors and three for the Juniors. In the 4 x 440 Yards Relay, we finished second to Dorking St. Pauls, and Jack Frost ran a fine third leg to make up lost ground. On the same evening the 3 Miles Team Race was decided, but owing to unforeseen circumstances, we only had three distance men available, but A. H. Sampson sportingly offered to turn out to complete our team, as in this competition it is 4 men to run and score. Tommy Rowe of Herne Hill was the individual winner, with Bill Lucas in second place, and Herne Hill also beat us in the Team Race. The 4 x 220 yards saw a similar result, although Jack Frost had a slight lead at the last take-over, but could not hold T. L. Higgins, the brilliant young Herne Hill runner. In the 1 Mile Team Race, Bill Lucas again ran well in finishing second to Tommy Rowe, with Ken Roberts of Mitcham third, but our lads packed better this time and we won the team race by 5 points. The 4 x 880 yards saw Mitcham turn out a good four, and they won from Dorking St. Paul's with ourselves third. In the final event of the competition, the 1 Mile Medley Relay, Parlett of Dorking gave his team a winning lead, but by finishing third, we managed to score sufficient points to retain our position at the head of the league table. The Juniors did quite well in finishing second in the table to Herne Hill, although not doing so well in the 4 x 110 yards Relay, they excelled themselves in the 1 Mile Team Race, and led by A. H. Bruce, 1st, E. A. Short, 4th, Len Bishop, 8th, and with Eric Bishop, 12th, they won this event by 1 point. In the 1 Mile Medley Relay, it was unfortunate that after Derrick Burfitt, running a 2 min. 1 sec. half mile, had given us a good lead that we had to run Len Bishop over the final 440 yards stage. Len, we hasten to say, had only turned out in order to make up the number, his usual distance being a mile or over, and the Herne Hill runner overhauled him near the tape to win a good race. Although these events were all held in the early part of the season the support given them was not up to expectations, and it remains to be seen on what lines the League will be held next season. e: Match v. Cambridge Harriers and Metropolitan Police
items.s: MATCH v. CAMBRIDGE HARRIERS and METROPOLITAN POLICE A.C. Report and results of the triangular track match at Charlton Park on 11 May 1946, won by Belgrave Harriers with 68 points from Metropolitan Police 60 and Cambridge Harriers 48. This was held at Charlton Park Track on Saturday, May 11th, and the 100 Yards was won by H. C. Wickerson, the well-known sprinter, who was running for Cambridge. Jack Frost, our track Vice-Captain, was second, and Dicky Dumbrill fourth. The 220 Yards saw Jack Frost an easy winner and A. A. Hawkins, a product of George Clay's school, was a good third. Syd Jarlett, although looking a bit thin on top, won the 440 Yards, and Rene Howell, our Poly member, sportingly turned out and gained a point by finishing fifth. Len Marchant, on leave from the R.A.F., won the 880 Yards in fine style, and a new member in D. W. Cattrall also ran well. The 1 Mile saw Pettet and Moody of the Police in front, followed by Bill Lucas, now demobbed from the R.A.F., and Tom Morrell and Stan Eales filled the next two places. The 1 Mile Medley Relay saw Syd Jarlett running the half-mile stage and although he kept with his opponents, our two sprinters lost ground, and Len Marchant was left a hopeless task over the final leg. A 2 Miles Walk was included in the match and it was pleasing to see this well supported by our members. Harry Churcher, the A.A.A. 2 and 7 miles champion, led throughout, although young McMullen kept close behind, and was a good second. Len Fletcher, an ex Inter-Counties champion, now making a welcome come-back, walked well to gain third place, and others in our team were, Scamell, Snr., Percy Wright and Don Heath. The field events saw the Police gaining most points, but Sid Jones, now out of the Army, showed some of his old form in the Shot Putt, and young Dick Negus won the High Jump. Charlie Melchior was second in the Javelin Throw, and our field event Captain, Charlie Jones, was second in the Long Jump. items.s: FIRST TRACK MEETING Report of Belgrave's opening track meeting at Tooting Bec on 18 May 1946, where the club won both the Senior match (68 points) and the Junior contest (36½ points). On Saturday, May 18th, at Tooting Bec Track, we held a most successful meeting to open our Summer programme. In the Senior match we met the Polytechnic Harriers, Thames Valley, Dorking St. Paul's and Cambridge, while in the Junior contest we had Cambridge and the Sutton and Cheam lads as our opponents. McDonald Bailey, the West Indian runner, won the 100 Yards for the Poly, and Jack Frost ran well to gain third place for us. Dicky Dumbrill also ran third in the second race over this distance. Jack Frost was second in the first 220 Yards, while Ted Read won the second-string race. Len Marchant found young Anzola, the T.V.H. lad, a little too speedy down the straight in the 880, but Len Herbert won the 1 Mile with D. W. Cattrall, a newcomer to the Club, in third place. H. W. Pascoe, who is second-claim to us, won the 2 Miles race from a good field, which included Doug. Wilson of the Poly. Pascoe did 9 minutes 35.8 secs, which was good running for so early in the season. We did not have any individual winners in the field events but our lads picked up some useful points in the minor placings. Final scores in the Senior match were: Belgrave H. 68, Polytechnic H. 63, Thames Valley H. 45, Cambridge H. 30, Dorking St. Paul's A.C. 25. In the Junior match the Cambridge boys won both sprint races with Dick Negus and G. J. Barker doing best for us. Two of our lads, A. J. Betterton and P. J. Briggs, were first and second in the 440, and A. H. Bruce gained second place in the 880 Yards. Derrick Burfitt turned out for the Club in the 1 Mile team race and won easily. With Eddie Short second and Len Bishop third, we won the team race with the lowest possible score. Dick Negus also won both High and Long Jumps and this young man will be most useful so long as he decides not to attempt too much at the one meeting. Scores in the Junior contest were: Belgrave H. 36½, Cambridge H. 23, Sutton and Cheam 10½. e: Junior match v. Whitgift Middle School
items.s: JUNIOR MATCH AT CROYDON Report and results of the annual Junior match against Whitgift Middle School on the School ground, won by Belgrave 26 points to 25. This match with the Whitgift Middle School, which is now an annual affair, was held on the School ground, and once again we had a most close and exciting match. Dick Negus made a good start by winning the 100 Yards, although Sexton of the School was only beaten by inches. The latter showed good form in winning the 220 Yards, and has now joined the Club, a must useful addition to our ranks. Betterton won the 440, and D. F. Platt ran a plucky race to win the 880 Yards. He was almost on his knees coming up the straight, but held on to win. Arthur Bruce had his usual opponents of Short and Bishop in the 1 Mile, although this time Eddie Short was running for his School. Once again Bruce proved too good for his rivals and this young man is going to be a far better runner than his father, who was a more than useful miler in Club colours. Dick Negus again won both jumps and in the 4 x 110 Relay, a good race was seen, with the School showing the better handling of the baton, an important point in such races, and they deservedly won. Final points were: Belgrave H. 26, Whitgift Middle School 25, a result we have previously had in this match, and then the competitors and officials were entertained to "tea and buns," which was much appreciated by our lads, and we look forward to next season's visit to this ground. items.s: MATCH v. SUTTON AND CHEAM Report of the four-club match at the Borough Sports Ground, Sutton, on 1 June 1946, won by Belgrave Harriers with 72 points. On Saturday, June 1st, we journeyed to Sutton to meet the local club at the Borough Sports Ground. This is the ground used by the Sutton United F.C., and the cinder track surrounds the football pitch. Although not in the best of condition, it is a pleasantly-situated ground, and all the members present enjoyed the meeting. The other competing clubs were Dorking St. Paul's A.C., and Mitcham A.C., and although it was originally arranged for both Senior and Junior matches to be held, owing to the number of competitors being limited, it was decided to merge the two contests. Dick Negus ran well in the Junior 100, while Dicky Dumbrill took second place in the Senior event, and also won the 220 Yards race. D. Cook did well to gain second place in the Junior 220, and Alf Orton showed something like his old form in winning the 880 Yards event. Bob Wise ran well in the Senior 440 Yards, and Len Bishop took third place in the 1 Mile with Micky Walker, having a change from marathon running, close behind him. In the field events, our representatives had very little opposition, and with Charlie Melchior and Syd Jones, we gained maximum points in the Weight and Javelin events. Final match scores were: Belgrave Harriers 72, Dorking St. Paul's 58, Mitcham A.C. 30, Sutton and Cheam 12. items.s: MATCH AT MITCHAM Short report of a match against Herne Hill and Mitcham at the Acc. and Tab. ground on 13 June 1946, where Belgrave shared second place with Mitcham. On Thursday, June 13th, we sent a small team along to the Acc. and Tab. ground, to meet Herne Hill and Mitcham in a meeting put on to encourage running among the employees of this firm. With a mixture of Seniors and Juniors we eventually shared the points with Mitcham, with Herne Hill winners, and we trust the events and the running was of interest to those concerned. What did interest our lads was the fine tea provided afterwards by the promoters, and I can say that all our lads did justice to the fine spread so generously given them. items.s: JUNE HANDICAP MEETING Report and results of the club handicap meeting at Tooting Bec on 5 June 1946, with the sprints, 880 yards, mile, walk, shot and javelin handicaps and the Schools' Invitation Relay. Held at Tooting Bec on June 5th, we had a full list of handicaps for Club members, and it was also decided to hold a School's relay race. We had five heats in the 100 Yards, and heat winners were R. C. Negus, T. C. Jones, P. W. Drew, S. Jarlett, E. R. Jessop. Drew made good use of his mark of 11 yards to win the final, with Syd Jarlett second and Charlie Jones third. V. S. Blowfield, a new member, showed good form in winning the 880 Yards, and D. F. Platt put in a good finish to gain second place, with Alf Orton third. The 2 Miles Walk Handicap was won by P. Wilson with W. G. True second and Len Fletcher, making a welcome come-back, gaining third place. With three heats in the 220 Yards, the following qualified for the final, G. Freestone, A. A. Hawkins, R. G. Dumbrill, A. H. Machell, R. C. Negus, M. A. Parker. Young Geoff. Freestone ran well to beat Dicky Dumbrill for premier honours with Hawkins in third place. The 1 Mile Handicap was won by D. W. Cattrall, a Liverpool Pembroke harrier, who is stationed down this way while in the Services. Rene Howell, also a second-claim member, was second, and young Arthur Bruce gained third place. We held two races for the Schools' Invitation Relay, and the Junior event was won by Wallington County with Whitgift Middle second and Wimbledon College third. Wallington County also won the Senior race with Tiffins' second and Sutton Grammar School third. Thanks are due to Bert Jannaway, who was responsible for the very good entry that we received for these races, and we hope to put them on again next season. e: Junior Match v. Latymer Upper School
items.s: JUNIOR MATCH v. LATYMER UPPER SCHOOL Report of a junior match against Latymer Upper School at Wood Lane on 15 June 1946, lost 59 to 18. Held on the School ground in Wood Lane on Saturday, June 15th, and although we were not at full strength the Latymer boys were far too strong for our lads. G. J. Barker finished third for us in the 100 Yards, and D. F. Platt occupied the same position in the 880 Yards event. In fact third position was the best we could manage in most of the events, but G. Osmint scored a good win for the Club in the 220 Yards. Len Bishop was third in the Mile and we sadly missed Bruce and Short, who were competing elsewhere. Dick Negus and Alan Sexton were also running at another meeting, and it seems that we shall have to make certain of having our strongest team out when next we meet this school. Final scores were : Latymer Upper School 59, Belgrave H. 18. G. J. Barker G. J. Barker third 100 yards D. F. Platt D. F. Platt third 880 yards G. Osmint G. e: Junior Match v. Whitgift Middle School
items.s: JUNIOR MATCH v. WHITGIFT MIDDLE SCHOOL Report and results of the return junior match against Whitgift Middle School at Tooting on 19 June 1946, lost 27 to 24 on the relay. In this return match, held at Tooting, on June 19th, the Whitgift lads gained their revenge for their defeat earlier in the season. It was a very closely contested match and the result was decided on the result of the Relay race. Alan Sexton, now running for his school, beat Dick Negus in the 100, and also won the 220 Yards. Geoff. Freestone won the 440 Yards, and D. F. Platt repeated his win in the 880 Yards race. Arthur Bruce once again beat Eddie Short in the 1 Mile and although Dick Negus won both Jumps, the score, with the Relay to be decided, was 24 all. The Whitgift quartet were too good for our lads in the final event and so won the match by 27 to 24. Results 100 Yards : 1 Sexton (W.M.S.), 2 Negus (Bel.), 3 Drew (Bel.). items.s: MATCH AT SOUTHAMPTON Report of the inter-club match for the Reynolds-Garrett Trophy at Southampton on 8 June 1946, won by Belgrave with 75 points at their first attempt. On June 8th we journeyed to Southampton to take part in an Inter-Club match held on the fine sports ground provided and maintained by the local council. It was a great pity that the weather prevented the expected large crowd from attending, and the track was under water in places, and the athletes are to be complimented on carrying through with the meeting under such conditions. We met the local club who combined with Eastleigh A.C., and the Portsmouth A.C., in a match for the "Reynolds-Garrett" Trophy, which we won at our first time of competing in this contest. Jack Frost ran second in the 100 Yards, and also finished third in the 220, which was won by Teddy Read. Syd Jarlett and Bob Wise finished second and third in the 440, and Len Marchant won the 880 Yards, with Alf Orton fourth. D. W. Cattrall gained us second place in the 1 Mile, and although we had 3, 4, 5, with Tom Clinton, A. E. Frost and Dick Tobin, in the 2 Miles race, we lost the team race by 1 point. This event was won by J. H. Peters, the Essex Beagles runner, who was representing the combined clubs on this occasion. Bob Wise was second in the High Jump and Charlie Jones won the Long Jump, and we won the Medley Relay with Len Marchant, Jack Frost, Ted Read and Syd Jarlett. Final match points were : Belgrave H. 75, Southampton and Eastleigh 66, Portsmouth A.C. 45. items.s: KINNAIRD TROPHY MEETING Report of the Kinnaird Trophy meeting at the Polytechnic Stadium, Chiswick, on 15 June 1946, highlighted by Len Herberts' mile win. Held at the Polytechnic Stadium, Chiswick, on June 15th, and although we fielded a team it was not as strong as we had hoped for. The high-light of the meeting, from our point of view, was Len Herberts' win in the 1 Mile event. He beat Rene Howell of the Poly, who is a second-claim member of the "Bels.", in the good time of 4 mins. 28.4 secs. Also included in the programme was a Mile Medley Relay for Juniors, and our team had Briggs doing the first leg of 440, followed by Negus and Sexton, who did their best to make up the leeway but young Arthur Bruce on the final half-mile, although making up a lot of ground to reach third place, found the effort too much and finally finished fourth. Len Herbert Len Herberts' won 1 Mile, 4 mins. 28.4 secs. items.s: MATCH AT DORKING Short report of a late-season match at Dorking, where a weak Belgrave team was third behind Dorking St. Paul's and Worthing. This match was arranged rather late in the season and we were poorly represented. Jack Frost won the 100 Yards, although the judges thought differently, and he also captured the 220. Bob Wise finished second in the 440, and V. Barrow was fourth in the 880 Yards. Len Herbert found Parlett's finishing powers too good for him in the 1 Mile, and the times on a sodden track were all on the slow side. items.s: MATCH v. POLICE AND SOUTHGATE Report of the match against Southgate Harriers and the Metropolitan Police A.C. at Tooting on 3 July 1946, won by Belgrave with 48 points, with two Club Junior Handicaps on the same programme. Held at Tooting on July 3rd, we welcomed old friends in Southgate Harriers and the Metropolitan Police A.C. Jack Frost beat Reynolds of the Police in the 100 Yards with Stan Botwright third. The latter, however, won the 220 with Ted Read in second place. Morris, the Police champion, won the 880 Yards and Alf Orton ran well to credit us with third place. Rene Howell gained us first place in the 1 Mile and V. S. Blowfield displayed good form in finishing a close fourth. E. J. Nankivell, the Southgate runner, won the 2 Miles race, and Tom Clinton was second with Ted Stimpson third. The 440 Yards saw an unfortunate clash between the Police and Southgate runners, both of whom fell, thus leaving our two men to finish alone. In the circumstances it was decided to declare the race void. Charlie Melchior won the Javelin Throw and also gained third place in the Weight Putt. Charlie Jones won the Long Jump and is showing a big improvement in his jumping. Final match scores were : Belgrave H. 48, Metropolitan Police 38, Southgate H. 24. Included on the same programme were two Club Junior Handicaps, and with two heats in the 220 Yards the following qualified for the final : Sexton, A. Fleming, Freestone, Negus, Davis, and E. M. Bishop. Dick Negus won the final, beating Alan Sexton with A. D. Davis third. In the Club Junior 880 Yards Handicap, A. H. Bruce was on the virtual scratch mark and he ran through his field in excellent style to win. Eric Bishop was second with C. N. Collis third. items.s: MATCH AT CHISWICK Report of the evening match at the Polytechnic Stadium, Chiswick, on 10 July 1946 against the Polytechnic and London A.C., won by Belgrave with 74 points. On Wednesday evening, July 10th, we visited the Polytechnic Stadium at Chiswick for a match with the home club and the London A.C. Ted Read gave us an encouraging start by winning the 100 Yards in 10.4 secs, but could only manage third place in the 220, which was won by B. W. Metcalfe of the Poly, who assisted us in Club matches during the War period when the Poly were not functioning. Bob Wise ran his best to date in finishing second to J. G. Hartley of L.A.C. in the 440 Yards race, and Alf Orton did well to gain third place in the 880 event. Rene Howell won the 1 Mile for the Poly but only after a great race with V. S. Blowfield, who improves with each outing and should be troubling the best before the season is out. Charlie Smart showed a welcome return to pre-war form in winning the 2 Miles in the good time of 9 min. 52.2 secs., and Dick Towndrow, running for the Poly, was second, and Tom Clinton finished a good fourth. Len Herbert had sportingly offered to run in the relay owing to our shortage of recognised half-milers, and although going off about 40 yards down over the final leg, Len ran a magnificent race to catch his Poly rival and so score a win for the Club. Charlie Jones was second in the Long Jump and our "heavy" brigade of Syd Jones and Bill Sutton gained useful points in the Weight Putt. Alan Dunn beat Charlie Melchior in the Javelin Throw in finishing second to Dalyrymple of L.A.C. Final match scores were : Belgrave H. 74, London A.C. 69, Polytechnic H. 65, and we can be well satisfied with our lads' performances against such strong opposition. items.s: INTER-CLUB MEETING AT BANSTEAD Report of an inter-club meeting at the Banstead Hospital sports ground, held in rain, where Len Herbert won the 2 Miles but Belgrave lost the team race to Surrey A.C. by 4 points. We were invited to take part in an Inter-Club contest at the Banstead Hospital sports ground, and our old friend Alec Robertshaw had been responsible for marking out the ground, etc. It was a great pity that the weather kept away the large crowd that had been expected, but the meeting was carried through despite the rain. A. W. Bedford, a new member, ran well in the 880 Yards race to finish second, and he also gained third place in the 1 Mile, in which Frank Close, the International runner, made a re-appearance to gain second place. Peter George turned out for us in the 440, and A. G. Lewis also competed in the 1 Mile Junior Novice race, but neither gained a place. The 2 Miles Run was the big event of the afternoon and Len Herbert travelled over from the Motspur Park meeting in order to compete. Len beat Stan Belton, of Surrey, to win the individual race but we lost the team result by 4 points to Surrey A.C. Among the competitors was none other than our old cross-country captain, Bert Footer, and it certainly is a pleasure to see Bert turning out once again. After the meeting the competitors were provided with tea, and for those who liked to stay, a dance was held in the spacious dance hall inside the hospital. Those of our lads who were present thoroughly enjoyed themselves and we look forward to next season's meeting on the same ground. items.sum: Report and results of the junior match with Herne Hill Harriers and Polytechnic Juniors at Tooting on 17 July 1946; Belgrave first won 32 to 29½ to 28½, but after a query over Alan Dunn's eligibility the result was amended to Herne Hill 31, Polytechnic 30, Belgrave 29.
e: Junior Match v. Herne Hill Harriers
items.s: JUNIOR MATCH v. HERNE HILL HARRIERS Report and results of the junior match with Herne Hill Harriers and Polytechnic Juniors at Tooting on 17 July 1946; Belgrave first won 32 to 29½ to 28½, but after a query over Alan Dunn's eligibility the result was amended to Herne Hill 31, Polytechnic 30, Belgrave 29. Held at Tooting on July 17th, this proved a very closely fought match between the home club, the Polytechnic Juniors, and our lads. Dick Negus ran well to gain third place in the 100, while G. Osmint also did well in finishing second in the 220 Yards. A. J. Betterton found Higgins too good for him in the 440 Yards, but gave the winner a good race. Eric Bishop gained third place in the 880, and then in the 1 Mile we called upon Derrick Burfitt to assist us, and he simply walked away from his field, and Derrick certainly makes running look a very easy business. What the other competitors thought is another matter, and Eddie Short had a good tussle with a Herne Hill boy for second place. Dick Negus could only manage a couple of second places in the Jumps but was up against stronger opposition this time. A. C. Allen also gained a couple of third places in the Javelin and Weight, and then in the final event we had first two placings in the Discus, with Alan Dunn and Dennis Fleming. This made the final scores : Belgrave H. 32, Herne Hill H. 29½, Polytechnic H. 28½. However, we had some correspondence with the home club over the question of whether Alan Dunn was eligible to compete in Junior matches, and at their request the result was amended to read : Herne Hill H. 31, Polytechnic H. 30, Belgrave H. 29. No matter what the result, and we must confess that results do not worry us, so long as our boys get some good keen and sporting competition, then we are all satisfied, whether we win or lose. items.s: MATCH AT ALPERTON Report of the evening match at the Alperton Lane Track on 23 July 1946 against Thames Valley Harriers and the Metropolitan Police, lost to Thames Valley by one point. On Tuesday, July 23rd, we visited the Alperton Lane Track for a match with the local club, Thames Valley Harriers, and the Metropolitan Police were also present. Jack Wigley won the 100 Yards for the home club, with Dicky Dumbrill in second place, a position he also occupied in the 220. Morris won the 880 for the Police and V. S. Blowfield beat K. M. Anzola in finishing in third place. Stan Botwright won the 440 and beat both Pettet and Moody, who were running for the Police in this event. Derrick Burfitt, on his home track, turned out for us in the 1 Mile and won easily in 4 min. 32.3 secs. V. Barrow, a comparative newcomer to our ranks, ran well to finish in third place. In the 2 Miles Team race we were beaten by 1 point by the home club, they scoring 1, 4, 5, to our 2, 3, 6. Tom Clinton, Ted Stimpson and Dick Tobin were our scoring team. In the 1 Mile Medley Relay, Blowfield ran a really good race behind Pettet of the Police but they could not catch the T.V.H. boy over the final half-mile stage. F. E. Norman won the Long Jump with Charlie Jones third, and we secured major placings in the Weight Putt. When the final points were totalled up, it was found that Thames Valley had beaten us by the narrow margin of 1 point, which was a good ending to an enjoyable evening's sport. items.s: MATCH AT IMBER COURT Report of the match against the Metropolitan Police at Imber Court on 17 August 1946, won by Belgrave 75 to 46. We visited the Metropolitan Police ground at Imber Court on Saturday, August 17th, but found our hosts very poorly represented. Our lads had turned up in good strength, and with Read and Dumbrill, we had first two home in both sprint races. Len Marchant ran a grand race to beat the Police champion, D. G. Morris, in the 880 Yards, in the fast time of 2 mins. 0.7 secs. Jack Frost also beat Morris in the 440, with Bob Wise in third place. Blowfield and Jimmy Wood had no real opposition in the Mile while Bill Lucas and Charlie Smart also ran home together in the 2 Miles event. Syd Jones and Bill Sutton were first and second in the Weight, and Syd and Alan Dunn also gained major points in the Discus. Dick Negus was off form in the jumping events and is maybe feeling the effects of a very full season. Final match points were : Belgrave H. 75, Metropolitan Police 46. items.s: CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP MEETING Report and results of Belgrave's first post-war Club Championship meeting at Tooting Bec in August 1946, with club records for Len Marchant (880 yards, 1 min. 59 secs.) and Len Herbert (mile, 4 mins. 25.6 secs.), and standards achieved. Held on August Saturday at Tooting Bec Track, before a large crowd, and the number of entries must have been very near a Club record, and speaks well for the present strength of the Club. In the 100 Yards Boys' Championship, A. D. Davis beat a fellow school-mate in D. M. Willis for first place. J. A. Longhurst, quite a tot in comparison, is to be congratulated on his pluck in tackling opponents several years his senior. The 100 Yards Club Championship was won by Ted Read, who beat Dicky Dumbrill with Jack Frost third, and the holder, Stan Botwright, beaten into fourth place. We had two heats in the 100 Yards Junior Championship, and the following qualified for the final : B. F. Walden, A. D. Sexton, D. Cook, and R. C. Negus. Basil Walden, a past Surrey junior sprint champion, beat Dick Negus with Alan Sexton third, in a very closely contested final. We also had two heats in the Club 220 Yards Championship, and the final was between Botwright, Machell, Read and Dumbrill. Teddy Read made no mistake and went right away to win in quite good time with Stan Botwright, the past holder, second and Dicky Dumbrill third. There was also two heats for the Junior 220 and the final saw P. J. Briggs, R. C. Negus, D. Cook and A. D. Sexton facing the starter, our old friend, A. G. Fell, who we must thank most heartily for his very valuable help in this direction throughout the season. Alan Sexton ran a fine race to turn the tables on his old rival, Dick Negus, and D. Cook also ran well to gain third place. There were again two heats required for the 440 Yards Championship, and Jack Frost, Len Dally, a newcomer to our ranks, Len Marchant and Syd Jarlett, who only beat Bob Wise on the tape, qualified for the final. This proved a hotly contested race with Jack Frost just staying home to beat Len Marchant with Syd Jarlett again displaying his finishing powers to gain third place. The 880 Yards Junior race saw Arthur Bruce gain a comfortable victory with Len Bishop just pipping his brother Eric on the tape for second place. A large field faced the starter for the 880 Yards Club Championship and Len Marchant made the pace throughout to win in 1 min. 59 secs., which is a new Club record. Len Herbert, the holder, tried vainly to overtake the leader, but had to be content with second place with John Brown, coming down from Catterick, to gain third position. Six runners beat the standard time of 2 mins. 8 secs., which must also be a new Club record. In the 1 Mile we had expected Derrick Burfitt to make a bold challenge to Len Herbert, the holder, but Derrick decided to save himself for the Bank Holiday meeting at the White City, where he was running for the English A.T.C. against the French Juniors. Herbert, however, ran a splendid race to win in 4 mins. 25.6 secs., which just beat his previous Club record for this race. V. S. Blowfield did 4 mins. 27.6 secs., to finish in second place, and John Brown gained yet another third place medal. The 2 Miles Walk saw Harry Churcher beat Joe Coleman, the past holder, and D. McMullen finished third with Jack Rutland fourth. In the Field Events several new title holders were seen, and Alan Dunn is to be complimented on bringing off a fine double in winning the Javelin and Discus events. F. E. Norman, a pre-war member, now out of the Forces, won the Long Jump, and was also second to Dick Negus in the High Jump. Jerry Thompson beat Syd Jones in the Weight Putt, although both men have done better performances during the season. So concluded our first post-war championship meeting, and we have every reason to be more than satisfied with the various results. We must also thank the various officials who came along to assist in what everyone agreed was a splendid meeting in every way. Results 100 Yards, Boys' : 1 A. D. Davis, 2 D. M. Willis, J. A. items.s: INTER-CLUB MATCH AT TOOTING Report and results of the five-sided inter-club evening match at Tooting on 21 August 1946, won by Belgrave with 27 points from Herne Hill, Cambridge H., Metropolitan Police and Surrey A.C. Held on Wednesday evening, August 21st, it was a five-sided Inter-Club Match, and some very keen competition was seen. H. Wickerson, running for Cambridge H., won the 100 Yards with George Pallett beating Dicky Dumbrill for second place. T. L. Higgins, the Public Schools' quarter champion, beat Ted Read in the 220, and scored a double by also winning the 440, in which Jack Frost finished third. V. S. Blowfield ran a great race to win the 880 Yards in the good time of 2 mins. 1.4 secs., and has fully justified our early season hopes. There being no Mile race, Len Herbert ran in the 2 Miles event, and after a fine tussle with Tommy Rowe of Herne Hill, Len ran home a good winner in 9 mins. 33.6 secs. Bill Lucas also caught Rowe close home and so gained second place. In the Field Events Syd Jones won the Weight with 38ft. 4in., and showed he is fast getting back to his pre-war performances. Syd also gained second place in the Discus, and it was the latter result that finally decided the match. The final match scores were : Belgrave H. 27, Herne Hill H. 24, Cambridge H. 19, Metropolitan Police 15, Surrey A.C. 5. items.s: "WADDILOVE" MEETING Report of the Waddilove inter-club meeting promoted by Birchfield Harriers at the Alexander Sports Ground, Perry Barr, where a depleted Belgrave team finished level fourth in the senior match and third in the junior contest. Held at the Alexander Sports Ground, Perry Barr, this Inter-Club meeting promoted by our old friends the Birchfield Harriers, was watched by a large crowd. We had sent up a team for the Senior contest, and as past holders of the trophy were keen on putting up a good show. This year they had a Junior contest in conjunction and it was also decided to support this. However, our team was sadly weakened by the absence of Marchant and Frost, who were on R.A.F. duties, and the terrific queue at Paddington looked like ending our journey before we had started. Eventually six Senior and seven Juniors arrived at the ground, and Ted Read did well to gain second place in his heat of the 100 Yards. Syd Jarlett also ran second in his 440 heat, and then Charlie Jones gained third place in the Long Jump, which he followed up with second place in the Javelin. Our three remaining Seniors were in the 2 Miles Team race and Len Herbert ran second to Sydney Wooderson in the individual race and with Bill Lucas fourth and Dick Tobin eighteenth, we finished third in the Team race, beaten by a margin of 4 points for first place. Even with our depleted forces we managed to finish level fourth with Blackheath in the match, and beat such clubs at Birchfield, Small Heath, Southgate, Tipton and Sparkhill. In the Junior contest, Dick Negus was second in his heat of the 80 Yards Sprint, and then in the 1 Mile Team race. Arthur Bruce was third in the individual race and was well backed up by Eddie Short, but Len Bishop found the pace too hot and was some way behind. Even so, our team finished second in the team result and can be well satisfied with their efforts. In the heats of the 4 x 110 Yards Relay, our team of Negus, Cook, Lewis and Sexton, were second and they finished third in the final, a very fine effort. In the match result we were placed third with Manchester A.C., and I am sure our lads will find the experience of such competition stand them in good stead for future contests. Thus, although our numbers were small it can be said that our lads did extremely well in the circumstances and it is hoped that next season we shall be able to send full-strength teams for both Senior and Junior contests.
