items.sum: Report and results of the final club handicap meeting of the 1946 track season at Tooting on 7 September, highlighted by Len Marchant's 1 min. 56.8 secs. half-mile from scratch, with a novices' mile and veterans' events.
items.s: FINAL CLUB HANDICAP MEETING Report and results of the final club handicap meeting of the 1946 track season at Tooting on 7 September, highlighted by Len Marchant's 1 min. 56.8 secs. half-mile from scratch, with a novices' mile and veterans' events. Our final track meeting of the season at Tooting was held on September 7th. The events were well supported but we still have a long way to go before we get back to the old days at Battersea Park, where we have had to run heats in the Half-mile Club Handicap event. Compared with other clubs, however, we must count ourselves very fortunate and with new members still coming in at every committee meeting, we look forward to once again being the strongest athletics club in the country. We had five heats in the 100 Yards, although not every heat was a full one, and heat winners were E. G. Read, B. F. Walden, A. D. Davis, A. D. Sexton and S. C. Botwright. Basil Walden won the final from Ted Read, the scratch man, and A. D. Davis just beat Sexton for third place. With three heats in the 300 Yards, the following qualified : Jack Frost, off the scratch mark, Bob Wise, P. J. Briggs, G. Weston, a son of our weight-putter, B. C. Lulham and Alan Sexton. Both Frost and Sexton were absentees from the final, which was won by a Junior member in P. J. Briggs, with G. Weston, Jnr., second, and Bob Wise third. The 880 Yards saw a really magnificent performance by Len Marchant who from scratch mark gradually overhauled his field to win by a yard or so in the startling time of 1 min. 56.8 secs. Apart from the days of Tommy Scrimshaw, we think this is the fastest half-mile accomplished by a Club member and it is a pity that Len did not produce this form until the season was almost over. However, it promises well for next season and we may yet have an A.A.A. title winner at this distance, bearing in mind Tom Scrimshaw's great effort when he was beaten into second place. In the 2 Miles Run, young A. H. Bruce ran a finely-judged race to win in easy fashion and here is another youngster who seems destined for the highest honours. Charlie Smart ran a fine race to gain second place and did 9.29 off his mark of 50 yards. Syd Jarlett showed his stamina by gaining third place in a fast-run race. A. H. East kept up his improved form by winning the 2 Miles Walk, and Joe Coleman walked well to finish second with P. Wilson third. The Field Event handicaps were well supported and Bill Sutton and Syd Jones were among the prize-winners, and it was pleasing to see Laurie Jackson gaining a first award. We also held a 1 Mile Novices' race and this attracted quite a good entry, and also resulted in several new members for the Club. Ken Stimpson, a younger brother of Ted, ran a good race to win the event while the second man, A. J. Wade, also showed nice style and should improve with added experience. The Veterans' A.C. also had a couple of events on the programme, and it was interesting to see Frank Webb and Ernie Duffet still doing their stuff to good effect. Before the War we used to hold Club Veterans' races, mostly over the sprint distance, but I remember a Club Veterans' Walk which included Bob Ricketts, Harry Evans and many others, and which was won by our old "clerk of the course," Bill Fish, who we were pleased to see at some of our meetings this season. e: Junior Match at Duke of York's
items.s: JUNIOR MATCH AT DUKE OF YORK'S Report of a junior match against the County of London Army Cadets Force at the Duke of York's Track, Chelsea, on 26 June 1946, won by Belgrave 17-10. On Wednesday, June 26th, we met the County of London Army Cadets Force at their headquarters, the Duke of York's Track at Chelsea. With only one representative allowed from each team, we had the individual winner in every event, bar one. Dick Negus won the 100 Yards and also the High and Long Jumps. Geoff. Freestone won the 220 Yards and D. Pollard, a son of our former Police sprinter, finished second in the 440. D. F. Platt won the Half-mile and Arthur Bruce the Mile, while P. J. Briggs won the 120 Yards Hurdles in quite good time for a Junior and should do well at this event with more opportunities of match competition. Our relay team, consisting of Negus, Briggs, Fleming and Freestone, won this event, and the final match scores were Belgrave H. 17, Army Cadet Force 10. items.s: JUNIOR MATCH v. S.L.H. Report of a junior match against South London Harriers at Tooting on 19 August, won by Belgrave 53-48. Held at Tooting on August 19th, this proved a closely contested match and I am sure the result gave our lads much pleasure. Bruty, of S.L.H., won both sprint races and Dick Negus was second in the 100 and Alan Sexton was second in the 220. Betterton and Freestone were first and second in the 440 and Eric Bishop gained third place in the 880 Yards. Arthur Bruce won the 1 Mile, and although the S.L.H. boys won the Relay, we picked up some useful points in the Field Events through the help of Alan Dunn, Dennis Fleming and A. C. Allen, and the final match scores were Belgrave H. 53, S.L.H. 48. items.sum: Notes on Belgrave long-distance runners' 1946 season: Finchley, Surrey County and Kent County 20-mile races, the Poly Marathon, the A.A.A. Marathon and a 15-mile invitation race at Salisbury.
items.s: MARATHON NOTES Notes on Belgrave long-distance runners' 1946 season: Finchley, Surrey County and Kent County 20-mile races, the Poly Marathon, the A.A.A. Marathon and a 15-mile invitation race at Salisbury. Our long-distance runners have had a busy season and some good performance have been recorded. The Finchley 20 Miles Open, held on a four-lap course at Ruislip, on April 27th, attracted a big field, and it was encouraging to see a number of Belgrave supporters. Dan Patience ran well to finish eighth, White and Doubleday, short of training, faded out over the last two miles and were both outside standard time (2.15). Will Spencer, one of our Police runners, made his first attempt at this type of race, but retired at 15 miles. The revived Surrey County 20 Miles Road Race was held at Mitcham, on May 18th, on what was roughly a two-lap figure-eight course. The race was started by His Worship the Mayor of Mitcham. For the first 10 miles the field kept together, then came a short sharp shower and the field split up. The winner was F. Harmer, of Herne Hill Harriers, who led one of his clubmates home in 2 hours 4 minutes 45 seconds. Syd Ring was third in 2.5.54, Bert Mitchell fifth in 2.8.10, Fred White seventh in 2.8.19, Gordon Doubleday eighth in 2.10.4, and Will Spencer eleventh in 2.17.21. Our finishers all gained County Standard Medals (within 20 minutes of the winner). Spencer deserves congratulations for his performance, and no doubt with more long-distance training he will show faster times; he has an easy flowing style which should suit him well for this type of race. In the team event, three to score, Herne Hill beat us 11 points to 14, with Mitcham A.C. third. In the Kent County Open 20 Miles, held at Chislehurst, on May 25th, Dan Patience ran his best 20 miles to date to finish third in 2 hours 0 minutes 13 seconds. Fred White and Bert Mitchell both finished inside Standard (2 hours 15 minutes), and the team (three to score) was third. The Poly Marathon was held on June 16th, from Windsor to Chiswick. Before the race the runners were inspected by H.M. the King, who acted as Starter to the 99 competitors. Fred White ran his best and finished eighteenth in 2 hours 58 minutes 50 seconds, Bert Mitchell twenty-seventh in 3 hours 7 minutes 0 seconds, Gordon Doubleday fifty-fourth in 3 hours 30 minutes 25 seconds, and Jim Watson sixty-fourth in 3 hours 41 minutes 37 seconds. Dan Patience and Syd Ring retired when well placed owing to sickness. The A.A.A. Marathon was held on the pre-war out and home course from the White City Stadium. Bert Mitchell was thirteenth in 2 hours 59 minutes 45 seconds, and Doubleday fourteenth in 3 hours 4 minutes 2 seconds, both gaining A.A.A. Standards (3 hours 5 minutes). Fred White had an "off-day" and retired. If he could have produced his previous form he would no doubt have gained a Standard too. As we go to press it has been announced that next year's Marathon Championship will be held apart from the Track Championships. If this means some refreshments and pointsmen along the route it will be a welcome step, as these were entirely lacking in this years' race, except for a few volunteer pointsmen. An Invitation "Marathon" of 15 miles was held at Salisbury on August Monday. The course included a mile-long climb over the Wiltshire Downs. Doubleday was ninth in 1 hour 34 minutes 56 seconds, and White eleventh in 1 hour 36 minutes 0 seconds, the winner being our old Tipton friend, Jack Holden, who covered the course in the very fast time of 1.22.05. items.sum: Report of the Belgrave Harriers Annual General Meeting at Belgrave Hall on 5 October 1946, with the secretary's and treasurer's reports, Honorary Life Membership for Harry Churcher and Charlie Jones, and the election of Harry Parker as President.
items.s: THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING Report of the Belgrave Harriers Annual General Meeting at Belgrave Hall on 5 October 1946, with the secretary's and treasurer's reports, Honorary Life Membership for Harry Churcher and Charlie Jones, and the election of Harry Parker as President. This was held at Belgrave Hall on Saturday, October 5th, with R. J. Savage in the Chair. The President opened the meeting by welcoming both those who had returned to the Club from the Services and our new members. He then paid tribute to the progress of the Club, especially the Juniors. He also thanked the Hon. Secretary and Hon. Treasurer, and other Club Officials for their good work through the last year. The minutes of the last A.G.M. were read and signed. An apology for absence was read from H. E. Thaxter. The Hon. Secretary then read his report. Mention was made of the great victories of our cross-country teams, of the gaining of International vests by Len Herbert (England) and David Main (Ireland) and of the great leadership of our Captain, Tom Carter, the Southern Champion. Of the walkers Jack Rutland was outstanding with seven individual wins in Open Road Walks. The Track and Field Events Sections had also performed well. The Juniors had maintained very good progress, with Derrick Burfitt again pre-eminent. For his win in the A.A.A. Junior 1 Mile Title—and many other excellent performances, the Club had awarded Burfitt an Honours Badge. The recruitment of new members was very satisfactory, 107 having joined us during the year. The Hon. Treasurer then presented his Accounts and Balance Sheet. The return to our normal programme had brought us in extra expenses, and he was pleased to be able to show us a balance on the right side. He expressed gratitude for the work done by Les Cohen in connection with the Building Fund. Before the Balance Sheet was put to the meeting and adopted, the Hon. Auditors, J. B. Belchambers and T. Cotton, paid tribute to the Hon. Treasurer's sound and efficient accounting. The next business was that of honouring two of our members with Honorary Life Membership. The Committee's nominations were Harry Churcher and Charlie Jones. In proposing the former, Syd Roberts recounted Harry's joining the Club in 1930 and of his rapid progress, culminating in his two seasons of invincibility on the road over the shorter distances, and of his winning the A.A.A. 2 and 7 Miles' Titles in 1939, having been placed to foreign winners in previous years. Frank Elson, seconding, recounted how Harry's progress had put Belgrave on the map again and linked his name with Tommy Green's in that respect. Harry's work for the Club behind the scenes was also mentioned, for he spends many hours helping brother Charlie. In proposing Charlie Jones, Alf Harley mentioned Charlie's early days with the Club in 1925 as a runner. He gradually transferred his affections to the Field Events Section, and has carried on the good work of George Powell. Thanks to Charlies' enthusiasm and leadership we can always rely upon the Field Events men to get us a good bag of points in Club Matches. Amongst many very good personal performances he can include a County Championship, the Surrey 440 Yards Hurdles, won in pre-war days. He had also done much good work on the administration and social side, and his help on legal questions has been of great use to the Committee. Harry Evans formally seconded, with further tributes to Charlie's work for the Club. Both were duly elected. The next business was the all-important one of Election of Club Officers. The President proposed to the meeting that his successor should be Harry Parker. This was seconded by Jimmy Belchamber, and received the unanimous vote of the meeting. It must have been a very proud and happy moment for Harry, as he proceeded to the highest honour the Club can bestow. It must be very gratifying to him to be President of the Belgrave Harriers, English Cross-Country Champions, etc., etc., especially as our present-day strength and position are in no small way due to his efforts. As the second world war dragged on most athletic clubs shrank to a very few members, some, including many famous ones, packed up for the duration. When Alf Harley joined the Forces, leaving us with no Secretary, Harry came to the rescue; and was key man of that band of club officers who kept things going. Harry has always paid generous tribute to those who helped the Club in those trying and difficult days, but, as General Hon. Secretary, he had all of the Clubs' activities at his finger-tips. In addition he kept track of our serving members, and Club literature has chased many members as they have moved from place to place. He must have written hundreds of letters—his postage bill must have given the Government more than any War Weapons Week did! One of the best tributes that can be paid to his efforts is that during one year of the war we signed on over eighty new members. (What club could boast of even eighty members then?) Harry inherits what he has largely helped to build and sustain, and it is hoped that his term of office will see further honours brought to the Club. It was then proposed by Alf Harley and seconded by Ken O'Kell, that those two great Belgravians and Clubmen, Tommy Green and Ernie Duffett, be elected to the list of Vice-Presidents. The meeting granted hearty approval. The other officers were elected as shown on an earlier page. Alf Harley resumes his old job of General Hon. Secretary, and the President has offered him every assistance. It might be added that communications regarding fixtures, etc., are normally dealt with by the Sectional Secretaries. With the expansion of the Club, and of the fact that the Hon. Treasurer is a very busy man nowadays, an Assistant Treasurer has been appointed, Tommy Morrell. Tommy is a "regular" at Belgrave Hall, and will be very pleased to know you—if he doesnt' already! With Bert Footer back at Cross-Country Captain we should be able to take on all-comers. We hope that the Juniors will support the new Junior Captain, Eddie Short. Frank Webb will be keeping an eye on the Juniors. Frank needs no introduction to the older members and can be commended as a pattern for any Junior. He has represented the Club from 100 yards to ten miles and is most willing to impart some of his experience to the younger members. So Juniors, it is up to you, get to know Frank and talk with him over your training and racing probliems. Coming to the Social Side, we have Dave Shepherd as Hon. Social Secretary, and Dave asks for the co-operation of all so that Club Social functions can be successful. When "Any Other Business" was called a number of points were raised, many of which will have the attention of the new Committee. It was pleasing to hear the Juniors stating their views, and, moreover, they presented them in a very able manner—we shall not lack good Committee men in future years ! The meeting closed with a vote of thanks to the Chair. R. J. Savage R. J. Savage chaired the A.G.M. H. E. Thaxter H. E. items.sum: Review of the Belgrave walkers' 1946 summer season on track and road, with new members and R.W.A. committee news; results follow as separate items.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS Review of the Belgrave walkers' 1946 summer season on track and road, with new members and R.W.A. committee news; results follow as separate items. The summer season provided a full programme for our walkers, both on the track and in the long distances on the road. All events have been well supported with creditable results to the Club. In the two National Championships on the road we had to be content with a minor placing—in the 20 Miles tieing for second place with Met. W.C., and in the 50 Kilos, third to Leicester, who scored a splendid double. Owing to "V" celebrations, our Police walkers were unable to assist in the 50 Kilos, resulting in the team being weakened. Another handicap has been the foot trouble of our Road Captain, Charlie Churcher, which eventually resulted in him giving up walking for a period whilst undergoing treatment. On the track Harry Churcher has made rapid progress during the summer in regaining some of his pre-war form and although he lost both his A.A.A. titles at 2 and 7 Miles, put up the best time of anyone in the country this season when finishing second in the 2 Miles. In the 7 Miles the following morning, Harry was seriously handicapped by having to work almost until the start of the race, but even so, finished third. Our Inter-Club match of 1, 2, 3 and 4 Miles, a popular feature of our pre-war programme, did not receive the support we hoped for, but a very keen struggle developed betwen us and Highgate Harriers, which resulted in a win for the Club by 3 points. Since the date of this match, however, many clubs have been considerably strengthened by the return of further men from the Forces, and we look forward to a good entry next year. The 24 Hours' race, promoted by Met. W.C., resulted in Colin Sutton and Bob Martin qualifying for membership of the Centurions' Club, and both are to be congratulated on their excellent performances under most adverse conditions. The Club Championship on the track proved a great success, five of our walkers gaining 1st class standard, with Harry Churcher wresting the Championship from Joe Coleman. In the Inter-Club match at Motspur Park on 31/8/46 against strong opposition and without the assistance of our track champion and Bob McMullen, both on holiday, we scored another success, Joe Coleman and Jack Rutland finishing second and third respectively, backed up by Bob Readman in seventh position. A very successful season terminated with a Track Handicap on 7/9/46 and the London to Brighton Walk on the following Saturday. In the latter, despite the fact that we did not get placed, four of our walkers qualified for 1st class standard, viz., Colin Sutton, Bob Readman, Stirling Wakeley and Joe Wilson, finishing in that order. Stirling Wakeley is to be congratulated on his very fine effort so early in his racing career. Ten of our walkers started off from Westminster followed by a strong band of supporters in coach and car. Many more familiar faces were met on the road down including Tommy Green and Bert Clayton. The weather was good for the first four hours of the race, after which a drizzle started which gradually developed into a steady rain and coupled with a strong wind, conditions gradually worsened, greatly handicapping the walkers in general. Colin Sutton, holder of our Long-distance Championship, recovering from an attack of flu' only a week before, maintained his position as leader of the Club and although he lost some ground over the later stages of the race, retained his title. Readman and Stirling Wakeley engaged in a battle for second place uuntil about 100 yards from home, when Bob found that extra bit necessary to take him in front. Of our ten starters, only Becke retired after covering about 40 miles, the continuous rain eventually proving too much for him. Despite the bad weather, Frank Thomson was on the front to see the walkers finish. New members continued to be enrolled, two as a result of a Novices' race at Tooting during the summer, and a hearty welcome is extended to A. Caldwell, W. Hooper, E. Fifield, W. Wesson and R. Frazer, who have all joined since our last issue. Fred Herring is now a first-claim member. Of these, three are Juniors, and should help to build up our team for next year. Congratulations to Bert Joels on his marriage. Bert is one of our most promising Juniors and now that he has settled down, we hope to see him out regularly again. Once again the Chairmanship of the R.W.A. Southern Committee has been awarded to one of our members, Syd Roberts, our Walking Secretary and Handicapper having taken over office from Alf Harley. The latter has found further work to do in the capacity of Treasurer to the R.W.A. Our Track Captain, Joe Coleman, is now a member of the Southern Committee, so that we now have three members representing us in this direction. Summing up, the activities of our walkers during the summer season, with the addition of our new members, points to a most successful winter season. All walkers are again asked to bear in mind the need for still more members. Results since our last issue are appended. items.sum: Article marking the 100th issue of The Belgravian, tracing its editors since 1925, Gordon Doubleday's resignation as Hon. Editor, and early club successes.
e: South of the Thames Junior Race
items.s: NUMBER 100 Article marking the 100th issue of The Belgravian, tracing its editors since 1925, Gordon Doubleday's resignation as Hon. Editor, and early club successes. We are all rather inclined to accept an issue of the Belgravian when it arrives as something that just "happened," and seldom do we think of the hours of preparation that go into each issue, or of the care and attention which somebody must devote to every sentence on every page before it passes into print. This issue of The Belgravian is No. 100, and an appropriate moment for wishing ourselves an ever-increasing measure of success for record in the next hundred issues, and to glance back quickly over the years which have given us our first hundred Belgravians. A Club Gazette of sorts existed in the earlier days of the Club and copies of a duplicated 1908 issue have been preserved; but our first printed Belgravian came off the presses in April, 1925. Harry Hare was the first Hon. Editor, and found time in addition to his other multifarious Club duties to give our Gazette an excellent start in life. After producing nine issues, in October, 1927, Harry handed over the Editorial blue pencil to Ben Knifton, who gave us thirteen issues, now in resplendent claret and gold colours. In April, 1929, Alf Harley took over and remained in the Editorial chair for nearly ten years, until becoming General Hon. Secretary in September, 1938. During those momentous years in the Club's history, 59 issues made their appearance. Our present Hon. Editor, Gordon Doubleday, followed on, but the coming of the war and an enforced move to Exeter rendered his task difficult, and its performance all the more praiseworthy. The cares of Editorship furrowed other foreheads for single issues during the difficult days of war, but in the main "Doub" was in charge of this important feature of our Club life, which became trebly important with our membership dispersed through the world on war service. He has now brought us up to No. 100, which you have before you. "Doub" has announced his resignation from the Hon. Editor's position to take effect immediately, and our very sincere thanks go to him for all his considerable work on our behalf, often under extremely adverse conditions. We hope he will be a frequent contributor to the Gazette he has graced as Hon. Editor during past years. And now a quick glance back to our early editions, just to remind you of the Club's progress during 21 years. The walkers had already known the thrill of winning National Championships, but in 1925 the runners were recording their first real successes, in winning the South of the Thames Junior Race and the Surrey County Cross-Country Championship. In 1926 we essayed our first London-Brighton Relay and finished fourteenth of 19 competing clubs. Our scribe wrote: "The prospect of competing next year is not hopeless and with some little enthusiasm among a few more members we shall find that we can show vast improvement on this year's performance, satisfactory as it may seem as a first attempt." Later we were to win the event three years in succession against the finest competition in the British Isles—and the history of this one event is akin to our Club improvement in all spheres. We have gone a long way since those early successes were recorded, and we all know, those who have assisted in any degree in our subsequent climb to fame. There are still further rungs to ascend, and may the Belgravian continue to record our successes (and our disappointments, lest we tend to lose any sense of proportion), our Club life, and all that goes to make Belgrave mean so much to everyone of us! And so, on from our first hundred Belgravians, towards our second century—with the goodwill and help of every loyal Club member! A. A. H. A. A. H. A. A. H. Harry Hare Harry Hare first Hon. items.sum: Gordon S. Doubleday's farewell note on resigning as Hon. Editor of The Belgravian.
items.s: Gordon S. Doubleday's farewell note on resigning as Hon. Editor of The Belgravian. You will have read in the above article that I am resigning from the post of Hon. Editor of the Belgravian. Producing this gazette has been a pleasure—a feeling which can be ascribed to anything connected with this Great Club. My work has brought me in close association with both officials and athletes, both in peace and in the trying days of war. We are, in a way, a motley crowd, we come from different walks of life, have different jobs, different outlooks and points of view, but, when we get together those are forgotten and we unite in the cause of the success and good-fellowship we have learnt to associate with the Club. During the war there were many incidents of kindness and sympathy between members whose only bond was just that they were fellow members of the Belgrave Harriers. The Committee, in the early days of the war, decided to continue publication of the gazette as a means of keeping members in touch with the Club. It has been pleasing and gratifying to read the letters from the lads who went overseas. Now I find that I have not the time at my disposal that I used to, and am taking the obvious step. I am extremely grateful to those who have helped me from time to time. I hope that I can be of some assistance to future Hon. Editors—I am confident that the lads will provide excellent material to write about. Keep it up! Belgrave. GORDON S. DOUBLEDAY. Gordon S. Doubleday GORDON S. DOUBLEDAY retiring Hon. Editor of The Belgravian

items.s: Short report of Belgrave's third place in the Invitation 2 Miles team race at the Blackheath Harriers Open Meeting, second place in the 4 x 100 yards relay, and a relay success at Guildford. At the Blackheath Harriers Open Meeting our team was third in the Invitation 2 Miles, in which Sydney Wooderson attempted to lower the British Record. The scoring was very close, Blackheath 18 points, Finchley 19 points, and Belgrave 20 points. Len Herbert ran very well to finish second to Wooderson. Charlie Smart and Ted Stimpson completed the team. In the 4 x 100 Yards Relay our four ran second to Achilles, our runners were Teddy Read, Dicky Dumbrill, Jack Frost and Michael Broadbent. Another Relay success was at Guildford, Lulham, Hawkins, Osmint and Read each pulled away from their rivals. At this meeting Read won the 220 Yards and Osmint the 100 Yards (under 18) off 3½ yards, in 10.15 seconds against a strong wind. items.sum: Editorial on the first full post-war winter season, urging the club to build a strong track team before the 1948 London Olympics, with news of Southern Championship wins by Len Herbert and Derrick Burfitt.
items.s: Editorial Editorial on the first full post-war winter season, urging the club to build a strong track team before the 1948 London Olympics, with news of Southern Championship wins by Len Herbert and Derrick Burfitt. We are now at the end of what can be termed the first full post-war winter season. From the afternoon of the season's opening meeting at Belgrave Hall the atmosphere was set: time seemed to have slipped back and the years of the war became, in many minds, non-existent. As one who "arrived back" that afternoon not having been near Belgrave Hall since 1940, it was a startling joy to see again so many well-remembered faces and to be greeted with such a warmth of welcome. Many things have changed these past seven years and this club has lost some of its dearest and best members, but we are still a club with enthusiasm and unity about us. At present most things are opposed, or unhelpful, towards the pursuit of Athletics. This country, unlike many others, gives no official or material support to Amateur Sports Clubs of any kind. Whether this is for better or for worse is a debateable question, but it is our heritage that such clubs as ours should be free to control and run their pursuits without any outside interference or aid, therefore what we achieve can verily be called our own. We have much to achieve, both for the benefit of the Athletic world in general and for the glory of this Club. The task of this Club in the future must be to build a strong, thoroughly ALL-ROUND Club, setting an example of fair sportsmanship that will make our name a byword for such things and influencing all those who have contact with the Club. In 1948 the Olympic Games will be held in London. Between now and then it must be our object to build a Track team as strong as our Walking and Country teams have been for so many years. If we can achieve such eminence in these two spheres there is no good reason why we should not do likewise on the track. We have the talent, some of it already shown, some of it dormant, but to mention only these few names is to comment on a strength which could do much: Broadbent, Botwright, Burfitt, Blowfield, Nankeville, Marchant, Herbert, Read, Lucas, Stimpson. To reach our object on the track our training must be made more rigorous, new methods must be tried, progress must be noted and used to advantage, and above all we must train together and help each other. It is the only way that standards can be compared and raised. Such must be our objects. They have in turn a more profound aspect, for Athletics is one of the few truly amateur sports left. It requires much selfless endeavour for no material gain and it can only be successfully pursued if loved, and to love it is to love something outside yourself. Thus it helps to form an essentially unneurotic outlook in a world where the selfish and neurotic is ever more shrill and powerful in its beseeching. To help counter this modern disease even in our small way, is to achieve something of a rare sanity these days. Whilst this Edition is in progress the Southern C.C. Championship has been run. Len Herbert ran a magnificent race to win the Senior race, and Derrick Burfitt found a fine finish to win the Junior race. A weakened team in the Seniors were second to Aylesford Paper Mills and the Junior team ran very well to finish third to S.L.H. and T.V.H. items.sum: Obituary of walker Ted Jackman, a member since 1930, who died aged 35.
items.s: Obituary Obituary of walker Ted Jackman, a member since 1930, who died aged 35. It is with the greatest regret that we have to announce the death of TED JACKMAN at the early age of 35 years. Ted joined us in 1930 and quickly showed that he had walking ability. During the summer of 1931 he was placed frequently in Club Track Handicaps and, improving apace, was successful in Open Track Handicaps, his win in the Ponders End Fete and Gala being particularly memorable. His walking on the road also showed improvement, and although never attaining championship rank he was always a dependable club man. His personality was pleasing. A gentle modest bearing, combined with sterling character and excellent sportsmanship endeared him to all, and he will be sorely missed, for we can ill afford to lose such a splendid club man. Only the day before his death he was talking of his many friends within the Club, of which he has been a proud member for seventeen years. We are the richer for his friendship and loyalty, the poorer for his passing at such an early age. Frank Elson, Charlie Churcher and Charlie Poulter paid the Club's last respects at the funeral, and a wreath in Club colours testified to the esteem in which he was held. Our profound sympathy is extended to Ted's parents and sister in their very great loss. items.sum: Club news column: Surrey C.C. Championship win and county colours, walking successes, Britannia Shield race, South of Thames races and Coleman Cup, Olympic hopes, and notes on individual members.
items.s: Commentary Club news column: Surrey C.C. Championship win and county colours, walking successes, Britannia Shield race, South of Thames races and Coleman Cup, Olympic hopes, and notes on individual members. On page 6 will be found a short note from the Hon. Treasurer, Bill Webb. It is hoped that any guilty members will take note of the paragraph on subscription. Dave Martin Shepard and the Social Committee are doing great work now and are putting the Belgrave social side on its feet again. The repairs to Belgrave Hall have been completed and its use for frolics in the future will be as deplorable as ever was! The Belgrave News Letter, edited and printed by Frank Elson, is at its 69th Edition. It is a very well edited Letter and the idea behind it a sound one, for it does keep all members of the Walking Section in the closest touch with the doings (or would you prefer the word "victories," Frank!), of this illustrious Section. The Club Annual Dinner was most successful. The attendance was a record, the speeches complementary to all and not too long, the food good and the party spirit most excellent. We won the Surrey C.C. Championship again and Cadogan A.C. (our friends) were third in the Middlesex. Surrey Colours were won by Tom Carter, Len Herbert, Bill Lucas and Leslie Stokell. Middlesex Colours by Vic Blowfield and Geoffry Pearson. In the Kent Championships George Lucas was 5th and in the Herts. Championship Albert Frost was 4th. Both these Belgravians won their County Colours. War-time members Jimmy Green and Peter Moughan won their County Colours for Kent and Herts. respectively. Congratulations to our Junior Captain, Eddy Short, who was 4th in the London University C.C. Championships: George Lucas, 3rd in the North Kent District Race; Geoffry Pearson, 2nd in the Banks Championship. The Walking Section is winning everything at present in a most glorious fashion. All the big Southern "Opens" have fallen to us and Harry Churcher, closely followed by Jack Rutland, has once again proved himself unbeatable over his distances. The National races are yet to come, but we can own a measure of confidence in our ability to do well in these. In the Britannia Shield race last November, Len Herbert, running for the R.A.F., was 5th and 2nd Englishman home. Our Belgian friend and member, Etienne Gailly, was 7th, running for the Belgian Army, and our Poly member, Dick Towndrow, 15th, running for the British Army team. This Club extends its most sincere congratulations to Mr. E. J. Holt, of S.L.H., on his being made an Officer of the Order of the British Empire for his services to Athletics, which have indeed been great. We won the South of Thames "Junior." Bill Lucas and Len Marchant ran fine races to finish 1st and 2nd. In the South of the Thames "Senior" we were 2nd. Our score of 87 points, the lowest ever recorded for 2nd place, would normally have won us the race. Our congratulations go to the Aylesford Club, who turned out such a good performance to beat us. We won the Coleman Cup for the lowest score for 12 men home. Michael Broadbent and Derrick Burfitt have been mentioned in the press as being British Olympic hopes. We believe they can do it given the chances, and we hope others will join them by 1948. In view of the above it is interesting to note that Derrick, and Arthur Bruce, are awaiting their call up any moment now. Your Hon. Editor is receiving copies of The Scots Athlete. This is a first-class journal dealing very fully with events over the border. It makes extremely good reading. It is published by W. J. Ross at 69 St. Vincent Street, Glasgow, C.2. Annual subscription 6/6. It is good to see Arthur Penny running again and running as well as ever. Such veterans as Arthur are the salt of this club and the fact that they can come back, when not far short of 40 years, tells that past training has been good. All younger running members can learn a thing or two from such as Arthur. Ted Stimpson has recovered from his operation and is training again. We give Ted our best wishes for the future Track season—and what about the 1948 Olympic 10,000 metres, Ted? We were pleased to see Dick Murphy starting the Ten Mile Walk and presenting his shield to the winner, Harry Churcher. No mention was made in the Handbook of the winning by P. J. Briggs of the Surrey Junior Hurdles Championship last season. This was a most regrettable omission and we give our apologies to Briggs, who is now serving in the Army, and is stationed at Larkhill. Victor Blowfield is showing international form over the country. His winning of the Club Ten was magnificent. With good training Vic is going to be a menace to the best in the country during the next Track season. Also congratulations to a new member, Leslie Stokell, on his fine and ever-improving running this season. There are also big things in store for Les in the future. This column would like to see him try the 2 miles Steeplechase next summer. Bill Webb Bill Webb Hon. items.label: No. 101
items.sum: Hon. Treasurer's notes on when subscriptions fall due, juniors on National Service, damage to and engraving of club trophies, engraving of medals, and badges.
items.s: Hon. Treasurer's Notes Hon. Treasurer's notes on when subscriptions fall due, juniors on National Service, damage to and engraving of club trophies, engraving of medals, and badges. SUBSCRIPTIONS. Some misunderstanding appears to exist as to the date on which the club Annual Subscription becomes due. A number of members have assumed that the club Financial Year runs concurrently with the calendar year and that January 1st is the date on which subscriptions are due; others have regarded the date of their election to Membership as the governing date for payment. The clarification of this point is best served by a reference to rules 7 and 9 on pages 18 and 19 of the handbook, where it clearly states that the club financial year ends on September 15th and that subscriptions become due and payable on the date of the Annual General Meeting. It is important that outstanding subscriptions should be paid immediately. The normal running expenses of the club have to be met and a reference to the last balance sheet will show that they are no mean liability. Subscriptions should be forwarded or handed to the Hon. Treasurer. Alternatively they may be handed to the Assistant Hon. Treasurer, Mr. T. F. Morrell, or, in the case of walking members, to the Hon. Walking Secretary, Mr. S. Roberts. The official receipt will be issued by the Hon. Treasurer in all cases. Whilst it is good to reflect on the growing strength of the Junior Section, we cannot overlook that their lot is not particularly happy, having regard to the inevitable operation of the National Service (Armed Forces) Acts at a very critical stage in their athletic careers. It behoves us to keep them fully informed of club activities and events, and ensure them of an easy resettlement into club affairs on their return to civil life. The committee do not enforce the payment of club subscriptions during the period a junior member is called to service under these Acts. It is hoped, however, that junior members will notify the Hon. Secretary immediately they are called to service and keep him posted with subsequent movements. DAMAGE TO CLUB TROPHIES. In the event of a club trophy becoming damaged whilst in the safe keeping of the holder, no action should be taken regarding the repair of the trophy without prior authority of the committee. Any such action is likely to prejudice a possible claim through the club Insurance Policy. Damage to trophies, however small, and also any loss of trophy should be reported to the Hon. Treasurer immediately and a detailed statement of the casualty given. ENGRAVING OF CLUB TROPHIES. Although most holders of trophies have had my circular letter, I would here repeat as a reminder and as a guidance for future holders, that it is desirable that all trophies should be engraved up to date before the date of the next competition. Where practicable it would be appreciated if holders would arrange for the delivery of the trophy to the club engravers, The Alexander Clark Co. Ltd., 38 Leadenhall Street, E.C.3, together with the particulars of the records to be engraved; any outstanding particulars can be obtained from the Hon. Running Secretary, Mr. E. Duffett. In those cases where the records are engraved on small silver shields affixed to the trophy or to the plinth of the trophy, it will suffice if the blank small shields to be engraved are removed and posted to the engravers together with the necessary particulars to be engraved. In these cases, however, it is important that the last engraved shield should also be sent to serve as a specimen for the engraver. Where holders find this arrangement impracticable perhaps they would be good enough to arrange to let me have the trophy at a convenient date so that I can make alternative arrangements. ENGRAVING OF MEDALS. On the question of engraving of medals won by members, the last ruling given by the committee on this subject, which is still extant, is as follows: That the club undertake to engrave (1) All club medals; (2) All team race medals awarded by Athletic bodies and Associations to which the club is affiliated. BADGES, ETC. Vest badges 2/6, and Coat metal badges 2/-, are in stock. As these are sold at cost price it is requested that applications by post should be accompanied by return postage. It is regretted that there is no immediate prospect of obtaining supplies of vests and ties or other clothing. Any helpful suggestions from members on this vexed subject will be appreciated. FINALLY do not forget those subscriptions. A small item, but a very important item. You may win an award in the next club event and it would be very disappointing to find at the last moment that it was withheld because you had forgotten to pay your subscription. Be on the safe side and post it to me at once. W. G. W. W. G. W. W. G. W. Hon. Treasurer T. F. Morrell Mr. T. F. Morrell Assistant Hon. Treasurer Mr. T. F. Morrell S. Roberts Mr. S. Roberts Hon. items.sum: Running section notes: South of Thames Junior win, retention of the Pickett Cup in the Surrey County Senior Championship, coaches for the London to Brighton Relay, and summer track fixtures.
items.s: The Running Section Running section notes: South of Thames Junior win, retention of the Pickett Cup in the Surrey County Senior Championship, coaches for the London to Brighton Relay, and summer track fixtures. The results so far this season have shown our members to be carrying on the good work of last season, and although new teams have had to be found owing to the many barring clauses in some of the races, we again won the South of Thames "Junior" Race, and also supplied the first two men home. We also retained possession of the "Pickett" Cup for the Surrey County Senior Championship, although our nearest rivals, Herne Hill Harriers, put up a good show, but the forward packing of our runners turned the scales in our favour. The London to Brighton Relay is being held on April 19th, and intending supporters will be well advised to book a seat in our club coaches, which is in the hands of our Social Hon. Secretary, Dave Shepard. Track fixtures are now being made and we are hoping to hold several meetings at Tooting Common L.C.C. track, our first being on Saturday, May 17th. The previous week we have a match at the Drayton Green track with Ealing Harriers and Reading A.C. for the "Gordon Stewart" Trophy. On May 24th we have an Inter-Club match at Banstead Hospital, and members who went there last year will remember the good time, apart from the weather, that was had by all. Other fixtures, both home and away, are being arranged and it is hoped that members will do their best to support these matches, both Senior and Junior. All enquiries to the Running Hon. items.sum: Field events notes on the winter Coaching School, the S.A.A. League field events programme and a new Polytechnic Harriers multi-event competition for the Sward Trophy.
items.s: Field Events Gossip Field events notes on the winter Coaching School, the S.A.A. League field events programme and a new Polytechnic Harriers multi-event competition for the Sward Trophy. The winter field events activities have been confined to the Coaching School, which has been functioning since the beginning of November, 1946, at Belgrave Hall. Unfortunately it has not been as well supported as was anticipated, but it is hoped all who have been regularly attending will put to good use the things they have learnt when they start their summer training. With the completion of the programme the course will close, and Charlie Jones, Bill Sutton and Sid Jones will be at the Tooting Bec Track on Saturday afternoons when it is hoped the Juniors will appear and be put through their paces. The S.A.A. League (Fields Events Section) programme has just come to hand. It will be run on the same lines as last year with the exception that all events will take place on Monday evenings at the Tooting Bec Track during the months of May and June. A Junior League will also function in which Field Events will be included. In addition a Decathlon competition has been added this year for individual competitors. An interesting new competition is announced by The Polytechnic Harriers to take place at their Stadium on May 10th. The programme includes all the usual field events, three hurdle races and a steeplechase, comprising 11 events in all. The competition is both for individuals and teams. In the team competition four men score, and in this and the individual competition each competitor will be allowed to compete in not more than five selected events. Scoring will be by points from 20 points for first place to one point for 20th place. The "Sward Trophy" will be awarded to the winning team. It is hoped we can put up a very good show. T. C. J. T. items.sum: Walking section review of the winter road season, with Harry Churcher and Jack Rutland leading an unbeaten run in the open races, hopes for the National championships, Sunday strolls and new members.
items.s: With the Walkers Walking section review of the winter road season, with Harry Churcher and Jack Rutland leading an unbeaten run in the open races, hopes for the National championships, Sunday strolls and new members. Our walkers started the winter season on the road in no uncertain manner, twenty-eight members turning out for the opening Club 5 Miles Handicap. The first open, Highgate Harriers promotion, made it clear that we were making a rapid return to our pre-war predominance, at least over the shorter distances. Four in the first nine with the majority of clubs at full strength was certainly very promising. As time went on we won many other opens, Harry Churcher taking most of the individual honours with Jack Rutland a close second. As yet unbeaten, our lowest score was in the Cambridge Harriers open, when our placings were 1, 2, 3 and 5. So far there has been little opposition from the Midlands and North and presumably we shall have to wait for the new 10 miles championship to find out their present strength. One thing is certain, all the leading clubs in the country will do their utmost to become the first 10 miles champions and our succession of wins in open races will no doubt make our opponents all the more determined to prevent us from crowning our successes with National Honours. We therefore look to all concerned to see that the next few months re-establish us as the premier walking club in the country. As the National Junior Race will be over before this issue is out, little need be said, but young Mac's present form is good enough to annexe the individual title and that he will receive good support from Bert East, Harry Rouse, Joe Wilson and others. The team race on paper looks a very open affair, but once again there is not much indication of the opposition likely from the North and Midlands. With the two longer distances being held in the South, we shall not this year have the disadvantage of travelling. Although we were placed in both these races last year, with the combined efforts of all concerned, we should not be content with less than first place and a return to our pre-war position as National Champions at all distances. We have plenty of good material; all that is required is plenty of regular training, and especially for the longer distances, lots of strolling. Regarding the latter, your Road Captain, Charlie Churcher, is anxious to get a good muster for Sunday Morning strolls. With the approaching spring the weather should be more suitable for this, and it is hoped that this side of training will receive full support. The venue is Putney High Street at 9 a.m., but if you want to join in somewhere en route, get in touch with your Road Captain and he will be pleased to make the necessary arrangements. As a result of a Novices Race promoted by the M.P.A.A., two more Police members were enrolled. P. Sapcote and M. Archer, both of whom show every prospect of becoming useful walkers. George Bently, Fred's brother, back from the Forces, is with us again, and George Atkinson, also of the Police and a son of ex-Chief Inspector Atkinson, a former Barking to Southend winner, has joined us. Also Mac's young brother Sid, and Fred Herring, now first claim, will soon be available for teams. To our new members we extend a very hearty welcome and wish them many happy years with the club. Our aim is 100 active walkers, so it's up to everyone to do their bit to increase our numbers still further and thus provide some champions for the future. The Olympic Games are gradually creeping nearer. We already have men of Olympic class; these can quite easily be added to, and there is no reason why we should not produce another Olympic Champion, or perhaps even two—track and road. So good walking to you all and may our successes continue. S. R. items.sum: Junior section report on matches with Surrey A.C., Dartford Harriers and the India Cadet Company, the Surrey County Youths' and Junior Championships, and the Club Junior Cross-Country Championship for the Savage Shield won by Derrick Burfitt.
items.s: With the Juniors Junior section report on matches with Surrey A.C., Dartford Harriers and the India Cadet Company, the Surrey County Youths' and Junior Championships, and the Club Junior Cross-Country Championship for the Savage Shield won by Derrick Burfitt. On October 19th, at Wimbledon, we had a match with the junior members of Surrey A.C. and Dartford Harriers. We had the first three men home in Derrick Burfitt, Eddie Short and Arthur Bruce, who came in together, and they were followed by Len Bishop. Scoring three aside, the points were—Belgrave H. 6, Dartford H. 19, Surrey A.C. 25. In a further match of five aside between Dartford and ourselves, we won with the lower score of 25 to our visitors' 41. On November 23rd our lads made the journey to the Guards Depot, Caterham, where they were entertained to a match with the India Cadet Company. Eddie Short and Arthur Bruce came home together in first place, followed by a couple of Cadets, and then came the two Bishops brothers, Eric and Len. Next followed a whole crowd of Cadets, and eventually our other three runners, who were R. Garwood, K. E. Aspinall and B. C. Potter. The latter had lost their way and therefore their positions could not be counted in the team race. In view of the fact that we had four lads in the first six home, the Cadets very sportingly called the match a draw. Our lads then sat down to a real "Naafi" tea, and a good time was had by all! We had a team entered in the Surrey County Youths' Championship, which was held at Coulsdon on December 7th, but only managed to field four runners. Their finishing positions were—13 L. C. Bishop, 25.1; 17 E. T. Gilbert, 25.50; 39 K. E. Aspinall, 27.48; 55 L. Cheesley, 32.52. We finished sixth out of an entry of twelve teams, so our lads can be said to have done well, for with the exception of Len Bishop, this was their initial effort in on open event. The club also entered a team for the Surrey County Junior Championship, held at Earlswood on January 4th. Owing to Service calls, the age for this race being 18 to 21, we only fielded four runners, but they can be said to have done well in being beaten in the team race by the narrow margin of 2 points. Arthur Bruce ran well to finish third, with Eddie Short fourth, then Len Adams scored fifth, and Eric Bishop seventh. The course was very heavy and most of the runners had trouble in keeping their shoes on, a point to be borne in mind for future races. Finishing times of our runners were—3 A. H. Bruce, 30.24; 4 E. A. Short, 30.32; 6 L. A. Adams, 32.27; 8 E. M. Bishop, 32.50. Team scores were—S. L. H. 17 pts., Belgrave H. 19 pts. On January 18th our lads visited the Surrey A.C. at their quarters at Kingston. The match was over about 2½ miles and once again our trio of Derrick Burfitt, Eddie Short and Arthur Bruce, came home together in first place. Len Bishop duly followed in fourth place, and with the match scoring four aside, we won with the lowest possible score of 10 points to Surrey A.C.'s 26. Positions and times of our runners were—D. R. Burfitt, E. A. Short, A. H. Bruce, equal to 1st, 14 mins. 54 secs. 4 L. C. Bishop, 15.3; 6 R. Garwood, 15.21; 8 E. T. Gilbert, 15.22. The Club Junior Cross-Country Championship for the "Savage" Shield, had been postponed from December 21st owing to the frost-bound conditions, and it was now held over our usual 5 miles course on February 1st. Conditions were still far from ideal, the course being snow-covered, but a field of 8 juniors braved the conditions and are to be complimented on their fortitude. Derrick Burfitt retained his title, although Arthur Bruce ran very well to finish so close behind in second place. Eddie Short finished third, although below his usual form, and Len Bishop occupied his usual fourth place in junior events. The handicap, held in conjunction, was deservedly won by Arthur Bruce with R. Garwood taking second award and Eddie Short the third prize. Positions and times are given below:— E. A. D. items.s: 5 Miles C.C. Handicap Report and result of the club 5 Miles Cross-Country Handicap and match with Surrey A.C. at Wimbledon on 26 October 1946, scratch race won by Dick Towndrow and handicap by Vic Blowfield. 5 MILES C.C. HANDICAP SATURDAY, OCTOBER 26th, 1946, WIMBLEDON Held at Wimbledon on October 26th, and once again a very large field was seen out. We had a match with Surrey A.C. in conjunction with this race, and were pleased to welcome many old friends. Dick Towndrow, making one of his rare appearances in our colours, was a good winner of the scratch race, followed by Vic Blowfield, who in his first attempt at cross-country racing, certainly surprised many by his forward running. Stan Belton, of Surrey A.C., came along with Len Herbert, and they appeared to be taking things fairly steady, as is wise so early in the season. The Club Handicap was won by Vic Blowfield, who made good use of the Handicapper's generosity. Len Bishop, one of our promising junior members, came second, with Les Stokell, another newcomer to our ranks, taking third award. We were pleased to see Bert Footer and Arthur Penny, the famous Belgrave "twins," making a return to active racing again, and look forward to their help throughout the season. Scoring six aside in the match with Surrey A.C., we won the team contest by scoring 29 points to Surrey's 49. Result of 5 Miles Handicap * Dead heat Position Name Act. Time Start Hcp. items.s: Match v. Finchley Harriers Report of a heavy-going cross-country match with Finchley Harriers at Ruislip on 23 November, won by Belgrave 224½ points to 240½. On November 23rd we visited Ruislip for a match with the Finchley Harriers. The course was in a very bad state, being almost water-logged throughout, and for some of our members it was a most gruelling race. Finchley had the first two men home and then came Derrick Burfitt, who made light of the conditions, although losing a shoe, and having to catch up on his field again. Scoring 15 aside, we won the match with 224½ points to Finchley's 240½, but all the runners are to be complimented on finishing such a sticky course. Placings of our runners were—D. R. Burfitt 3, T. items.s: South of Thames "Junior" Race Report of the South of Thames Junior cross-country race at Nonsuch Park, Cheam, on 9 November, won by Bill Lucas with Belgrave "A" retaining the team title from Herne Hill. Held at Non-Such Park, Cheam, on November 9th, a field of 209 runners, representing 29 teams, fought out a closely-contested race over a two-lap course. As winners of the race last season, we thus had to find a new scoring team, and our hopes received a set-back when Vic Blowfield failed to arrive in time. However, at the half-way stage in the race, Bill Lucas and Len Marchant were in the leading bunch of four runners, which was a good start-off to our team's chances. When they came in sight of the finish Bill Lucas was clear away in front and in second position came Len Marchant, a fine performance by both runners. Herne Hill had three runners finish in a bunch and the team result was in doubt until the discs had been checked over. It was then found that we totalled 41 points to Herne Hill's 48, and we had thus repeated our victory of last year in this event. Finishing positions and times of our runners were:— 1 W. E. items.s: Match v. Thames Valley Harriers Report of a four-cornered cross-country match at Cranford on 7 December with Thames Valley Harriers, Surrey A.C. and Metropolitan Police A.C., won by Thames Valley with Belgrave second. Held at Cranford on December 7th, and a good crowd of our members were present. Other clubs competing in a four-cornered match were Surrey A.C. and Metropolitan Police A.C. Once again the course was very muddy but Stan Belton of Surrey, revelled in the conditions to come home a good winner. Vic Blowfield ran excellently to finish second, and continues to show great promise in his first season over the country. Scoring six aside in the four-club match, resulted thus—Thames Valley H. 45 points, Belgrave H. 59, Surrey A.C. 114, Metropolitan Police 256. items.s: Club Seven Miles C.C. Championship Report and result of the Club Seven Miles Cross-Country Championship at Wimbledon on 14 December 1946, won by Len Herbert from Vic Blowfield, with handicap placings. CLUB SEVEN MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP SATURDAY, DECEMBER 14th, 1946, WIMBLEDON The day was mild, but the fog which had hung over London for two previous days was still covering the common. The President started a field of 30 runners, a total nearly up to pre-war standards. Dick Tobin lead the field out at a fair pace, then bunched together were Carter, Bill Lucas, Clinton, Abberton, Eales, Blowfield, Penny, with Footer and Morrell a little behind, and Len Herbert at the rear. The race was next seen at the Windmill on the first lap. Here the field was beginning to shake itself out, Tom Carter was leading a group consisting of Clinton, Abberton, Penny, Blowfield and Herbert, but it was still anybody's race. This order was kept at the turn on to the second lap, albeit Footer was coming up to the leaders and was obviously running his usual "snaky" race. By now the Common was turning dark and very foggy, and it was obvious the race would finish in darkness. Over the last two miles or so Herbert went away in fine style to win from Vic Blowfield with Frank Abberton a strong third. These three were followed closely by Tom Carter and Bert Footer, Bert managing to beat Tom in a sprint down the finishing straight. Congratulations must go to Len Herbert on his first C.C. Club Championship and to Vic Blowfield and Frank Abberton on their improved running. Also to Bert Footer and Arthur Penny on their "comebacks." Result of 7 Miles C.C. items.s: Club Boxing Day Meeting Report and results of the club's Boxing Day track meeting at Tooting Common track, with the 100 yards handicap won by A. D. Sexton and the 2 miles by L. M. Marchant. Our annual track meeting was held on Boxing Day morning at Tooting Common track, and a large crowd was present to witness some good racing. In the 100 Yards Sprint Handicap there were six heats, although owing to absentees, some were sparsely filled. Heat winners were—D. Cook (8 yds.), A. C. Allen (8½ yds.), A. D. Sexton (5 yds.), R. C. Negus (5 yds.), J. Heathfield (7½ yds.) and E. M. Bishop (8½ yds.). The final was a closely-contested race between three of our junior members, and Alan Sexton just beat Dick Negus, with D. Cook third. In the 2 Miles Run, Derrick Burfitt, the A.A.A. junior mile champion, was on the virtual scratch mark of 20 yards. He ran an excellent race to work his way through the field, and although Vic Blowfield hung closely on his heels, Derrick finished a good second to Len Marchant, the winner, with a yard or two to spare from Vic Blowfield, who was third. 100 Yards Handicap—1 A. items.s: The County Championships Reports of Belgrave members in the Surrey, Middlesex, Kent and Hertfordshire county cross-country championships, including Belgrave's Surrey team title and Derrick Burfitt's fourth successive junior win. SURREY. The Surrey County Senior Cross-Country Championship was held over 7 miles of heavy country at Earlswood, on January 4th. Stan Belton, of Surrey A.C., soon went into the lead, and although Len Herbert, making his usual slow start, gradually overhauled his field, he could not catch Belton, who won in good style. Frank Abberton displayed fine form in gaining third place, and as he has now joined us first-claim, he should prove an asset to our teams. Bill Lucas ran in his usual excellent style to finish 4th, and Les Stokell, in his first season over the country, put up a fine performance to gain sixth place, and so gain his County colours. Tom Carter, although below his usual form, nevertheless ran a plucky race to gain twelfth position and split a couple of Herne Hill runners up the finishing straight to do so. Bert Mitchell was the sixth scoring member of our team in nineteenth place, and our thanks go to Jimmy Wood, our second-claim member, for helping Bert along. Other members of our team finished—21 Eric Herbert, 23 Tom Morrell, 25 Stan Eales, 32 Syd Jarlett, 39 Con Abberton, 42 Gordon Doubleday. The team championship resulted—1 Belgrave Harriers 45 points; 2 Herne Hill H. 74 points; 3 Surrey A.C. 101 points. MIDDLESEX. Our members in this race were representing Cadogan A.C., the holders of the title, but they sadly missed Dave Main, Dan Patience and Charlie Smart, and had to take third place in the team championship. Our members' positions and times were—8 G. M. Pearson, 53.5; 11 R. W. Tobin, 53.45; 23 K. G. Stimpson, 55.16; 32 H. W. Shields, 56.12; 37 A. E. Taylor, 57.4; 41 T. G. Clinton, 57.36; 46 A. Smith, 58.17; 59 C. Mains, 59.56. Derrick Burfitt retained his hold on the Junior title, which he won in 34 mins. 18 secs., and this makes his fourth successive win, which must be a record which will last for all time. KENT. George Lucas ran as an individual in his County Championship, and did well to finish in sixth place, thus gaining his County Colours. HERTS. A. E. Frost, our Civil Service member, ran in this race and finished fourth, and is now displaying a return to his pre-war form. items.s: Inter-Counties' Championship Report of Belgrave members running for Surrey, Middlesex, Kent and Hertfordshire in the Inter-Counties cross-country championship at Nottingham on 18 January, with Vic Blowfield sixth. This race was held at Nottingham on January 18th, and there were quite a number of Belgrave members representing their Counties. Tom Carter had made the journey as captain of the Surrey team, which also included Frank Abberton, Len Herbert, Bill Lucas and Les Stokell. Running for Middlesex were Vic Blowfield, who had dropped out of the County race owing to shoe trouble, and Geoff Pearson, while George Lucas was in Kent colours, and A. E. Frost was running for Hertfordshire. Our congratulations go to all these runners for the honour conferred upon them in representing their County, and Vic Blowfield is to be complimented on his fine showing in such company. To finish sixth only six seconds behind the winner was a fine performance and further honours should certainly come his way. George Lucas also did well in finishing thirteenth and helping his County to win the team championship. Frank Abberton was sixteenth, Len Herbert thirty-sixth, Bill Lucas forty-third, Les Stokell forty-fifth, Geoff Pearson sixtieth, and A. E. Frost ninety-fifth. S. Blowfield 58.45 (59.58 less 1.15 = 58.43, and the same 58.45 as A. H. Bishop, placed 9th) and B. Olver 70.15 (74.45 less 5.30 = 69.15). CLUB TEN MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP SATURDAY, JANUARY 25th, 1947 A very cold day greeted the small field for this race. Owing to sickness there were many notable absentees including both the Herbert's, both the Lucas's and Frank Abberton. The field was led out by Tom Carter but was well together when at 2 miles Carter went into the lead. Tom's lead, however, was doomed as his injured leg gave way immediately and he had to retire from the race. At the halfway stage Arthur Penny and Vic Blowfield were running together with the rest of the field strung out in this order—Pearson, Frost, Eales, Tobin, Stokell. Here Tommy Morrell, looking beat, retired, and Tom Clinton, well off form, was seen running well to the rear. Over the last three miles Blowfield moved away from Penny to win well and strongly. Thus at his first attempt Vic won the Macher Shield. His running this season being consistently good and improving, he certainly deserved the honour. Arthur Penny also showed some of his old form in giving Vic such a stiff race, his comeback is a magnificent one. Albert Frost and Stan Eales showed welcome returns to form and took the first and second handicap prizes. Position Name Act. Time Start Hcp. Time Postn. in Hcp. 1 V. S. items.s: Highgate Harriers' Open 7 Miles Report and Belgrave placings in the Highgate Harriers' open 7 miles walk on 26 October 1946, won by Harry Churcher from Jack Rutland, with Belgrave winning the team race and A. East disqualified. HIGHGATE HARRIERS' OPEN 7 MILES OCTOBER 26th, 1946 The first open event of the winter gave an indication of the possible opposition we were likely to encounter during the first real post war season. Our entry of four teams (29 individuals) was second only to that of the promoting club. Harry Churcher, going over the course for the first time, found it necessary to keep with Jack Rutland the greater part of the way. After a slow start up a very trying hill, these two soon got to the front of the field and thereafter maintained their lead throughout until the last few yards, when Harry just managed to finish 1 second in front of Jack. Backed up by McMullen (4th) and Joe Coleman (9th), we scored a fairly easy win with 16 points, the promoting club being 2nd with 24 points. A. items.s: Belgrave Open Walk Report and Belgrave placings in the club's own open walk on 30 November 1946, with 158 starters, won by Jack Rutland after Harry Churcher was ruled out, Belgrave winning the team race from Woodford Green and Leicester Walking Club, with thanks to prize-fund donors. BELGRAVE OPEN WALK NOVEMBER 30th, 1946 Our own open did not attract quite as large an entry as had been anticipated, but of the 176 entries 158 started on a signal from the Club President. Harry Churcher contented himself with accompanying C. Morris of the Surrey A.C. for the first lap, after which he began to make a lead. Jack Rutland, on returning to the common, then went up into second place, and with McMullen, Joe Coleman, Len Fletcher and Bob Readman not far behind it soon became apparent that, barring a number of accidents, we should add one more to our list of successes. Harry continued to walk in excellent style until about half-a-mile from home when, to the surprise of everyone, he was ruled out, leaving Jack Rutland in the lead. This unfortunate occurrence gave Len Fletcher, competing in his first open for a considerable time, an opportunity of sharing in the team honours. Despite Harry's misfortune we won easily from Woodford Green by 21 points to 55 points, with Leicester Walking Club third with 57 points. From the result of the Enfield Open it was evident that competition between the "A" and "B" teams for handicap awards would be very keen. This proved even closer than was anticipated and resulted in the "A" team taking first place with the "B" team 1 second behind. Colin Sutton, starting from a longer mark than Len Fletcher found his way into the winning handicap team at Len's expense. Joe Scamell took the Veterans' prize, and Bob Readman the special prize for the first club member not gaining any other award. The account would be incomplete without recording our most sincere thanks to the following for their donations to the prize fund:—Messrs. H. Evans, J. Bellchamber, A. A. Harley, A. Harley (Senr.), A. Beales, P. Wright, C. Sutton, F. Elson, C. Churcher, H. Churcher, J. Crump and F. Thompson. Also to Mrs. Churcher for presenting a special prize. Lastly we are indebted to the R.W.A. Officials and Hon. Handicappers, to the many club members who assisted as stewards and pointsmen, and to those clubs and individuals who supported the event and helped to make it the success which it has always been. Despite the close proximity to Christmas, 12 of our walkers turned out to tackle the hilly course, to our opponents 15, both sides had most of their best men out. This gave Harry Churcher the chance to catch up with him and after a neck and neck race, Harry eventually took the lead to win by 23 seconds. Sapcote took the novice's prize. M.P.A.A. 7 MILES OPEN JANUARY 18th, 1947, AT IMBER COURT The absence of Mac from our "A" team did not prevent us from continuing our succession of open wins. The very fast course was lengthened by 300 yards so that no comparison can be drawn with previous times, but despite this for the first time since the new handicapping system was introduced, the time standard of 53.30 was broken by Harry Churcher, who completed the course in 53.15, 29 seconds in front of Jack Rutland. Dick Murphy was there to start the race and also presented the awards at the conclusion. The cold weather and the additional distance, after sevens, seemed to affect many of the walkers, and apart from Harry Churcher times were not very good. Jack Rutland suffered with leg trouble during the later stages of the race and dropped back into 3rd position. items.label: No. 102
items.sum: Editorial apologising for the long gap since the last issue and, in the club's Diamond Jubilee year, urging members to remember the work behind Belgrave's success and to volunteer as officials.
items.s: Editorial Editorial apologising for the long gap since the last issue and, in the club's Diamond Jubilee year, urging members to remember the work behind Belgrave's success and to volunteer as officials. It has been a long time since the last issue. Your Hon. Editor must take some of the blame for this lapse. He apologises and hopes you will accept his excuses of too much work and, therefore, too little leisure in which to produce this journal. The rest of the blame must fall on that well-known scapegoat, “ circumstances beyond our control,” and on those few contributors who were tardy in sending their material. This is Belgrave's Diamond Jubilee year. Sixty years is a long time for a Club such as ours to have been in existence. It has seen two most terrible World Wars and it has lost some of its best sons in each. But now in this Year of our Lord, 1947, it is flourishing, winning and expanding like no other club in England to-day. Those of us who know Belgrave know the reason for this happy state of affairs. And we also know that we are not just enjoying one of those cycles of success but that the youth of the Club is pressing towards the day when it can burst into its own. One had only to observe, this summer, the members performing in the “ under sixteen ” events to see furthermore that we have a second layer of younger members already keen and already infused with the Belgrave spirit. Very satisfying all of this, but we must not become too smug, we must not accept our success as falling from the heavens to us. Remember, that it took hard work to build the Club. Hard work raising every penny of its money, hard work making runners, walkers, throwers, hard work organising, hard work enlarging the membership, and all of this must have often seemed at the time nothing but “ sweat, tears and blood.” We are now reaping our sowings. But let us remember, that it still means sowing, and to sow is to labour. The older members who helped to turn this Club into such a glorious one will not forget that which has passed. The younger members, knowing only the fullness of the Club, might be tempted to forget and take too much for granted at times unless they always carry in their minds a knowledge of the labour accomplished for their benefit and for the glory of the Club. So that a Club of Belgrave's size and importance should function efficiently a great deal of work is still being done by its officials. These people, the president, secretaries, treasurer, captains and vice-captains, elected committee, and many other volunteers and helpers, give up most of their spare time for the Club's good. We are always in need of good officials and willing helpers. So let anybody who thinks he can be of use in this way not hide his light under a bushel. We need you!

items.sum: Commentary column of club news: Frank Elson's recovery, Charles Smart's running in Germany, new member Bert Ellsey, members elected to S.C.C.C.A. and R.W.A. committees, Alf Harley's offices, Alf Taylor's return, Dick Towndrow joining, and social dates.
items.s: Commentary Commentary column of club news: Frank Elson's recovery, Charles Smart's running in Germany, new member Bert Ellsey, members elected to S.C.C.C.A. and R.W.A. committees, Alf Harley's offices, Alf Taylor's return, Dick Towndrow joining, and social dates. Mention of members' athletic feats are not being made in the Commentary for this issue. This is mainly because there have been so many of them that space would hardly permit. Such mentions are made elsewhere in this journal. It is, however, our aim to produce “ The Belgravian ” quarterly in the future and therefore enable this Commentary to cover its traditional wide range again. Frank Elson is now out of hospital and has been seen training at the Duke of York's. We are all most happy to see Frank making such a recovery, and we hope it will continue. Charles Smart, writing from Germany, tells of some fast running, including a win he accomplished in a half-an-hour's race. He missed the six mile mark by a mere 220 yards or so, and that on a wet, gusty day! Bert Ellsey, who has recently joined us, is one of the old school of cross-country runners, having graduated with the now defunct Boro Poly A.C. and Ashcombe St. Georges. He was always a good team man and should be a useful addition to our list of officials. He is a vice-president of the English Cross-Country Union, is past-president of the Southern Counties C.C.A., vice-president and vice-chairman of the Surrey County A.A.A., president of the South of Thames C.C.A. and has a seat on the Southern Committee of the A.A.A. Harry Shields has been re-elected to the committee of the Southern Counties C.C.A. Harry will, no doubt, raise a shout for us here! Joe Coleman, Charles Churcher and Harry Rouse have been elected to the Southern Committee of the R.W.A. Our hon. secretary, Alf Harley, is organising the Olympic Road Walk. Besides this, Alf is hon. treasurer of the R.W.A., vice-president of the Southern Committee of the R.W.A. and R.W.A. delegate to the A.A.A. Alf Taylor has come through an operation and is now running again. One of our best runners of the past, it is good to see Alf out again. Dick Towndrow has now joined us as a first claim member. Our Social Hon. Secretary sends these dates for Belgrave Socials at Belgrave Hall; 15th November, 13th December, Special Xmas Party 27th December, 24th January, 1948.
