items.label: No. 106
items.sum: The new co-editors thank retiring editor Harry Parker, now President of the E.C.C.U., and promise improvements including a suggestion page.
items.s: Editorial The new co-editors thank retiring editor Harry Parker, now President of the E.C.C.U., and promise improvements including a suggestion page. Dear Fellow Belgravians, We humbly present to you the Belgravian issue for November, 1949. In doing so we first of all give thanks to your past Editor, Harry Parker. Many onerous duties have come Harry's way during his career with Belgrave, extending over many years and all he has tackled with great enthusiasm and with remarkable achievements. He is not the kind of person to relinquish his commitments without very good reason, but now he finds his official duties in the service of athletics at least one too many, and he has been obliged with very great regret to hand the editorship over to new co-editors. As we all know Harry has certainly plenty on his plate and always has had and now that he is President of the E.C.C.U., he finds it hard to carry on as Editor. In congratulating him on his great honour, we also thank him for his great work to the club. As for ourselves, your new co-editors, we follow in the wake of Harry Hare, Ben Knifton, Alf Harley, Gordon Doubleday, Freddie Bradnum and Harry Parker. We are fully conscious of the great work and standards built up and maintained by our predecessors and we assure you of our best endeavours to keep up this standard. We have several ideas for the possible improvement of our magazine which we hope you will all approve but, as with this issue we are endeavouring to bring all reports up-to-date, pressure of space prevents us introducing new ideas on this occasion. We do intend, however, to issue another Belgravian at a very early date and to include these ideas, chief among which will be a "Suggestion page," and we ask those of you who have any suggestions, to let us have them in as brief a letter as possible, but let us get this issue among you first and we hope you will find the next one and subsequent issues interesting, entertaining and topical. Best wishes, Your EDITORS. Harry Parker Harry Parker retiring Editor of The Belgravian; President of the E.C.C.U. Harry Hare Harry Hare past editor Ben Knifton Ben Knifton past editor Alf Harley Alf Harley past editor Gordon Doubleday Gordon Doubleday past editor Freddie Bradnum Freddie Bradnum past editor E.C.C.U.

items.label: No. 106
items.sum: Report of the club's 1949 Annual General Meeting, at which Bill Webb was re-elected President and officers' reports were heard.
items.s: Annual General Meeting—October 8th, 1949 Report of the club's 1949 Annual General Meeting, at which Bill Webb was re-elected President and officers' reports were heard. The attendance at this meeting was not as large as was hoped nor as large as we have the right to expect. However, a very representative gathering of somewhere about 80-90 members assembled to elect your new officials and committee and to define the club policy for the year 1949-50. Once again our popular President, Bill Webb, was elected to the premier office of the club and this was received with unanimous acclamation. Secretary Alf Harley's report struck a very optimistic note in spite of one or two reverses during the past season. In reading his report we had a moment or two of thought for the passing of three of our club members: dear old Charlie Cook, Tom Sullivan and Rowland Rowbottom, which we all regret. The Hon. Treasurer's report showed us that although we were spending much more money than we received in ordinary receipts and subscriptions, we were able to balance our club budget through the efforts of the Supporters' Club. The Building Fund is in an extremely healthy state and a word of appreciation was given to Les Cohen and his supporters. Our Treasurer, Syd King, has done a wonderful job in carrying on after that great treasurer, Bill Webb. We all thank him for his work and congratulate him on his achievements. We were sorry and considerably concerned, however, when he warned us that this would be his last year of office. Under the capable chairmanship of Bill Webb the meeting progressed. Your officers and committee were duly elected and during the ensuing phase under the heading of "Other Business," the future policy of the club was discussed in a most rational and democratic manner. One left the meeting convinced that the management of the club was again in most capable hands and with a feeling of confidence for the season 1949-50. items.label: No. 106
items.sum: Stage-by-stage account of Belgrave's win in the Brighton road relay of April 1949, the club's sixth win in the race.
items.s: The "Brighton" Relay held April 2nd, 1949 Stage-by-stage account of Belgrave's win in the Brighton road relay of April 1949, the club's sixth win in the race. RUNNING NOTES Starting from Mitcham, our runner on the first stage to Purley was Derrick Burfitt. He did well to finish 5th in 30 mins. 6 secs. On the next stage to Merstham, Ted Stimpson held his place and his time was 27.25. Then Frank Abberton tackled the up-hill stage through Redhill and ran a fine race to take us up into 2nd place with a time of 23.9. On the next stage, Jack Brown took us in front and running well clocked 28.7. Len Herbert went off on the 5th stage which had been slightly altered. Jimmy Wood, our Poly. member, caught and passed him but Len managed to hang on to second place with a time of 25.29 and handed over to Albert Frost who did well in putting up the fastest time for that leg which is now only just over 2 miles and his time of 10.51 kept us in second place. Vern Blowfield went off on the long stage to Handcross and soon passed his man to put us in the lead once again. His time was 31.25. Len Marchant was our next but he lost the lead to Green of Reading and clocked 21.40 for his stage. Eddie Short went off on the up-hill climb to Patcham. He passed the leader and in clocking 21.34 did the second fastest time and gave us a lead of 11 secs. over our nearest rivals. Bull Lucas, running the last stage, as usual, did not give his opponents any chance of getting on his shoulder and although Green of Birchfield took his team into second place, Bill finished an easy winner and moreover did second fastest time of 17.49 for his leg. The order for finishing was 1, Belgrave, 3 hrs. 57 mins. 35 secs; 2, Birchfield, 3.57.52; 3, Tipton H., 3.58.35. This makes our 6th win in this classic road race, a feat which no other club has performed and moreover, is our second series of three wins in a row as we won in 1934-5-6 and then again in 1947-8-9. items.sum: Track match at Tooting in which South London Harriers narrowly beat Belgrave in both senior and junior contests, with club handicap results.
items.s: Match v. South London H.—May 7th Track match at Tooting in which South London Harriers narrowly beat Belgrave in both senior and junior contests, with club handicap results. Held at Tooting, this was our opening fixture of the summer season and we had senior and junior events with a few club handicaps on the programme. The senior match was a very close affair and our visitors won by the very narrow margin of 2 points. They also won the junior match by 5 points. Mike Broadbent finished second to Grieve in the 100 yards. John Cope was second to Pugh in the 440 and we had first two home in the 880 in Len Marchant and Jack Brown. Bill Lucas won the mile and Eddie Short won the two miles, beating Ted Stimpson. George Powell's win in the javelin, was our only success in the field events side and we also won the medley relay. In the junior match our only winner on the track was Alan Sexton in the 220 yards, but a new member in H. R. Delger, won the javelin and we also won the 4 x 110 yards' relay. Final scores were: Senior.—S.L.H., 63 points; Bels., 61 points. Junior.—S.L.H., 25 points; Bels., 20 points. Handicap events:.— 100 yards: 1, A. Law (11); 2, D. Clements (11); 3, P. Morrison (7½). In the mile handicap a good crowd turned out and after Jack Brown looked like running through the field, he was held off on the final lap by Alf Orton who used his head as well as his legs. Placings: 1, A. H. Orton (135); 2, J. Brown (50); 3, L. Adams (110). Time: 4 mins. 17.8 secs. The two miles' walk was a scratch race with a handicap in conjunction and the eventual winner was our old friend Charlie Speechley with S. James second and P. Wilson, third. items.h: Match v. Ealing Harriers and Walton A.C.—May 14th
items.sum: Gordon Stewart Trophy match at Drayton Green won by Walton A.C., with Belgrave second and Ealing third.
items.s: Match v. Ealing Harriers and Walton A.C.—May 14th Gordon Stewart Trophy match at Drayton Green won by Walton A.C., with Belgrave second and Ealing third. Once again we visited the Drayton Green Track for the inter club contest for the "Gordon Stewart" Trophy, promoted by the local club. We congratulate Walton on their win, but as they had two Olympic men in their team we were not disgraced. Once again the two short sprints proved our undoing and we had to run Alan Sexton in the 100 yards in order to put up a show. Bill Lucas won the mile with A. Bedford second and Derek Burfitt gave Nankeville a good run in the half mile. In the two miles team race we had the first three home, with Jack Brown, Vern Blowfield and Len Marchant finishing in line. We lost the Medley Relay where John Cope tried hard to hold Nankeville over the first 880 but the Walton man gave his team the lead which they maintained to the end. Final scores were: 1st, Walton A.C., 34 points; 2nd, Belgrave H., 29 points; Ealing H., 11 points. Also on the programme were a few junior events and Walton again proved successful in these by scoring 27 points to our 18 and Ealing's 10. George Stace ran well in the mile, and Brian Rice ran second in the half mile. Dave Marshall won the 220 yards in fine style in 23.8. items.s: Match v. Walton A.C. and Thames Valley H.—May 21st Triangular track match at Stompond Lane in which Belgrave and Walton A.C. tied on 56 points with T.V.H. third. On May 21st we visited Stompond Lane for a triangular match. Here again a few junior events were included in the programme, also a 120 yards hurdles event and the home club scored in these events. They also did well in the short sprints with Lewis scoring a double and our only placed man in these events was Les Christmas, third in the 220. R. C. Sharp, running in the 440 yards, gained third place. Len Marchant put up a new ground record in the 880 yards when he beat Alec Olney in 1 min. 58 secs. Olney, however, won the mile with A. Bedford fourth and in the 2 miles Reg. Ruddick beat off the challenge of L. Field of T.V.H. to win in 9 mins. 56 secs. Our Latvian member, A. Bergvalds, was second in the shot and then won the discus throw and should prove a great help to this branch of the club. N. Gibson was second in the high jump and evergreen George Powell was second in the javelin event. We gained third place in the 4 x 110 yards relay and the final scores were: Belgrave and Walton A.C. 56 points each, T.V.H. 49, a very closely contested match and much enjoyed by all, including our supporters who turned up in good numbers. items.s: Junior Match at Croydon Return junior match against Whitgift Middle School on 30 May, won by the school 52 points to 20, several of whose placers were Belgrave members. The return match against the Whitgift Middle School was held on May 30th and a good crowd of our youngsters made the trip. Our only winner of the evening was John Morrison in the 440 yards. Wolton was second in the 880 and Hazel second in the mile. Sexton and Marshall running for their school, again completed a double for the first two places in the 100 and 220 yards and the school also won both the relay races. Cooper and Stinton who were first and second for the school in the high jump are also members of our club and so it can be seen that although we lost the match, our club members were well to the fore. items.s: Surrey County Championships Belgrave members' placings at the Surrey County senior and junior championships, including county records for Alan Sexton, John Grey and Len Herbert. The Senior and Junior Championships, with one or two exceptions were held at Motspur Park on June 4th when the club did quite well and the result of the club's coaching methods was clearly seen. Alan Sexton performed a double in winning the 100 and 220 yards and in the latter event he set up a new county record of 22.7 secs. Another club member set up a new county record when John Grey, in the Junior Discus, recorded a throw of 137 ft. 3 ins. The 3 miles championship was held at Tooting on July 6th and Len Herbert set up a new county record in the fast time of 14 mins. 38.6 secs. Bill Lucas unfortunately had to retire with leg trouble, otherwise we may have had the first two home. We are glad to see Len Herbert getting back to form as he had a disappointing season over the country and we hope that he will keep it up and lead our lads in their effort to regain our lost title of National Champions. This meeting held at the News of the World Sports ground, comprising both senior and junior matches, resulted in a win for the seniors by 49 points to 34, but the juniors lost their match by 1 point—12 to 11. Mike Broadbent and Gordon Lowers were first two home in the 100 yards, while Jim Beaumont and Heathfield were second and third in the 440. John Cope won the 880 yards with Archie Bedford third and Len Marchant won the mile with Len Adams third. We won the senior 4 x 100 yards relay and in the field events, Charlie Jones won the long jump and John MacKenzie the discus throw. In the junior match of three events we won the 4 x 100 yards relay, but Mitcham won the 100 and 880 yards. items.sum: Belgrave's B team beat Ace and Tab A.C. at Croydon on 13 June by 40½ points to 35½.
items.s: Match v. Ace and Tab A.C. Belgrave's B team beat Ace and Tab A.C. at Croydon on 13 June by 40½ points to 35½. Held at Croydon on June 13th when our "B" team won a very enjoyable match by 40½ points to 35½. Archie Bedford won the 880 yards and also did this same distance in the medley relay to give us a winning lead in this event. Len Adams won the mile, beating Eddie Short and Steve Charlton. Jim Heathfield was second in the 440 and Terry Bateman won the high jump. Tea and sandwiches were provided afterwards by our hosts, prominent among whom were our old friends Syd Jarlett and Bill Speaight.. items.s: A.A.A. Championships at White City—July 16th Belgravians' performances at the 1949 A.A.A. Championships, including Harry Churcher's 7 miles walk win and Charlie Smart's standard medal. On Friday evening Michael Broadbent competed in Heat 1 of the 100 yards and was beaten by Mac Bailey in the fast time of 9.9 secs. He qualified to run in the second round on Saturday afternoon but was 5th in a 10.2 secs. heat! Geoff Jarvis won his heat in the 440 yards hurdles in 56.9 secs, and was third in the final won in 56.7 secs. In the 880 yards John Cope was fifth in his heat. In the mile, Derrick Burfitt won his heat in 4.20, but in the final was seventh in 4 min. 19 secs. Marchant and John Brown also competed. Charlie Smart made a gallant effort in the 6 miles on Friday evning and eventually finished fifth in 30 min. 42 secs., thus gaining a standard medal. Ruddock and Towndrow also ran. Harry Churcher won the 7 miles walk in 52 min.41 secs. on the Saturday morning after a deluge of rain which left the track waterlogged. Len Herbert was sixth in the 3 miles in 14 min. 37 secs. Both Smart and Ruddock had another "bash" but after their gruelling 6 miles on Friday only Smart gained a standard. The 2 miles walk was held at Birmingham on July 29th and Harry Churcher was beaten 10 yards by the Swede, Borgesson. items.h: Match v. Cambridge H. and Dartford H.—July 27th
items.sum: Report of the match at Charlton Park lost narrowly to Cambridge Harriers, with the junior match also lost to Cambridge.
items.s: Match v. Cambridge H. and Dartford H.—July 27th Report of the match at Charlton Park lost narrowly to Cambridge Harriers, with the junior match also lost to Cambridge. This was held at Charlton Park and after a very close tussle with the home club, they won by the narrow margin of 2 points. Basil Walden was second in the 100 yards and Lionel Grimshaw won the 220. Jim Heathfield was third in the 440, John Cope won the 880 in 2 mins. 1.6 secs., while Bill Lucas won the mile in 4 mins. 30.2 secs. Charlie Smart, home on leave from Germany, turned out in the 2 miles and clocked 9 mins. 45 secs. to win a good race with Ted Stimpson second. We won the medley relay, but Cambridge gained first places in all three field events and this finally decided the match in their favour. items.s: Final Club Track Meeting—September 17th Report of Belgrave's final handicap meeting of the season at Tooting Bec on 17 September. The final handicap meeting of the season was held at Tooting Bec on Saturday, September 17th, and although the entry for the 3 miles run was up to standard, the other events on the programme were not too well supported. The final of the 100 yards was a good race and Clements just beat Kemp with Mitchell third. The 880 yards saw Ken Cuff beat A. Tapley by about one foot with J. S. Tranter third. The mile race for unattached novices only attracted four entries and P. W. Adams, a younger brother of our own runner, displayed promising form in winning this event. In the 2 miles walk, Harry Churcher walked in fine style and eventually finished second to Joe Scamell, with George Oliver third. In the 300 yards, Alan Sexton was on scratch mark and duly qualified for the final by winning his heat. The final saw the field well away but Alan went after them and on coming into the straight came through strongly to win a great race in 32.3 secs. R. Holtum, a new member was second with Johnny Morrison third. The 3 miles run was the main event on the programme with Jack Brown, the back marker off 60 yards and the limit man on 500. C. Walker who won our novice road race last winter, was off 120 yards and running strongly he eventually took the lead followed by Len Marchant and they finished in that order with Rene Howell, our Poly. member, third off 160 yards. Eddie Short lost a shoe but pluckily kept going and Archie Bedford came through to finish a good fourth. Jack Shields and Ken England were also well up and a new member in J. H. Braggington also did well in his first club race. W. Hadley scored a good handicap double by winning the javelin and long jump events and in the former George Powell was second with A. Machell third. Alan Law was second in the long jump with Frank Simmons third. items.label: No. 106
items.sum: Terry Bateman's review of Belgrave's 1949 field events season, highlighting Geoff Jarvis, John Grey, Bergvalds and Peter Lowe.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS REVIEW Terry Bateman's review of Belgrave's 1949 field events season, highlighting Geoff Jarvis, John Grey, Bergvalds and Peter Lowe. Although the year has brought a slight improvement in the standard of field events it has been due to outstanding individual efforts rather than to improved general performances. However, our juniors show great promise and we must see they are given every encouragement. One of the outstanding and commendable performances of the season was the 440 yards hurdles run by Geoff Jarvis in 56.7 secs. which gave him third place in the A.A.A. Championships. This was followed by another good performance in his winning the R.A.F. Championship and in being chosen as reserve for England v. France match for the same event. Previously Geoff had concentrated on the high hurdles and the change to 440 yards has obviously been most successful. Another outstanding performance was that of John Grey's discus throw of 137 ft. 3 ins. which won him the Surrey County Junior Championship and broke the existing record by about 18 ft. He also gained a standard medal in the A.A.A. Junior Championships. Our weakest events have been the high and long jumps. Conditions were not improved when mid-way through the season we lost the services of Steve Gibson, one of our most promising high jumpers who went into hospital for an operation on an old war wound. We take this opportunity of wishing him a speedy recovery and hope to see him out at the winter training sessions John Sinton a junior who has given good support to our senior matches is to be congratulated on his 5 ft. 6 ins. jump in the Police match at Imber Court. Both the juniors, Bob Cooper and Jim Purdy, have been jumping well and show promise. We were not too successful in either the Svard or Kinnaird meetings. One of the best performances was that of Harry Delger at the Kinnaird meeting when he threw the junior javelin about 154 feet to gain third place. Bergvalds was the outstanding performer in the club championships. He won the discus and shot, and was third in the javelin. His discus throw of 123 ft. 8½ ins. set up a new club record. Peter Lowe established a new club record in the hop, step and jump, with an effort of 41 ft. 5 ins. Charlie Melchoir retained his javelin title with Les Higgins as runner-up. Our old stalwart, George Powell, has been consistently throwing the javelin over 140 ft. in matches and has been a source of inspiration to younger aspirants. It is intended to resume the field events training periods through the winter months at Tooting on alternate Saturday afternoons. items.s: JUNIOR NOTES F. Simmons's letter to the juniors reviewing their county and Southern successes and announcing winter P.T. and Sunday strolls; it gives J. Grey's county record discus as 137 ft. 8 ins., where the field events review on page 14 prints 137 ft. 3 ins. Dear Juniors, The summer season is now finished and it is with pleasure that I say thank you for your support in both matches and in championships. We had a successful season ending in successes in County and Southern County Championships. Our successes in the County Championship were: A. Sexton, 100 yards in 10.5 secs.; Equals County record. 220 yards in 22.7; New County record. D. Marshall, 100 yards, third; 220 yards, second. Picton, 220 yards. County standard. J. Grey, Discus, 1st. New County record; 137 ft. 8 ins. Southern Counties: A. Sexton, 220 yards, 1st, 23 secs. We had three in the final of the 220 yards and John Morrison gained his Southern standard in the 440 yards. In addition we won the Southern Counties 4 x 110 yards relay. Our congratulations to Desmond Mullen on winning the Irish Junior 100 yards and his second in the 220. Some of you did not do as well as you hoped, but keep trying and success will come and when it does it will be all the sweeter. Some of our junior pals will be leaving our section to go forward to the seniors and our best wishes for continued success goes with them. To all new recruits to our section we give a “ Belgrave ” welcome and assure you all of a healthy and happy time. To our cross-country juniors, we wish you every success in the coming months. It is hoped, all juniors who can possibly attend, will come along to our winter P.T. class at Belgrave Hall. Details will be available later, also Charlie Jones and I are arranging all day strolls from November until April every Sunday, which we hope you will all make an effort to come along to. They are very good for you, in fact, the senior successes were built up on their strolling and I see no reason why you cannot do the same. The strolls will be worked out so that the cost will suit everybody's pocket. I thoroughly understand that some of you have home studies, but when you can make it, come along, you can be sure of a welcome and a good time too. In conclusion, on behalf of the juniors, I convey their congratulations to Harry Churcher on his winning the A.A.A. 7 miles' walk again and also on his new world's record. F. SIMMONS. F. Simmons F. e: Belgrave Harriers Club 20 Miles' Walk Championship
items.s: WALKING NOTES Review of Belgrave's 1949 race walking season: Met. W.C. 15, Chichester–Portsmouth, club and national championships, Harry Churcher's records and titles, and the London to Brighton walk. Looking back over the season which has just finished, we certainly have not disgraced ourselves. Our wins in Open Races in the South have been up to our usual standard and we have been placed in two of the Senior National Championships. That we can do better there is no doubt, especially do we need some more young members and it is hoped that the coming season will see an improvement in this direction. Continuing our activities, following the National 10, three teams were entered for the Met. W.C. 15 miles at Regent's Park, but alas, before any great distance had been covered, Charlie Churcher was ruled out and our chances of success thereby greatly reduced. This race seems to be very unfortunate for us, as like last year, we suffered more than the usual disqualifications. These included Pat Sapcote and Jack Baker. The unusual distance of the race got the team selectors guessing with the result that two of our “ B ” team men finished before the second “ A ” team man. Outstanding was Bob Readman who held the lead throughout the greater part of the race, but on the last lap he tired rather badly and dropped back to third place. With a team score of 64 points we were very surprised to find that we gained third place. In the Chichester to Portsmouth race on Easter Saturday, Charlie Churcher repeated his brilliant performance of last year by winning the individual honour. As we did not send a very strong team, it was not surprising that we were unable to get better than third place, 9 points behind the winners, Woodford Green. The following Saturday we held our own Club 20 Miles' Championship. As usual, being the first 20 of the season, a number of the starters failed to finish the course, but the 14 who completed the distance walked exceptionally well. Veteran Jack Bidgood, after 20 years with the club, succeeded in winning his first Championship after a well-judged race, followed by Pat Sapcote and Charlie Churcher. And so we came to the National 20 and from the performances of our walkers in the Club 20 it seemed that we had a reasonable chance of success. Unfortunately Bert Webb was unable to make the journey to Manchester and we were without any knowledge of the capabilities of the Sheffield boys over the longer distance. The weather, for Manchester, was extremely good, in fact, no rain fell throughout the day. At the start the two Sheffield lads, Allen and Proctor, made a quick getaway and joined by Lloyd Johnson, set up a good pace. Lloyd however, did not last with them for long and soon began to drop back. Most of our lads walked extremely well and were ably assisted by Harry Churcher, Syd Roberts and Percy Wilson, but despite all their efforts, they were unable to do better than second place, with Charlie Churcher taking third individual honour. Competition for the Nijmegen Shield was very keen. Sheffield being successful, with Woodford Green second and ourselves third. In a new promotion this year, the Watford 25, we entered a small team and succeeded in gaining third place in both the scratch and handicap sections. The last National Championship of the season, the 50 Kilos. was held from the Police Sports Club at Chigwell over a very stiff course. The weather, which was very warm, added to the trials of the walkers and of 73 starters, no less than 31 retired without completing the full distance. These included Charlie Churcher, who developed leg trouble, Pat Sapcote, Fred Herring, Jack Wakeley and Don Heath, so that by the end of the race we had just a bare four left, who finished in fourth position, 2 points behind Woodford. For the Eastleigh A.C. 50 Kilos. on July 16th, Pat Sapcote was unable to make the journey at the last minute, thus depriving us of one of our best men. However, Bert Clayton sprung a great surprise by leading all the way through and eventually winning the individual race, and although the rest of the team walked exceedingly well, they had to be content with second place to Surrey W.C. Jack Bidgood also won a style prize, and Bert Clayton was second in the handicap. On August 23rd we were invited to field a team in Surrey W.C.'s 6 miles road race at Tooting Bec Common. Despite the fact that the fixture did not appear on our summer programme, 12 of our walkers turned out and after a very interesting race, Surrey just managed to win by 103 points to 107. So much for the road walks. On the track Harry Churcher, as is now well known, succeeded in lowering his world's record time of last year for the 5 miles. Walking in excellent style, Harry lapped the track time after time in almost identical times, eventually clipping 10.4 secs. off his time at Motspur Park. In addition to this he succeeded in taking the Surrey County 2 miles' title, the Southern Counties 2 miles title, and on a water-logged track at the White City, the 7 miles A.A.A. title. A fortnight later Harry took second place to Borgesson in the A.A.A. 2 miles but revenged his defeat in the London-Gothenburg Match a week later by winning the 7 miles at the White City in 51.2.2, his fastest time for the distance. This race prevented him from defending his Club 2 miles title and in his absence Bob McMullen, walking in very fine style, became this year's club champion. On June 22nd we had our annual mob match with Surrey W.C. on the track at Tooting, beating them by 89 points to 121, with Joe Scamell (jr.), Brian Shepherd and Mac taking the handicap awards in that order. A “ B ” team match against the Veterans A.C. at Tooting Bec on July 9th also resulted in a win for us. Our Annual Inter Club Walks of 1, 2, 3 and 4 miles proved a great success this year, no fewer than 66 walkers competing. The competition proved to be very keen, eventually resulting in a win for Woodford Green with Highgate Harriers second and us third. A number of our walkers have figured well in Open Handicaps and Veterans' Events, successes being scored by Bert East, Syd James, Charlie Speechley and young Joe Scamell. As usual our Police members figured well in the Barking to Southend Walk. Jack Bidgood was once again second with Bob Readman, Pat Sapcote and Bert Webb following him home in that order. The winning team, “ B ” Division, was completely Belgrave. On August 27th we had a 25 miles match with London Vidarians and Surrey Walking Club. This race next year is to be an Open Event and should prove a good training walk for the Brighton. The race resulted in a win for Surrey W.C. with us second. In the London to Brighton Walk on September 10th, eleven of our walkers started off on the stroke of Big Ben at seven o'clock, to be joined later by a number of supporters. In the early stages, Jack Bidgood, Bert Clayton, Jack Baker, Jack Wakeley and George Oliver, walked in a group with Don Heath and Joe Wilson not far away. Gordon Doubleday, F. Herring, Sid Spencer and Bill Urry, followed at an easier pace. Jack Bidgood eventually went away from the others and at the Chequers Horley was in ninth position. A check at Crawley (29¾ miles) showed that our men had held their positions with the exception of Jack Wakeley who had stopped for a massage. By the time Bolney was reached, Jack Bidgood had improved his position to seventh, Clayton was 16th, Baker 21st and Wilson 27th. With the retirement of Bert Martineau from the Surrey team there seemed a chance that our team would be placed and although Jack Bidgood dropped a couple of places to go back to ninth Joe Wilson moved up to 23rd and at the finish our positions were: Jack Bidgood, ninth; Bert Clayton, 16th; Joe Wilson, 21st; Jack Baker, 23rd, making a score of 62 points and just losing us the third position. So Jack Bidgood became our long-distance champion as well as holder of the 20 Miles Championship. He's a champion to be proud of. His judgment of pace and unflagging stamina throughout the race set a fine example. Bert Clayton was a worthy second and showed his grit in overcoming tiredness in the last few miles. Joe Wilson walked his best Brighton to date and came along in fine style in the latter half to finish remarkably fresh. Jack Baker pluckily stuck it out over the last half to complete the team. items.label: No. 106
items.sum: Note urging Belgravians to thank wives and sweethearts by bringing them to the club's social events on 19 November and 10 December.
items.s: THE LIGHTER SIDE—SOCIAL ACTIVITIES Note urging Belgravians to thank wives and sweethearts by bringing them to the club's social events on 19 November and 10 December. The Social Hon. Secretary, Dave Martin Shepherd, has asked for more space for social activities. We shall certainly give him all we can for the social side is just as important as any other part of the club. In promoting these social events we are really showing our appreciation to the wives and sweethearts of Belgravians who without support and encouragement from their dear ones would never achieve the great performances they do. Do you stop to think what you owe to them. Who washes your running clothes each week? Who looks after the diet prescribed either by yourselves or well-meaning advisers? Who sits and listens over and over again to stories of walking, running and field events until they could scream? Who sits alone night after night waiting for committee men to return, having resignedly relinquished many hours of their domestic life to officialdom of Belgrave? Aye, give them a little in return, and we can assure you that nothing pleases them more than to join in our social activities at the club to whom they undeniably give so much. So make a note of the following dates and come along. Saturday, November 19th. Saturday, December 10th. Dave Martin Shepherd Dave Martin Shepherd Social Hon. Secretary

items.label: No. 106
items.sum: Report of the club's Annual Dinner and Dance at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction, on 15 October, where Len Herbert's Sir Harry Barclay Cup award was announced.
items.s: ANNUAL DINNER AND DANCE Report of the club's Annual Dinner and Dance at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction, on 15 October, where Len Herbert's Sir Harry Barclay Cup award was announced. The Annual Dinner and Dance which was held at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction, on Saturday, October 15th. was again a huge success and the hall was filled to capacity. Despite the extensive enquiries of the Social Hon. Secretary, it was not possible to find a suitable hall which would hold a larger number of club members and it was with much regret that we were obliged to turn down applications for tickets. Bill Webb once again presided over the gathering and received a great ovation. The theme of Bill's few words in proposing “ The Club,” was the “ Belgrave Spirit,” and in replying to the toast, Secretary Alf Harley gave us some interesting data on the very early days of the club when handicap meetings were held on mid-week nights on the Embankment, lasting as late as eleven o'clock. During the course of the evening it was announced that Len Herbert had been awarded the Sir Harry Barclay Cup by the Surrey County A.A. for the best performance of 1949. The dance which followed dinner was very ably conducted by Bert Ellsey and our thanks are due to “ Dave ” for a very splendid evening. items.sum: Short items of news about Belgrave members at home and abroad, including appointments of R.W.A. judges and sympathy for Highgate walker R. Dick.
items.s: NEWS FROM MEMBERS Short items of news about Belgrave members at home and abroad, including appointments of R.W.A. judges and sympathy for Highgate walker R. Dick. Tony Whincup writes to say that having got over his exam. he is getting down to training. Tony Davis is soldiering at Horsham but says there's not much doing in the way of athletics. Jimmy Coates, one of our young walkers, who has recently emigrated to Canada, writes to say he is very impressed by the Canadian juniors but says there's a shortage of cinder tracks. Frank Thompson was a very welcome visitor at the A.G.M. He tells us that our old friend, Fred Rickards, who married again last year, has started another family and has a daughter. Good luck Fred, when are we going to see you again. Tommy Green is reported to be “ retiring ” from business and getting down to walking again. What about next year's National, Tommy? B. Lulham has passed his Coach's exam. for sprints and relays, and is now a A.A.A. Hon. Coach. Colin Sutton, settling down in Australia, is already winning races and is the district champion for 4½ miles. Stan Manning, who was ill last year, is now recovering and hopes to get to Wimbledon during the winter. Jack Rutland informs us that he will soon be out training again with an eye to long distance. Jack already holds an important executive post and he is now studying for further promotion. We all wish him luck. Syd Roberts and Frank Elson have been appointed R.W.A. judges. We have just learnt with regret of the serious accident which befel R. Dick, the popular and leading Highgate Harrier walker. We wish to express the club's sympathy with Mr. R. Dick and wish him a speedy and successful recovery. Tony Whincup Tony Whincup getting down to training after his exam. items.label: April 1940
items.sum: The secretary reviews the first wartime season: racing kept going, club quarters lent to other bodies, members serving in the Forces or recently married, social fixtures, the Southern Counties substitute team race win, and plans for track racing at Tooting Bec.
e: Southern Counties C.C. Association substitute team race
items.s: Hon. Secretary's Commentary. The secretary reviews the first wartime season: racing kept going, club quarters lent to other bodies, members serving in the Forces or recently married, social fixtures, the Southern Counties substitute team race win, and plans for track racing at Tooting Bec. This Athletic Season has been unlike any other within recollection. In September last it seemed impossible that we should enjoy much of a season. After the few first anxious weeks, however, we began to piece together a racing programme until, as we write, it seems as though there is some racing of importance every week. This is very gratifying, and it is very pleasing to think that most Associations and Clubs have succeeded in adapting themselves to difficult circumstances. Of necessity, late decisions have been made and last-minute difficulties surmounted, but it is pleasing to think that every week has found large numbers of our men busy athletically. Unfortunately it has not been possible to publish our Gazette earlier, and we are still compelled to restrict the size of "The Belgravian." Once again we would ask for the co-operation of all members, and particularly do we wish to hear from all members now serving with H.M. Forces. * * * * * Our last issue informed our members of our intention to carry on with the provision of training facilities and racing, as far as circumstances permitted. This issue shows that we have succeeded, and that our efforts have reaped a rich reward. It was decided early on that no Club Championships should be held, in fairness to those who would be unable to train and compete, but that substitute races and inter-club events should be held. Our Twentieth Annual Open Walk was promoted on the last Saturday in November, and succeeded in showing that a keen desire existed for competition. It is pleasing to note that, following our lead, several other similar events have now been held, and there are others to follow. Additionally, our quarters have become a focal point of Athletics in the South. Athletes of other Clubs have been invited to come along, and the Surrey County A.A.A., Printing and Allied Trades C.C. Association, South of the Thames C.C.A., Southern Committee of the R.W.A., Southern Counties C.C.A., and "News of the World" S.C., have all been granted the use of our quarters for their promotions. Needless to say, we have been only too glad to help in any way the continuance of Athletics, and to assist in keeping our sports of cross-country running and road-walking alive, and in a healthy and vigorous state. We are proud to have made our contribution towards this Season's sport in such difficult times, and trust it will not be long before a normal Season's programme will once again engage our attention. * * * * * Meanwhile, many familiar faces are missing from our Wimbledon meetings. Some are serving in the Forces; others are compelled to carry on their normal work miles away from London. Among those we know to be serving in H.M. Forces are: A. Allum, W. H. Appleby, J. T. Beer, F. Bellchambers, A. A. Bird, A. S. Blunden, F. S. Bradnum, L. J. E. Bailey, L. J. Coleman, H. G. Clayton, C. Dennis, J. E. Flower, J. Ginty, W. E. Ives, C. H. Lloyd, A. Patience, D. Patience, R. Patience, L. Penny, K. Penney, R. V. Reynolds, J. E. Rutland, E. Saunders, F. J. Skelley, W. Timberlake, J. H. Thomas, J. Tosh, E. J. Watts, D. Winton and P. G. Wright. J. A. Bellchambers and J. R. Shotter are training in Officer-Cadet units, whilst V. Berlemont is serving in the French Army. We wish the best of luck to all our members, and trust we may have frequent good news from them. Before long they will be joined by other members, and we wish them all a safe, quick return to normal Club activities. * * * * * The early days of the War brought strange irksome restrictions, many of which have since been relaxed. Despite all difficulties, we have managed to carry through a very full programme of Social fixtures, and our grateful thanks are due to Tom Morrell and the Social sub-committee for all their efforts. We have always believed our social side to be an integral part of our club life, and largely responsible for the club spirit of which we have been justly proud. Hence our desire to carry on despite difficulties. * * * * * Our win in the Southern Counties C.C. Association substitute team race was very pleasing, and we congratulate the team on its excellent running. * * * * * Many members have recently entered into the married state, and we congratulate them and wish them all happiness in the future. They include T. Cotton, G. R. Chantler, F. G. Ford, H. L. Rollins, J. E. Rutland,. E. C. Heather, L. G. Bennett. * * * * * A cheery letter from our Hon. Editor—at present far removed from the Club—asks for his good wishes to be extended to all friends. "Doub" is finding time to train and run over the Devon moors, to serve on the Exeter Harriers Committee, and is part-holder of a Challenge Cup awarded over a series of races. Nice work! * * * * * Heartiest congratulations to our sprightly Hon. Timekeeper, Charlie Cook and Mrs. Cook upon the celebration of their 50th anniversary of marriage. We trust they will enjoy many more years together and that we shall be able to congratulate them upon their Diamond Jubilee in due course. * * * * * We are hopeful of arranging an interesting track programme for the Summer months, and our Track Captain will require the loyal assistance of every track man if we are to succeed in carrying this through with credit to the Club. It is obvious that many of our better-known performers, particularly among the sprinters, will not be available. Some of our members will find themselves running at strange distances, some will be called upon several times during an evening, but we are certain that despite difficulty and inconvenience, we shall find the sporting traditions of the Club maintained, and Athletics still a very live sport, despite the regretted enforced absence of many of our members. * * * * * Battersea Park is not available this season and we have decided to use the Tooting Bec Track for Club training and racing. The following dates have been booked for Club meetings: Wednesday, May 8th; Saturday, May 25th; Wednesday, June 19th; Wednesday, July 10th; Wednesday, July 24th. The Club Junior Championships will be decided, probably on June 19th, and it is hoped to arrange some Club handicaps and inter-club fixtures, which together with "away" fixtures, should form an excellent programme. A fixture list will probably be circulated in due course, and once again it is emphasised that a really good track season can only be enjoyed if every available member co-operates to the full with the Track Captain. * * * * * May we commend to our readers who wish to keep in touch with current athletic matters, "The Amateur Athlete," published by J. Armour Milne from 8 Fraser House, Albion Avenue, S.W.8. This news-letter of Athletics reaches one by post every Wednesday morning and the charge per copy is 3d. Most subscribers find it convenient to send a P.O. for 1/- or so in advance, or our Hon. Secretary will pass on any subscriptions. * * * * * This year our Hon. Secretary is President of the Middlesex Co. A.A.A., and it is hoped that all Middlesex qualified members will support any fixtures the Association may be able to arrange. A. Allum A. e: Surrey County A.A.A. 7 miles C.C. race
items.s: Brief reports of the Surrey County A.A.A. 7 miles race from the Wimbledon quarters on 6 January, where Belgrave dead-heated with Mitcham A.C. in the team race, and the Middlesex event at Ruislip where Cadogan A.C. were second to Polytechnic Harriers. On January 6th the Surrey County A.A.A. promoted a 7 miles C.C. race from our quarters at Wimbledon. Close (S.A.C.) had an easy win and was followed home by two of our stalwarts, Carter and Jerman. The team race resulted in a dead heat between Mitcham A.C. and ourselves, both teams scoring 26 points. Our team was completed by E. H. Herbert (10) and R. E. Stride (11). In the Middlesex event held the same day at Ruislip, Cadogan A.C.—consisting of E. S. Stimpson (4), W. H. Rispin (5), H. W. Shields (13), R. W. Tobin (17)—were second to Polytechnic Harriers. items.label: April 1940
items.h: Match v. Thames Hare and Hounds.
items.sum: Report and result of the home cross-country match against Thames Hare and Hounds on 27 January, in which R. A. Clough beat Tom Carter, Belgrave won 44 pts. to 61 and F. P. King won the handicap; P. R. Smith (T) is printed 18th with a time (42 24) faster than those placed 12th to 17th.
e: Belgrave Harriers v. Thames Hare and Hounds
items.s: Match v. Thames Hare and Hounds. Report and result of the home cross-country match against Thames Hare and Hounds on 27 January, in which R. A. Clough beat Tom Carter, Belgrave won 44 pts. to 61 and F. P. King won the handicap; P. R. Smith (T) is printed 18th with a time (42 24) faster than those placed 12th to 17th. On January 27th we had the pleasure of entertaining that very well-known cross-country club, the Thames Hare and Hounds. They paid us the compliment of bringing along a fairly strong team including L. R. McIntyre, the Southern cross-country champion. Also in their team were R. A. Clough and B. F. Brearley, whom our lads had previously met when running against Cambridge University. The visitors totalled 9 while we had 11, a surprisingly small number for a home fixture, but this was probably due to the bad weather conditions. It was decided to score 7 aside, and as Tom Carter and Wilf Rispin were turning out after illness, we were not too optimistic about the result. A. H. Beaumont led the field along at a good pace round the starting field, but when they came round at the end of the first lap of the country, Dick Tobin was in front of a small bunch which included Clough and McIntyre, of Thames, and Carter and F. P. King. The latter was running very well and put up quite his best performance of the season. When they reached the finishing field, Clough was just in front of Carter with McIntyre lying third. Tom put in all he knew down the straight but Clough was too strong and held him off to win a fine race. In view of Tom's enforced absence during the last few weeks, his present performance was little short of marvellous. When he won the Club's 7 miles race earlier in the season over this course, his time was 39 min. 15 sec., so to do only 30 sec. worse after a lay-off and in much worse weather conditions proves the excellence of his running. Dick Tobin also showed a welcome return to his old-time form and was rewarded by securing second place in the handicap. This was won, very deservedly, by F. P. King, our new member from Epsom, who is better known on the track, being an excellent miler. Third prize was taken by that old war-horse, Harry Shields, who keeps going season after season and still manages to keep well up with his field. I hope Harry will not mind my referring to him as a "veteran," although actually Harry started his running career at an early age and is still quite a "youngster." Those members who did turn out are to be congratulated, as are the Club officials who were present, including Dick Savage, Charlie Jones and our worthy Hon. Treasurer. Our thanks are also due to Tom Morrell and "Tiny" Jarlett, who went out with the flags and made a very good job of pointing the course. RESULTS. Pos. Name. Act. Time. Start. H'cap. Time. e: Southern Counties C.C. Association inter-team race
items.s: Report of the Southern Counties C.C. Association 7½ miles inter-team race from the Blackheath H. quarters at Hayes on 9 March, won individually by M. Bingham of Finchley H., with Belgrave H. winning the team event from 18 teams. MARCH 9TH.—On this day took place the most important race of the season—a 7½ miles inter-team race promoted by the Southern Counties C.C. Association, from the Blackheath H. quarters at Hayes, Kent. M. Bingham, of Finchley H., showed that he is undoubtedly the runner of the season by his easy win, whilst our team showed excellent packing to win the team event. 18 teams closed in. Our winning team consisted of Carter (5), Hewitt (8), Stimpson (9), L. W. Herbert (10). Others to finish were Tobin (20), E. H. Herbert (23), Shields (31), Rispin (33), Jerman, and Mitchell. 1. items.s: Report and result of the last club race of the season, over the usual 5 miles road course, won by Len Herbert with Smart first on handicap; Shields's printed handicap time does not agree with his time and allowance. Our last Club race of the season was on the road over the usual 5 miles course, and some really fine running was seen. Jerman early cut out the pace, but Stimpson and Len Herbert raced away over the last lap of the Common. Herbert's reserve pace gave him a good win, but the form shewn by all our runners inspires confidence in their ability to win the "News of the World" event at the end of the month. items.s: With The Walkers. Walking section notes: the handicap result of the walkers' first winter race over 5 miles on 14 October (won by W. H. Snell, H. G. Churcher fastest), then the club's 20th Annual Open Walk on 25 November, where Harry Churcher won the scratch race, Belgrave's scratch team won the "Berman" Cup outright and W. G. True won the handicap. Our first race of the Winter Season was held on October 14th over the 5 miles course, with the following result :— Our Committee decided to give a lead to the Athletic world by promoting our 20th Annual Open Walk on November 25th. Despite a financial loss, the event must be considered a great success, for not only were 102 entries received, but—more important—our promotion brought together all interested in Walking in the South, and as a result a full programme of racing came into being. Harry Churcher had an easy win in the scratch event, and our scratch team, with a 17 points total for four men, were also easy winners. Incidentally, the "Berman" Cup had been allocated, by kind permission of the R.W.A., to our event, and this win—our third in succession—made the trophy the Club's own property. Bill True (10 min. 30 sec. allowance) won the handicap event, with A. H. Webb (9 min. 30 sec.), now a Belgrave Harrier, second. Our "C" team (comprising Messrs. True, Jones, Snell and Brunning) won the team handicap. Our thanks are due to the generous donors to the Prize Fund, to Mr. W. Allen, who again presented a special prize, to the R.W.A. officials for their invaluable co-operation, and to all the competitors who rallied to our support. Handicap was won by W. G. True (allce. 10-30); second A. H. Webb (9-30); third, R. Andrews (Woodford Green A.C.) (10 min.). The Rest, 405 points; Met. Police W.C., 827 points. 88 competitors finished the course—over a quarter of them Belgrave Harriers. Our own numbers were very gratifying, and the performances, as the results show, excellent. Pos. On December 9th we held a 7 miles Club handicap, and invited other clubs along for an inter-club event. Scoring 10 aside, we defeated the Met. Police W.C. by 60 points to 150 points, and scoring 8 aside we beat Surrey Walking Club by 39 points to 97 points. Our handicap was won by Bill Snell with 8 min. 45 sec. allowance. items.label: April 1940
items.sum: Report and result of the first Southern 10 miles walking Championship from Belgrave's Wimbledon quarters on Easter Saturday, 23 March, won by F. J. Redman, where Belgrave lost the team title narrowly to Surrey Walking Club after Harry Churcher's disqualification.
items.s: Report and result of the first Southern 10 miles walking Championship from Belgrave's Wimbledon quarters on Easter Saturday, 23 March, won by F. J. Redman, where Belgrave lost the team title narrowly to Surrey Walking Club after Harry Churcher's disqualification. Easter Saturday, March 23rd, was the day chosen for the first Southern 10 miles Championship, and the event was held from our quarters at Wimbledon. A good representative entry was obtained and our team were undoubtedly "favourites"—but as "favourites" so often do, we failed narrowly to take the Championship. Up to eight miles it was easily ours, but at this point Harry Churcher suffered disqualification and our lead on points became a deficit. A gallant but unavailing effort by Harry Thaxter over the last mile reduced the margin to two points, but could not displace Surrey Walking Club, whose team rose to the occasion splendidly. How we longed for the help of Jack Rutland, greatly improved this season, who was being married at the time of the race! Heartiest congratulations go to our friends of the Surrey Walking Club on their win. Their walkers excelled themselves, and they had undoubted cause to feel very proud of themselves when the awards were presented. Our team (incidentally, we were the first club to finish a team) was led home by our Captain, followed by Joe Coleman, who did not quite reproduce his usual form in this race. Colin Sutton gave sound support, and Thaxter as already mentioned, did all that could be expected of him. After this our men followed one another in close succession, as the result shows. We entered three teams and all closed in; and again showed the Club's great all-round walking strength. m. s. m. s. 1. F. J. Redman (Met. W.C.) 79 53 24. R. D. McMullen (Bel. "B") 89 32 2. D. items.label: April 1940
items.sum: Summary of the walkers' season: good numbers and many successes despite Service claims, with Harry Churcher and Jack Rutland singled out, new members welcomed and veterans thanked.
items.s: Summary of the walkers' season: good numbers and many successes despite Service claims, with Harry Churcher and Jack Rutland singled out, new members welcomed and veterans thanked. To summarise the season, our walkers can claim to have had a most successful time. Numbers throughout have been good (although Service claims have robbed us of some we should have been glad to have had with us); enthusiasm has been high, and our successes many. Harry Churcher repeatedly led our team home, although he has had an unfortunate spell in the latter part of the season. Jack Rutland is probably our most improved walker of the season. We have welcomed new members in A. C. Beales, A. H. Webb, F. T. Halls, J. Wilson, R. D. McMullen, Junr., all of whom will greatly assist our teams; and we have been glad to see one of our warriors of the past, R. D. McMullen, out again. Our "veterans," T. W. Green, F. Rickards, C. H. Speechley, have all assisted us again, and a glance at the results appearing in this issue will show that most of our walkers have been in action. items.sum: Preview of the inaugural R.W.A. Southern Committee 20 miles Championship from De Bohun's Farm, Enfield West, on 4 May.
items.s: Preview of the inaugural R.W.A. Southern Committee 20 miles Championship from De Bohun's Farm, Enfield West, on 4 May. The big race still before us is the inaugural Southern Committee of the R.W.A. 20 miles Championship, to be held from De Bohun's Farm, Enfield West, on May 4th. We hope we shall have a number of Club members there to cheer our walkers on. Our team are certain to be prominent and we have every hope of winning this Championship, for our representation will be a worthy one. Let's have as many as possible at Enfield West to help our team along! R.W.A. Southern Committee 20 miles Championship De Bohun's Farm, Enfield West Enfield West R.W.A.

Additionally, the Southern Committee of the R.W.A. hope to promote some races during the Summer months. items.label: April 1940
items.sum: Announcement of Belgrave's Hour's Walk at Tooting Bec Track on 25 May, intended to stand in for the A.A.A. 7 miles championship.
items.s: Announcement of Belgrave's Hour's Walk at Tooting Bec Track on 25 May, intended to stand in for the A.A.A. 7 miles championship. Our contribution to the Walking programme is an Hour's Walk to be held at Tooting Bec Track, on Saturday, May 25th. It is hoped that this will go a long way towards taking the place of the normal A.A.A. Championship at 7 miles, and we propose making a small award to all walkers covering seven miles or more within the hour. We expect all the principal walkers in the South to participate, and given good conditions, an excellent race should result, with many talented walkers striving to show that seven miles in an hour is simple; and eight miles in the hour, within their compass. No doubt many Belgrave walkers will be out to show what they can do. Belgrave Harriers Hour's Walk A.A.A. Championships Tooting Bec Track A.A.A.

items.label: April 1940
items.sum: Column looking back ten years to the club's Gazettes: the 1929 Open Walk and Club Junior Walk, H. E. Footer's club cross-country titles and South of the Thames win, the "Murphy" Shield, Belgrave's first placing in the Southern Cross Country Championship of 1930 and an R.W.A. Junior Championship team win.
items.s: Ten Years Ago. Column looking back ten years to the club's Gazettes: the 1929 Open Walk and Club Junior Walk, H. E. Footer's club cross-country titles and South of the Thames win, the "Murphy" Shield, Belgrave's first placing in the Southern Cross Country Championship of 1930 and an R.W.A. Junior Championship team win. Ten Years Ago. Glancing back to our Gazettes of ten years ago, we find much of interest. Our Open Walk of 1929 attracted 205 entrants (23 teams) and was won by A. H. Pope, with Tommy Green second. Our team won the scratch team race and consisted of Green, Fletcher, Scamell and Frank Elson. The Club Junior Walk was won by Elson, with E. Saunders and P. Khlopin following him home. The Club 7 miles Cross-country title was won by H. E. Footer, who also won the handicap with a 10 seconds allowance. Jack Flower and Arthur Allum took the place medals. Footer won the Surrey County Championship and also led our team to an easy win. Our Bert (this was certainly his year) followed this by winning the South of the Thames race and we read that this was a reward for "such magnificent services to our Club in the past seven seasons." Keep going, Bert! The Club 10 miles Championship was also gathered in by Footer, and again he won the sealed handicap, this time from the scratch mark. J. E. Flower, A. Allum, A. Penny, S. H. Warboys and W. G. Webb followed him home in that order. The "Murphy" Shield race held on the same day went to Len Fletcher, who beat Green by inches, with Harold King third. The sealed handicap prizes were won by S. L. King, A. A. Harley and A. L. Fletcher. The Southern Cross Country Championship of 1930, held at Brighton Racecourse, saw Belgrave placed for the first time ever in this event. Warboys (13), Footer (21), Allum (31), Duffett (37), J. E. Flower (38) and Mitchell (49) composed the team, which gained third medals. This was followed by an excellent performance in the "National," when we finished sixth of 37 teams—and Belgrave had "arrived," or were well on the way! The R.W.A. Junior Championship gave Belgrave another win. F. H. Elson (2), E. Saunders (7), J. E. Field (10), S. L. King (14) gave us a total of 33 points, to the 38 points of Enfield A.C. items.label: April 1940
items.sum: Social notes on the winter's Socials and Dances at Belgrave Hall and Zeeta Hall, Charlie Redgrave's concert party, the Boxing Day Party and the closing Carnival Social, with no Dinner-Dance this year, by the Social Hon. Sec. T. F. Morrell.
items.s: The Social Side. Social notes on the winter's Socials and Dances at Belgrave Hall and Zeeta Hall, Charlie Redgrave's concert party, the Boxing Day Party and the closing Carnival Social, with no Dinner-Dance this year, by the Social Hon. Sec. T. F. Morrell. The Social Side. Several Socials and two Dances have been held during the Winter season, and we have been glad to arrange these affairs, which give so much pleasure to our members and friends. We can ill-afford the space these days, or we could really spread ourselves on the happenings in Belgrave Hall, and at Zeeta Hall. We owe a special debt of gratitude to Charlie Redgrave and his friends, a full concert party, who came along on December 9th and delighted us all. The Boxing Day Party went with a swing, although there was room for a few more. Our "knobbly-knee" champion proved to be Charlie Jones; and Footer being used as a broom by two of the "weaker" sex, caused much laughter. The Social season came to an end with the Carnival Social of March 30, which was well-attended. It has been decided not to hold a Dinner-Dance this year, but we hope it will not be long before we can resume these functions. To conclude, the Social Committee are always glad to see and hear from members now serving in the Forces. At odd times, in many odd places, thoughts must come to some of our members of pleasant times enjoyed in the company of other members, of races, and social occasions. Let's hear from you! T. F. items.s: From Our Track Captain. The Track Captain F. R. Webb's message for the coming track season, on Club Championships, training at Tooting Bec Track, whom to ask for advice and giving notice when unable to turn out for matches. From Our Track Captain. Once again we are about to turn our attention to the Running Track and, although we shall be without several of our most prominent members, we shall still hope to be able to carry on the good work of previous years. For this to be done the full co-operation of all members will be required. Inter-club matches and Club handicaps are being arranged and particulars of these will be in the hands of all members very soon. For the Juniors, the usual Club Championships will be held, so now is the time to start getting down to it. Tooting Bec Track is now available for training and the usual Tuesday and Thursday evenings will find most members hard at it. It is open on Sunday mornings also. Either myself; the Vice-Captains, Harry Shields or Les. Bennett; or T. H. Scrimshaw (Junior Captain) will always most probably be in attendance, so if you require any information as regards training, etc., do not be afraid to ask any of the above, or any other Club Official. To all members who are chosen to represent the Club in various matches, I wish to remind them that if they are unable to turn up, please to be sure and let the Track Captain know at least two or three days before the race to enable him to get in touch with somebody else. Thank you! F. R. WEBB (Track Capt.), 50, Longford Avenue, Southall, Mx. Harry Shields Harry Shields Vice-Captain (track) Les. Bennett Les. Bennett Vice-Captain (track) T. H. Scrimshaw T. H. items.label: December 1940
items.sum: The club president recalls joining Belgrave forty to fifty years earlier, the old headquarters at the King's Arms and Boxing Day events, and wishes members on active service a safe return.
items.s: FROM OUR PRESIDENT The club president recalls joining Belgrave forty to fifty years earlier, the old headquarters at the King's Arms and Boxing Day events, and wishes members on active service a safe return. When I joined the Club, between forty and fifty years ago, I did not dream that I should ever attain the dignity of President of the Club. I wish I could have occupied the office under happier conditions than those which we are now going through. The Club has during its history gone through several critical periods and has emerged successfully; and we shall carry on the tradition of the Club and, in the end, be prepared to take our place in the front rank of athletics when the "All Clear" is sounded. My experiences of the Club are many and varied, some of them amusing and some of them had disturbing effects on the Club's existence. Still we live and our strength is greater than that it has ever been. The social side, which has developed during the last few years, has been a great help to the Club, and was non-existent in the early days. The accommodation for the members for training and racing is also a great advance on the old days. I can remember on the formation of the Club, that the headquarters was the King's Arms, Ranelagh Road, where we could hold about forty members, with one bath of hot water to be shared by everybody. I also recollect some handicaps at 100 yards, when the final was run at 10 o'clock in the evening. Then we had our great Boxing Day events, when the occasion was used for a reunion of the old members, and the price of beverages was well below to-day's prices! The Editor reminds me that I have used up my space, so I will conclude with my sincere wish for the safe and speedy return of all the members on active service, and trust that I may be of good health and cheer to help the Club through until the time comes to propose the health of "The Club." King's Arms, Ranelagh Road

items.label: December 1940
items.sum: The secretary's commentary on wartime club life: the slimmer Belgravian, the Wimbledon headquarters, deaths of three members, a list of members serving in H.M. Forces, Harry Parker standing in as secretary, subscriptions, marriages, and Joe Turner's election to cross-country presidencies.
items.s: HON. SECRETARY'S COMMENTARY The secretary's commentary on wartime club life: the slimmer Belgravian, the Wimbledon headquarters, deaths of three members, a list of members serving in H.M. Forces, Harry Parker standing in as secretary, subscriptions, marriages, and Joe Turner's election to cross-country presidencies. The days we live in compel a rather different-looking "Belgravian," reminiscent of our 1925 efforts, when W. H. Hare was Hon. Editor, with fewer pages than usual, and with more condensed reports of our activities. It is regretted that quarterly publication has not been found possible, but here again, the current difficulties are responsible. We are pleased to record, however, that our athletic activities have gone on, despite the decreased number of members available and the reduced training and racing facilities owing to the closing of Battersea Park Track. Our Wimbledon headquarters are now open for the winter season, and every Saturday finds a number of stalwarts enjoying their training. It is hoped that all available members will make the fullest use of these facilities and keep alive the spirit of comradeship and earnest endeavour which has made the Belgrave Harriers pre-eminent in the world of athletics. All of us hope for an early victory, and a return to happy, care-free days with our normal athletic programme before us. May it come soon! * * * * It is with deep regret that we have to record the deaths of E. G. W. Birch and W. F. Pigott, both of whom were killed on active service. It is with sorrow, also, that we announce the death of Harold Titherley, former Civil Service 880 yards champion, and valued member of our track teams, who was killed in a recent air raid. We extend our profound sympathy to the relatives and friends of these three members who have left us for ever. * * * * We have a record of the following members serving in H.M. Forces, and we wish them the best of luck wherever they may be. We are always glad to hear from members; and should be pleased to receive any further information which will amplify the following list. W. H. Applebee (R.N.), A. Allum (R.A.), N. Steer (Merchant Navy); and, of course, our many Regular Police and Fire Brigade members are very fully employed these days. Many others best serve the nation's war effort by carrying on in their normal work; whilst others find time to serve in the Home Guard and other Civil Defence services. Good luck to them all! Our Hon. Secretary has recently been taken out of civil life and appointed to the rank of Pilot-Officer in the R.A.F., and has now reported for duty in the West Country. In his absence the secretarial duties will be performed by the genial Harry Parker, and communications should be addressed to:— H. PARKER, 3, FRITHAM CLOSE, NEW MALDEN, SURREY. * * * * Our Hon. Treasurer is still at the same address (see page 1), and would welcome subscriptions, which are now due. It is our desire to keep the Club functioning in a modest way for the duration of the war; and to maintain our quarters in good condition against the day when we can all be together again for our accustomed sport. Income is needed to do this, and prompt settlement will save the Hon. Treasurer much effort and a big postage bill. * * * * Our congratulations and best wishes to Stan Botwright (now of the R.A.F.) and Tony Bellchambers (now 2nd Lt. in the Royal Artillery) and Syd Jones (now of the Army) on the occasion of their recent marriages. May good luck go with them! * * * * Our heartiest congratulations and best wishes go to our popular timekeeper and well-known A.A.A. official, Joe Turner, on his election as President of the Southern Counties Cross-Country Association, and also of the English Cross-Country Union. It is a matter for regret that his year of office cannot be a very full one; but the honour is well deserved for many years of hard work on behalf of cross-country running; and we know that Joe will do his utmost to keep the sport alive, and will be one of the first to ensure its revival to greater popularity than ever when peace comes again. * * * * Many members have written us lately, and it is regretted that limitations of space prevent quotations from being printed for the information and amusement of all. Several have achieved considerable success in the Service racing in which they have participated; and every letter asks for the writer's good wishes to be extended to all fellow-members. W. H. items.label: December 1940
items.h: REPORT OF TRACK SEASON, by TRACK CAPT. F. R. WEBB.
items.sum: The track captain's review of Belgrave's 1940 track season: ten wins from twelve matches, open team-race successes including the first News of the World 7 mile relay, and praise for Len Marchant, Bill Bowers and Harry Parker.
e: News of the World 7 mile relay
items.s: REPORT OF TRACK SEASON, by TRACK CAPT. F. R. WEBB. The track captain's review of Belgrave's 1940 track season: ten wins from twelve matches, open team-race successes including the first News of the World 7 mile relay, and praise for Len Marchant, Bill Bowers and Harry Parker. The 1940 Track Season was to most Clubs a problem, owing to so many of their Active Members having been called up for military service. This was, however, soon overcome. Club Officials, etc., got together, and decided to carry on in the usual way; with one exception, no Championship would be held. The membership shortage was also got over by clubs joining forces with each other for the duration of war. Belgrave were, however, more fortunate, being able to kick-off in early matches with some of the regular stars, but as the season advanced, together with the calling-up of the older age groups, so did our numbers reduce. With the aid, however, of several of our promising junior members, we were able to complete our full programme for the season, which was, on the whole, a most successful one. Twelve matches were fixed up, and we proved successful in ten, being beaten on the other two occasions by the Combined Clubs, whose combination of Blackheath H., London A.C. and S.L.H. members, were a little too strong for us, although in the first match we were defeated by only 4 points. In addition to the above matches we took part in four open track Team Races and a 1 Mile Medley Relay race, winning fairly easily each time, and then finally finishing up with a great win in the newly formed "News of the World" 7 mile relay race round Mitcham Common, five runners each to cover a distance of 1 mile 3 furlongs. I should like very much to thank all those members who have taken part at these meetings and helped to make them the success they were. It is hard to single out any one person, but special mention should be made of Len Marchant and Bill Bowers, both of whom have proved they are fast approaching the front rank of athletes by their fine performances. Len, in fact, has already represented the A.A.A. in their match against the Metropolitan Police, and has also assisted his county, Surrey, in several matches. It would hardly be correct to conclude this report without paying our tribute to our worthy Assistant Hon. Sec., Harry Parker, who has, if my memory is correct, turned up at every meeting throughout the season, and whose help was invaluable. Below are details of the various meetings:— F. R. Webb F. R. Our first Track meeting of the season was against the Combined Clubs, (Blackheath H., London A.C. and S.L.H.) Some keen racing was witnessed by many, and the result was a narrow win for the T.C.C. by 4 points. items.s: MATCH v. H.H.H. and M.P.A.A. 25.5.40. Report and results of the triangular match won narrowly by Belgrave over the Metropolitan Police and Herne Hill, with an open 3 miles team race, an open 1 hour walk, members' handicaps and junior events at the same meeting. This triangular match ended in a very narrow win for the Bels, 38 pts. against 36 M.P. and 25 H.H.H. In the 100 yds. Bowers finished 2nd and Read 3rd. Read also finished 3rd in the 220 yds. Jarlett was just beaten in the 880 yds., whilst in the mile Len Herbert and Bill Lucas came home easy winners. Shrubb finished 4th. The Medley relay was a very close race, Belgrave winning from the Police in 3 mins. 46 secs. Syd Jones, Jeal, Powell and T. C. Jones gained us valuable points in the field events. Also at this meeting was an open 3 Miles Team race, and Belgrave gained an easy win, filling first 3 places with Smart, Carter and Stimpson. Reeve, of Poly, was the actual winner, but was running as an individual. items.s: Return Match against T.C.C. 1.6.40. Report and results of the return match against the Combined Clubs (T.C.C.), with S. Wooderson winning the 880 yards and Belgrave taking the medley relay; the report puts Bowers 2nd in the 100 yards while the result lists him 3rd. Unfortunately we were unable to turn out a very strong team, but the home team were given quite a good match. Bowers and Bennett finished 2nd and 5th in both 100 yds. and 220 yds. F. R. Webb was second to Trodd, T.C.C., in 440 yds., whilst Ernie Duffett gained us a valuable point by finishing 4th, although he pulled a muscle in the first 100 yds. The 880 yds. proved an easy win for S. Wooderson, with Len Marchant 3rd and Alf Orton 4th. Bill Lucas won the mile, and Shrubb was 3rd. Carter was 2nd in the 2 miles, after a keen tussle with Bingham, T.C.C. Charlie Smart gained points by finishing 3rd. The final event, the 1 Mile Medley relay, was a great win for Belgrave, despite the inclusion of 3 distance runners and 1 sprinter—Marchant 880 yds., F. Webb and Bowers 220 yds., and Orton 440 yds. items.s: "News of World" Relay Race. 24.8.40. Report of the News of the World track-and-road relay on 24 August 1940, won by the Belgrave team nearly four minutes clear despite an air raid warning. The above took place on Saturday afternoon, from the "News of the World" Sports Ground, each runner starting the lap round the track, and then out on to the road for about 1 mile, and return to finish on the track once again. Allan Jerman was our first runner, and running very strongly, finished second to Frank Close, Surrey A.C. Les. Cohen then took over, and soon caught his man, to hand over a long lead to Charlie Smart, who continued after the restart through an air raid warning, in which the race was held up, to increase the lead, which was carried on by Tom Carter and Len Herbert, who finally broke the tape nearly 4 mins. ahead of the 2nd team. Allan Jerman Allan Jerman first leg, 2nd on his leg Frank Close Frank Close fastest on first leg Les. Cohen Les. Cohen second leg Charlie Smart Charlie Smart third leg, run through an air raid warning Tom Carter Tom Carter fourth leg Len Herbert Len Herbert final leg, broke the tape News of the World Relay "News of the World" Sports Ground Surrey A.C.
