items.label: December 1940
items.sum: Walking column with wartime news of the club's walkers in the forces, the club's One-hour Walk at Tooting Bec on 25 May 1940 with full results, Road Walking Association committee elections, and Belgrave's win in the first Southern 20 Miles Championship and other spring walks.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS Walking column with wartime news of the club's walkers in the forces, the club's One-hour Walk at Tooting Bec on 25 May 1940 with full results, Road Walking Association committee elections, and Belgrave's win in the first Southern 20 Miles Championship and other spring walks. "With the Walkers" would take us far afield these days, to many different parts of the country, but censorship will not permit us to say exactly where our friends now find themselves Our Hon. Secretary has a commission in the R.A.F.; our Road-Walking Captain, Charlie Churcher, is in an R.A.F. unit in the North; and our A.A.A. Champion and hero of many walks, Harry Churcher, is also in the R.A.F., undergoing a physical training instructor's course. Vice-Captains Joe Coleman and Reg Elson are serving in the R.A.F. and A. F. S. respectively. Our Track Walk Captain, Percy Wright (recently proud father of a son and heir), still mans the A.A. guns, whilst Vice-Captain Eddie Heather is, we regret to write, in a sanatorium, but making progress. All his many friends will wish him a speedy and complete recovery, and we hope to see him about again shortly. Jack Rutland (R.A.P.C.) audits Army accounts somewhere in the Midlands; and Len Coleman instructs Army cooks on how to cook! A former champion, E. L. Reeve, is in the R.A.O.C.; whilst Ted Saunders is a corporal in an R.A.M.C. unit functioning in the Near East. A. E. Elliott has duties with the Royal Corps of Signals, and W. H. Jones is in the Army Dental Corps. Bert Clayton and E. J. Watts are in the R.A.F., Tony Bellchambers holds a commission in the Royal Artillery, W. E. Ives is an Anti-Tank Regiment man, whilst his friend, C. H. Lloyd, is a Royal Engineer. Altogether, quite enough to affect the numbers out training from Wimbledon, especially as many of our Police members have little time for training; and others, such as Alan Bridger, Colin Sutton and Charlie Speechly are working seven days a week, and at least one, G. S. Doubleday, evacuated many miles away on important work. We still have a few who are taking their training seriously, however, and we are glad to know they are carrying on. Those serving will hope to be out again soon, getting ready for championship tussels and the thrill of the close-fought race. We imagine a "Belgrave—R.A.F." team consisting of H. G. Churcher, C. E. Churcher, J. G. Coleman and H. G. Clayton (reserves: E. J. Watts, A. A. Harley), would take some beating over seven miles. Perhaps a "Belgrave—Army" team chosen from L. J. Coleman, J. E. Rutland, P. G. Wright, A. E. Elliott, J. A. Bellchambers, W. H. Jones, C. H. Lloyd, E. L. Reeve, W. E. Ives, would like to try conclusions—if it could be arranged—with perhaps a "Belgrave—Police" team to make a three-cornered affair of it. We should certainly see some very fine walking, if only such a fixture could leave the realms of fantasy for actuality! * * * * On May 25th we promoted, at Tooting Bec Track, a One-hour's Walk in an endeavour to make yet another contribution to the sport. The entry received was quite good, having regard to the general conditions, and 22 started, 19 finishing. Fred Redman walked in excellent style, and with nine other walkers, detailed below, covered over seven miles in the hour. We are certain that in normal times such a race as this would be overhelmingly popular. It is the mark of a "useful" walker to be able to cover seven miles within the hour; and many of us have experienced a thrill on the first occasion we have succeeded in doing so. Conditions vary so widely in road races that standardisation is impossible, but in a track race such as we promoted competitors had the opportunity of earning an engraved award should they succeed in walking seven miles or over in sixty minutes. We feel that when the war is disposed of, an event of this nature, held on one of our best tracks, would attract an embarrassingly large entry, and do much to popularise walking as a sport. 1, F. J. Redman (Met. W.C.), distance in 1 hour, 7 miles, 1,270 yards; 2, H. H. Whitlock (Met. W.C), 7 m., 900 yds.; 3, M. J. Fisher (S.W.C.), 7 m. 885 yds.; 4, E. A. Staker (H.H.), 7 m. 740 yds.; 5, N. A. L. Burt (S.W.C.), 7 m. 620 yds.; 6, H. D. Neilson (Poly. H.), 7 m. 455 yds.; 7, A. L. Fletcher (Bel. H.), 7 m. 400 yds.; 8, A. H. Rayner (S.A.C.), 7 m. 130 yds.; 9, C. C. Saunders (H.H.), 7 m. 110 yds.; 10, T. B. Kent (W.G.A.C.), 7 m. 106 yds.; 11, E. G. Barnes (H.H.), 6 m. 1,750 yds.; 12, J. J. Allen (Enf. A.C.), 6 m. 1,740 yds.; 13, R. D. McMullen, Jnr. (Bel. H.), 6 m. 1,680 yds.; 14, A. D. McSweeney (H.H.), 6 m. 1,480 yds.; 15, F. H. Elson (Bel. H.), 6 m. 1,470 yds.; 16, C. Megnen (H.H.), 6 m. 1,438 yds.; 17, W. H. Snell (Bel. H.), 6 m. 1,220 yds.; 18, G. G. Swan (B.W.C.), 6 m. 1,200 yds.; 19, S. E. Horton (S.W.C.), 6 m. 1,090 yds. A Cup, suitably engraved, was presented to the winner, and engraved miniature souvenir cups have gone to the nine other successful walkers. War service and duties robbed the race of entries from some of the well-known walkers in the South; but the Club has every reason to be proud of its promotion and the interest it created. * * * * The Club has been paid a high compliment by the Southern Committee of the Road Walking Association in the election of A. A. Harley to its Chairmanship, and of J. C. Bidgood to the Vice-Chairmanship. In addition to F. G. Thomson, a past Chairman, we also have F. H. Elson and S. C. Roberts serving on this Committee. J. G. Coleman was a member of the Committee last year, but would not allow his name to go forward this season as he is now serving in the R.A.F. * * * * A glance at the last issue of the "Belgravian" published shows that we were then looking forward to the newly instituted Southern 20 Miles Championship. The race took place on May 4th from De Bohuns Farm, and it is now very much late news that Belgrave won the title after one of the most exciting races ever. Charlie Churcher played a real captain's part in finishing second only nine seconds behind Whitlock. Our team was completed by Rutland, Bidgood and Roberts finishing 10, 11, 12. This gave us a total of 35 points—the same as Surrey Walking Club, whose men scored 4, 8, 9, 14. According to rule, lowest time aggregate decided the winning team, and here we had the advantage of 3 mins. 29 seconds. A wonderfully fine finish between two splendid teams. The closing stages were most exciting in both individual and team race, and we received great help when the two Essex Beagles, Abel and Everard, overhauled S.W.C. walkers in the last two miles. Altogether a very fine race, which held compensation for our defeat by Surrey Walking Club in the 10 miles race held earlier in the season. * * * * Two other walks held earlier had served as preparation for the Championship just described. In the Metropolitan W.C. 15 miles race, held in Regents Park, we won the scratch team race by two points from Surrey Walking Club. Harry Thaxter won the individual handicap, with Charlie Churcher second; and so, inevitably, we won the handicap team race. The "Godstone," held on April 20th, did not find us quite so prominent. In this race Charlie Churcher walked splendidly to take second place, and in the scratch team race S.W.C. won by 13 points to our 25. * * * * Our congratulations go to Harry Thaxter, who won the Metropolitan Police A.A. 10 miles Championship in April last. items.label: December 1940
items.sum: Account of the Annual General Meeting at Belgrave Hall on 25 September 1940: the Hon. Secretary's report on the club's wartime year, the accounts, a war-time rule change, Life Membership for C. E. Churcher and R. J. Savage, F. G. Thomson's election as President and the new Committee.
items.s: THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING Account of the Annual General Meeting at Belgrave Hall on 25 September 1940: the Hon. Secretary's report on the club's wartime year, the accounts, a war-time rule change, Life Membership for C. E. Churcher and R. J. Savage, F. G. Thomson's election as President and the new Committee. The Annual General Meeting was held at Belgrave Hall on September 25th, and in view of the comparatively small attendance (37 were present) we give some account of the proceedings. In the absence of the President, Mr. J. B. Belchamber was elected to the Chair and the meeting began with the formal reading of the notice convening the meeting, and of the Minutes of the last A.G.M., which were approved. The Hon. Secretary then made his report. He announced that two members, E. G. W. Birch and W. F. Pigott, had been killed on active service, and the meeting stood for a few moments as a tribute to their memory. The Hon. Secretary then said that the Committee had kept their promise of the previous year to keep things going; and that the Club had enjoyed an excellent winter season and a very fine track season. The Club had given a lead to the Athletic world in the previous November, when it had promoted its Annual Open Walk, and its Headquarters had been at the disposal of promoting bodies time and time again for their races. Two open events had been included in the first summer track programme in a further endeavour to give a lead to the sport. The Hon. Secretary said, with some emphasis, that in the year under review the Belgrave Harriers had done more to keep athletics alive—and vigorously alive—than any other organisation. He did not expect nor desire columns in the Press praising the Club's efforts; but he knew that but for the Belgrave Harriers, its headquarters, its promotions, and its athletes, the Athletic year would not have been nearly so successful as it had proved. He said that Club members had greatly distinguished themselves, and without giving detailed statistics, contented himself with pointing out that both runners and walkers had carried off the highest honours during the winter season, and that on the track and in the field the Club members had greatly distinguished themselves. He regretted the spasmodic appearance of "The Belgravian," occasioned by current difficulties, but promised an edition in the course of a few weeks. The Hon. Secretary recalled that as the year had progressed, more and more members had been absorbed into H.M. Forces, until we had now reached the stage when almost every member between the ages of 20 and 34 (with the exception of a few working long hours in reserved occupations) was either serving in some way or expecting to do so in the near future. He then paid tribute to the Committee's efforts during the past difficult year. The President had early been placed in an important position taking him out of London and monopolising the whole of his time; and so the Chair had been occupied at various times by Messrs. Gordon, Thomson, and Webb, who had helped the business through. The Hon. Secretary expressed his personal gratitude to H. Parker and E. A. Duffett for their ever-ready help; and also said that the Club owed much to their Hon. Treasurer; to T. F. Morrell for his excellent social arrangements; to the Club Captains for their work, and to the three Hon. Secretaries, who had carried the burden of the Club's money-making schemes. He also expressed the Club's thanks to W. J. Fish, A. G. Fell, W. Redgrave and the other Club officials, without whom track meetings would be an impossibility. The Hon. Secretary continued by saying that, although the future was obscure to all, he felt confident that if the Club affairs were left in the hands of the older members—men who had done much for the Club and were prepared to do a lot more—the younger element would come back and find that the stewardship had been wisely administered. All members felt pride and a personal interest in the Hall, the Club's investments, and in the growth and development the Club had made in recent years, and those members called upon to don uniform would do so knowing that these interests were being maintained and preserved. When the longed-for day arrived and everyone could get back to the normal life, members would have the satisfaction of knowing that they had a Committee in being which, with an infusion of the younger blood, would get the Club away to a flying start and a clear lead. There would be no inertia to overcome. The Hon. Secretary concluded by wishing all members the best of luck, and asked for their continued support for years to come as active members, officials, helpers, supporters—anything as long as they attended on occasion, and so continued in the good fellowship all had learned to value so much. It was proposed by F. H. Elson, seconded by G. H. Powell, and unanimously agreed that the report should be adopted. The Hon. Treasurer then introduced his Accounts and reported thereon. J. B. Bellchamber, Club Hon. Auditor for approaching thirty years, praised the Hon. Treasurer's work; and the report and accounts were duly adopted. The Hon. Secretary then explained the proposed alteration of rule relating to the management of the Club, which had been circulated. It was made clear that this was only a war-time measure, and designed to facilitate the conduct of the Club's affairs in such difficult times. The alteration to rule was approved. On behalf of the Committee and in accordance with the Law governing the matter, the Hon. Secretary then proposed the election of C. E. Churcher as a Life Member. He spoke of Churcher's services to the Club as a walker, as a Club captain, leading the Club teams to many victories, of his valuable help on the social side, but above all, of the unremitting care and many hours of labour that he had devoted, often at great personal inconvenience and without any thought of reward, to Belgrave Hall and its maintenance. It was a matter for regret that C. E. Churcher could not be present and witness the appreciation of his fellow-members for his many efforts on their behalf; but that morning he had joined his R.A.F. unit in the North. The proposal was seconded by T. F. Morrell and carried unanimously. The Hon. Secretary then made a further proposal on behalf of the Committee, that R. J. Savage should be similarly honoured. He said that Mr. Savage, who had joined the Club in 1910, had always devoted himself to the Club's interests, was an ever-willing worker, an enthusiast who had presented us with a Junior Cross-country Championship Shield, and a man who had done more than his share to build up the Club. The proposal was seconded by E. Gordon, and carried unanimously. Mr. Savage replied suitably and assured the meeting of his willingness to help the Club at all times. The meeting then proceeded to the election of officers. E. Gordon proposed that F. G. Thomson should be President for the ensuing year. He said that Mr. Thomson had joined the Club in 1889—two years after formation—and had been honoured with Life Membership as far back as 1897. He had served athletics in many high positions and was one of the best known and most respected A.A.A. officials of the day. G. H. Powell seconded the proposal, which met with the meeting's unanimous support. Mr. Thomson returned thanks for his election. The existing Vice-Presidents were all re-elected, as were the Hon. Secretary, Hon. Treasurer, Trustees, Hon. Auditor and other officials. Ten members were elected to serve on the Committee as follows:—F. R. Webb, H. Parker, T. F. Morrell, F. H. Elson, H. W. Shields, L. J. Cohen, C. T. Carter, E. A. Duffett, R. J. Savage and T. C. Jones. A vote of thanks to the Chairman concluded the meeting. J. B. Belchamber J. B. items.s: THE WALKERS TAKE THIS OPPORTUNITY— Note from the walking section thanking A. A. Harley, now a Pilot Officer, and captain Charlie Churcher, now in the R.A.F., for their work, and saying the posts have been left unfilled in their absence. of expressing their combined thanks to A. A. Harley (now Pilot Officer) for his work on behalf of their Section over a number of years. Although he has had many other voluntary duties, the walkers have always felt that his chief concern was for them, and they know very definitely that the many successes and the proud reputation their section has in this branch of athletics is, without doubt, greatly due to his untiring efforts on their behalf. We also thank our captain, Charlie Churcher, now in the R.A.F., for his brilliant leadership and good comradeship, and we remind both these gentlemen that the Club has not elected anybody to fill these positions in their absence. So we thank very sincerely our Walking Secretary and our Captain for their work, and say that the Walking Section will be ready again to follow their lead when we all re-unite in happier times. A. A. Harley A. A. items.sum: Letter from the President, Frank Thomson, to Harry saying his health has broken down and he cannot help the Club for now, with the members' wishes for his recovery.
items.s: THE BELGRAVIAN Letter from the President, Frank Thomson, to Harry saying his health has broken down and he cannot help the Club for now, with the members' wishes for his recovery. THE BELGRAVIAN The Official Gazette of the Belgrave Harriers. 30, Middle Green Road, Langley, Bucks. May, 20th, 1941. My dear Harry,— I am sorry to inform you that my health has broken down again and I have gone to the above address. I don't know how long I shall be here. Under the circumstances I am not good for anything at the moment, and I shall not be available for any help to the Club. I am extremely upset about it and cannot imagine how it is all going to end. After so many years of happiness and joy with the Club, I feel my position acutely. I am unable to write more, I'm feeling so despondent. I hope for the best. Yours sincerely, FRANK THOMSON. All members will wish our hard-working President a speedy and lasting recovery. Frank Thomson FRANK THOMSON President; health broken down, staying at Langley, Bucks. Langley, Bucks.

J. Marsden. The notes announce "twelve new members" but list fifteen names. Tooting Bec track is now available for training on Wednesday and Thursday evenings and Sunday mornings. It is the desire of the Committee to keep in touch with all members serving with the Forces. Members are asked to advise the Hon. Secretary of any change of address or their Service address. A " Service Address " book is kept at Belgrave Hall for reference for members on leave. Letters from servisg members will be circulated amongst members. Don't make the excuse that you have lost the Secretary's address; letters addressed to Belgrave Hall will always find him. Since our last issue many members have joined the Services, amongst whom are: Don Brown, H. D. Brown, S. G. T. De Beau, R. Dunford, Charlie Smart, L. W. Herbert, W. Merryman (R.A.F.); F. C. Clayton (Hants Regt.), C. F. Calvert (A.A.), Frank Elston (R.A.O.C.), W. Hewitt (R.A.M.C.), R. G. Michael (R.N.), J. McDonald (R.F.), L. E. Spooner (A.P. Office), V. D. Wynyard (Signals). A. Smith (R.B.), V. N. Ley. Members will be pleased to hear that Jim Tosh, our quarter and half-mile champion of a few years past, has gained his Commission in the Queen's Regiment. Our congratulations to Bill Lucas on winning his " wings." Our new Sergeant Pilot has only just been posted to his Squadron, and more news is now awaited from him. We also congratulate Alf. Taylor, Bill Sutton and G. M. Murray on their recent marriages, and our Hon. Secretary upon his engagement. We also have to place on record the death of George Pepper. George was a cross-country champion of years ago, who later took up track work and was frequently to be seen on the Battersea Park track helping the youngsters, and giving advice to the seniors in his capacity as Track Captain. He frequently officiated at our meetings and will be sorely missed. We are very pleased to record the election of twelve new members:— R. H. Bryan, L. J. Higgins, S. C. Moore, G. R. Matheson, Lieut. A. J. Marsden, A. W. G. Peck, W. H. Speight, A. B. Simpson, J. R. Strachan, J. B. Thomas, K. J. Webb, W. K. Wright, J. Chappel, L. E. Daniels and R. H. Gibb. W. K. Wright is the proud owner of " Percy ' as father, and is. I believe, the youngest member ever elected, having only been born in October. 1940! For the purpose of inter-club matches, etc., we have arranged to combine with the Polytechnic Harriers. There has always been a very friendly feeling in existence between our two clubs, and in difficult times it is natural that we should turn to one another for mutual help. Have you seen Percy Wright's News Letter circulated to the Walkers? I should like to hear from an enthusiast who would do the same for the runners. Any offers? The following is an extract from a letter received from one of our new members, Lt. J. Marsden, recently transferred out of London:— " When I was in London I enjoyed running with the " Belgrave Harriers " more than anything else I did in the week. The kindness of Mr. Parker, who wrote inviting me, of those I ran with, of those whose Hall I shared for tea and bath, of international runners waiting at corners for me to catch up; of Tom Carter telling me to cut off a corner and rejoin the pack on the way home I shall never forget. I long to see old "George" setting off on his "weekly" 5-miler. How I look forward to trying to keep up with the pack a little further than the pond, though I doubt whether I shall make it. My thoughts are with you as I proceed soon, I do not know where. If I have the chance I shall come and have another run on a Saturday with you before I am transferred. Meanwhile all the best, and good luck on the track." Don Brown Don Brown joined the Services H. D. Brown H. D. Brown joined the Services S. G. T. De Beau S. G. T. De Beau joined the Services R. items.s: " BELGRAVE NEWS LETTER " Percy Wright announces a regular monthly news-letter for walkers to be passed on from member to member, and asks walkers who have not received it to contact him. " BELGRAVE NEWS LETTER " At a time like the present, when it is so essential to keep the fellows in contact with each other, the difficulties against regular issues of the " Belgravian " are enormous. One quickly loses touch with the Club, and its affairs, and for that reason I have instituted a regular monthly news-letter for walkers. It is not possible to issue one to each member, but it is hoped everybody will get the chance to reach each issue. Those walkers who so far have not received the " Letter " please let me know at—C/o 3. Ivor Street, Cwmcarn. Mon,— and I will arrange for one to be passed on. You, in turn, will be given another address, to which you will post it when you have finished. By this means it is hoped we can all keep track of each other, so when the time comes. we can meet again in that congenial spirit we have known so well in the past. PERCY WRIGHT. Percy Wright PERCY WRIGHT started a monthly news-letter for walkers Cwmcarn

items.sum: Extracts from a letter by former Junior Captain H. M. Quackenbo in New York to G. S. Doubleday, with American athletics news and his own studies and running at M.I.T.
items.s: NEWS FROM U.S.A. Extracts from a letter by former Junior Captain H. M. Quackenbo in New York to G. S. Doubleday, with American athletics news and his own studies and running at M.I.T. NEWS FROM U.S.A. (We are indebted to G. S. Doubleday for extracts of a letter from our former Junior Captain and popular member, H. M. Quackenbo.) 20, Yonkers Avenue, ... ...... Tuckahoe, New York. December 26th, 1940. Dear Doub,— Christmas Day was unnaturally warm all over the country. Here, just outside New York City, it was 60 Deg.F. Unlike skating and ski-ing enthusiasts I am thankful for these warm spells, being not yet accustomed to the bitter dry cold prevailing most of the winter. Running outdoors in the cold is very hard on your lungs. The air rushing in and out doesn't have time to get heated up and lungs and throat take a beating. After running a race I am reminded of Footer, shaken by coughing after a training run, erasing his name from the Southern team. Glen Cunningham has retired at last to take up the post of physical director at a small college in Iowa. Indoors he failed to win a single race. Outdoors he won only one—the Missouri Valley 1,500 metres in 3 m. 49 s. by 70 yards from San Romani (who also had a most unsuccessful season. After such a good time he seemed all set to win the National 1,700 metres, especially as Fenske was ill. Cunningham did 3 m 48.1 s. in this race, his best yet, but Mehl created a tremendous surprise by getting first place in 3 m. 47.9 s., a new American record. Performances in the Nationals, in California were generally record breaking. Warmedan pole vaulted 15 ft. 1⅜ ins., the Shot went 56 feet and the Discuss 170 feet. A California college freshman ran 400 metres in 47 secs., and another won the 200 metres in 20.4 secs. Since that time the only big event has been the National Cross Country Championship three weeks ago. Don Lash won for the seventh consecutive time from Greg. Rice and Luigi Beccali, who now seems to be a New Yorker. Most of the boys are now getting quietly into shape for the indoor season. As I'm finishing my courses at M.I.T. in February, my chief concern now is to get a job. Quite a few of the big chemical firms send their representatives to Boston to interview chemists and chemical engineers. If the representative's report is favourable and the company concerned places you on their final list for selection you often get an invitation to visit them and see what processes are being carried out at the plant. The company usually pays expenses. I received an invitation to visit the paints and pigments department of Dupont at Newark, N.J. You chat with the big shots, get taken over the plant, are given lunch and altogether spend an agreeable day. All I want now is a definite offer from them. Your mention of Belgrave successes, both running and walking, made very pleasant reading. As for myself, I'm looking to 10 minutes for 2 miles. I did 10 m. 15 s. last November, and the coach keeps improving my half and mile times over trials in training in the theory that this brings down the 2 and 3 mile times. Yours "-QUACK." G. S. items.label: June 1941
items.h: BELGRAVE HARRIERS BUILDING FUND FOOTBALL COMPETITION
items.sum: T. Cotton recounts how the club's football forecasting competitions, begun by Frank Elston, grew from 1935-36 to fund the Building Fund, were dropped in wartime, and looks ahead to a club-owned headquarters after the war.
items.s: BELGRAVE HARRIERS BUILDING FUND FOOTBALL COMPETITION T. Cotton recounts how the club's football forecasting competitions, begun by Frank Elston, grew from 1935-36 to fund the Building Fund, were dropped in wartime, and looks ahead to a club-owned headquarters after the war. BELGRAVE HARRIERS BUILDING FUND FOOTBALL COMPETITION Previous to the Winter 1935-6, Frank Elston had run a small competition in which one forecast how many goals would be scored in the first and second divisions of the English leagues. Each forecast cost one penny, and the prizes, I believe, began as 10s. and then incresed to £1 as the scheme grew. This, though seemingly a small thing, proved to be a very valuable addition to our " Building Fund," and several of us began to think seriously of increasing the scope of a football competition among members. After all, with 600 members, many of whom already were entering outside competitions, we thought we could do something rather bigger than had hitherto been attempted. A committee was formed after the matter had been delegated from the General Club Committee. Frank and I were taking, with several others, a very keen interest in all this but I think our eventual plunge into a really large scheme was largely influenced by our old friend Teddy Gordon, who was all for taking a crack at something really large. So it was that in the season 1935-36, with Frank and myself as Joint Hon. Secretaries, the Building Fund Committee, supported by the General Committee, launched a competition very similar to the one which ended last winter. The prizes in our peace-time competition were, of course, larger than those run during the war period. The competitions disproved all our early anxieties and went from strength to strength, thanks to the many fine helpers we had in the Club. I will give no figures but a reference to the last Building Fund balance-sheet will show how our wildest dreams were surpassed and the future, as well as the present Belgravians will owe much to those who so heartily supported us in those days. Well now, Frank is in the Army somewhere, and I am an auxiliary Fireman, and many of our good helpers in various services or out of London on important national work, so the competitions have had to be dropped. For good? Not likely! As soon as this bad dream has ended and we get back to civilian life we are going all out to put Belgrave in such a financial position that we will have the finest headquarters of any club, equipped with baths and showers, indoor exercise facilities, massage room, etc., etc., and all our very own, by our own efforts. That independence is very dear to all Belgravians and we shall insist on maintaining it. We shall never be forced to elect officials simply for their financial support, and thus have the policy of the Club altered by persons who do not hold the same views on sport for sport sake that we have always maintained. A club built by the boys for the boys, and run by the boys, though some of them have been forced to hang up their spikes by Old Man Time, that is what we have always desired and what we have always achieved. So just get ready to carry on! T. COTTON. Frank Elston Frank Elston ran a small football forecasting competition before winter 1935-6; Joint Hon. Secretary of the competition from 1935-36; now in the Army Teddy Gordon Teddy Gordon "our old friend"; encouraged the large football competition scheme T. Cotton T. COTTON Joint Hon. Secretary of the Building Fund Committee football competition from 1935-36; now an auxiliary Fireman

items.h: A FEW NOTES FROM OUR TRACK CAPTAIN
items.sum: The Track Captain asks members and juniors to make themselves available for track matches, handicaps and junior championships.
items.s: A FEW NOTES FROM OUR TRACK CAPTAIN The Track Captain asks members and juniors to make themselves available for track matches, handicaps and junior championships. A FEW NOTES FROM OUR TRACK CAPTAIN By the time you receive this Magazine we shall have taken part in several track matches. An interesting programme has been arranged at home and away, and it is hoped therefore that these will be well supported. It has not been possible to get into touch with all members, so if there are any who will be available for forthcoming fixtures, will they please get in touch with Vice-Capt. Harry Shields or myself as soon as possible. It will thus relieve the pressure on the members who have been giving valuable assistance in the earlier matches. Club handicaps will be arranged as the season advances, but these are only possible if we get full support from all available members, so it is up to you to put in an appearance at the track whenever possible and help to keep the Club's name in the front line of Athletics. All junior members who are also available should get in touch with me as soon as possible so as to enable me to arrange fixtures for them. Club Junior championships will probably be held this year if sufficient numbers turn out, so round up all those juniors you know of, and let's keep our sport going during these eventful days. All enquiries to F. R. Webb, 50, Longford Avenue, Southall Mdx. Harry Shields Harry Shields Vice-Capt. F. R. Webb F. R. items.label: June 1941
items.sum: Outline of the club's 1941 track season, the second under war conditions: home dates at Tooting Common Track, matches with combined clubs, joining forces with Polytechnic Harriers, junior fixtures, A.A.A. open handicaps and the Southern Junior Championships.
items.s: THE TRACK SEASON FOR 1941 Outline of the club's 1941 track season, the second under war conditions: home dates at Tooting Common Track, matches with combined clubs, joining forces with Polytechnic Harriers, junior fixtures, A.A.A. open handicaps and the Southern Junior Championships. THE TRACK SEASON FOR 1941 In this our second track season under War conditions, we are endeavouring to give those of our members who are still with us as much competition as possible. , Also, of course, we hope that if any of our lads in the Services can secure leave to come along and help us—they will do so—and we promise them all a run. We have booked Tooting Common Track for three home dates, and have arranged matches with as many of our old friends and rivals as possible. These include the Combined Clubs—L.A.C. Blackheath & S.L.H.—London University Tyrian—Metropolitan Police A.C.—Shaftesbury H.—and a new combination, the West Middlesex Triangle, which is the T.V.H. Finchley H. & Southall A.C. combined. This combining of clubs seems the only solution to fielding a full side under present conditions, and for the present season we are joining forces with the Polytechnic Harriers, at their request, and we heartily welcome their kind co-operation, and they have also placed their track at Chiswick at our disposal for training purposes. I have been rather disappointed at the non-appearance of our Juniors this season, and hope that any of them that can do so will come along to Tooting Track—Thursday is now the training night there—and I am also hoping to arrange a Junior match with the Whitgift Middle School at Croydon. In our matches with the T.C.C. will be included a 100 Yds. and 880 Yds for Juniors under 19, and I trust we shall be able to field teams in each. The A.A.A. are also helping towards keeping the sport going by promoting three Open Handicap meetings, and I hope all our members that can do so will support these meetings and so show the governing body that their efforts are appreciated by the athletes. Whether we shall be able to hold the usual club handicaps will depend on the numbers that turn out during the season, but if the Committee feel that they are warranted we shall certainly put some on. Also the Southern Committee of the A.A.A. are holding the Junior Championships once more, and these are open to all those over the age of sixteen and under nineteen years on day of the meeting—21st June. Thus it will be seen that there is still plenty for the really enthusiastic member to do, and I hope you will fetch out those spikes and come along to lend the Club a hand and so still keep the name of Belgrave a power in the athletic world. I append hereunder a list of our fixtures together with the principal open ones, but hope to add to this list as the season progresses. A.A.A. items.sum: Review of the club's field-event performers last season (javelin, weight, discus, high jump and long jump) and hopes for this season, with enquiries to T. C. Jones, whose address is printed here as S.W.11 (S.W.6 in the masthead).
items.s: FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP Review of the club's field-event performers last season (javelin, weight, discus, high jump and long jump) and hopes for this season, with enquiries to T. C. Jones, whose address is printed here as S.W.11 (S.W.6 in the masthead). FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP This season as regards Field Events will, it is hoped, be as successful as last. Some of the performances last season were very good. Charlie Melchior was, I think, our most outstanding performer. His Javelin throwing was very consistent at over 160 feet in most competitions, one or two over 170 feet, and then in the Match v. Police at Imber Court he managed 190 feet. He is to be congratulated on these performances, and also on his selection by the A.A.A. for nearly all their representative teams. It is to be hoped that he will crack that 190 feet again this season. George Powell, in spite of his large number of years in competition. still manages to keep among the best, and he managed a few throws of over 160 feet last season. This season we are looking forward to his valued support again. Ron Jeal managed one or two good throws but was rather inconsistent and does not seem to be able to recapture the form which enabled him to win the Surrey Championship two or three years ago. This season it is hoped he may regain that form. He was also a valued supporter in the Discus and managed one or two good performances in that event also. Sid Jones was again the outstanding Weight Putter and Discus man. He was consistently doing over 38 feet and his best performance was over 40 feet in the Weight. We shall unfortunately not be able to call upon him this season, but it is to be hoped he will be able to turn out when on leave. Bill Sutton was fairly consistent at about his usual distance with the Weight. He still does not seem to be able to reach that 40 feet which might be expected of him. His Discus throwing was perhaps a slight improvement over the previous season and once or twice he managed to beat Sid Jones. E. J. Brewer turned out a number of times, but whilst not showing the form of which we know he was capable he proved a valuable member of the teams, both in the Discus and Shot. In the High Jump, Brooks was almost our only representative. He is young and should improve in the future. His best performance was 5 ft. 4 ins. and consistently he did 5 ft. 2 ins., and wth more of Mr. Thomson's coaching he should master the " Western Roll " and show some good performances. In the Long Jump we were without the services of Skelley and Wiley last season. Charlie Jones, whilst not doing anything outstanding, managed to gain 2nd or third place in most of the matches. Frank Simmons and Dunford were both good supporters and enabled us to pick up points in this event, but the services of Skelley and Wiley were sorely missed. We have, still available, for the coming season nearly all the fellows mentioned and there may be some Junior members who wish to specialize in Field Events, and at the present time they can gain valuable experience in the matches which we have fixed up. Any enquiries should be addressed to:—T. C. Jones, 6, Broomwood Road, S.W.11. Charlie Melchior Charlie Melchior javelin: consistently over 160 feet, 190 feet in the match v. items.s: Report of a new fixture against Epsom College on 1 March 1941 over a five-mile course, won individually by Abberton, with Belgrave winning 49 points to 56. March 1st, 1941. A new fixture v. Epsom College, but over "old country"—and thoroughly enjoyed by all who took part. Seven aside scored over a five-mile course; and Abberton showed the way home despite a very gallant effort on the part of Dobson, of the College. Lomas showed the result of good systematic training by finishing a close third only 50 seconds behind the winner. Afterwards both teams sat down to tea, which was heartily appreciated. A vote of thanks to the College for their cordial welcome and the hope that further fixtures will follow were heartily echoed by all Belgravians present. 1, Begrave H. : 49 points; 2, Epsom College : 56 points. Abberton Abberton won Dobson Dobson gallant effort, of the College Lomas Lomas close third, 50 seconds behind the winner Epsom College Begrave H.

e: News of the World Road Relay
items.s: " News of The World " Road Relay Race Report of the News of the World road relay at Mitcham on 17 May 1941, where Belgrave finished second to Mitcham A.C. after a course-marking blunder, with the Belgrave lap times. May 17th. 1941. " News of The World " Road Relay Race This popular fixture was held at Mitcham on Saturday 17th May, and attracted an entry of over 40 teams, which included many Service sides. Running for an Air Force team was Charlie Smart, and his team had the satisfaction of being the seccond Service side to finish. Our first runner was our track captain Frank Webb, and he did well to finish sixth with Nicholson, of Woodford Green A.C., leading the field. Harry Shields went off next and battled his way round to hand over in third position to Tommy Morrell, who was our next runner. Tom ran very well indeed and took us up a place so that Alf. Shaw was sent off in second place, and with Les. Cohen and Tom Carter to follow our chances looked fairly good. Richards, of Mitcham, however rudely upset these by running a sterling relay which took his team into first place, and moreover gave them a 150 yards lead from Les. Cohen, who went off behind Fox, of Mitcham. The latter always seemed to give of his best in these road relays, and Les. did well to hold his ground against such a formidable opponent. For the last leg Tom Carter was given the hopeless job of trying to concede Ivor Brown a long start, but amazed everybody by getting to within 50 yards of his rival and clocking the time of 14 mins. 10 secs. for the three mile lap. Brown was in a very distressed condition at the finish, but is to be complimented on leading his team of Welsh athletes to victory. Unfortunately a bad blunder was made in pointing the course and the first two relays were only two miles instead of three. The mishap was rectified then so that the later runners covered the right course. We know that it was the same for everybody, but over the first lap the Mitcham man was well down the field and with a further mile may have been further behind still. Also Harry Shields, who ran second for us, finished full of running and would have gained more ground for us had he run the proper course of three miles. However, it is no good supposing now that the race is over, and we look forward to meeting our Mitcham rivals again as we hear a rumour that Joe Binks is contemplating holding another road relay in the near future. A Canadian Army team had the honour of being the first Service side to finish, and their abbreviated shorts were a sight for sore eyes! Chief team placings :—1, Mitcham A.C. (81.42); 2, Belgrave H. (81.47); 3, Finchley H. (82.45). BELGRAVE TIMES. F. Webb ... ... ... ... ... ... 11m. 20s. H. Shields ... ... ... ... ... ... 11m. 27s. T. Morrell ... ... ... ... ... ... 15m. 11s. A. items.s: Match v. U.L. Tyrian Club Report and results of the track match against U.L. Tyrian Club at Tooting Bec on 31 May 1941, the season's first, which Tyrian won 49 points to 44. Match v. U.L. Tyrian Club This enjoyable fixture was held at Tooting Bec Track on Saturday, May 31st. We were especially pleased to see so many of our Service members present. These included—Stan. Botwright, Bill Bowers, Sid. Jones, Charlie Melchior and Alf. Orton. Our sprinters proved very short of training, although Metcalfe, of the "Poly.," ran very well in the longer sprint. A newcomer, J. W. Thomas, together with Tommy Morrell, represented us in the Mile, and they both ran well against a much stronger opponent. Tom Carter, without any "real" opposition, ran a training 3 miles and reeled off his laps in faultless style. Harry Shields had to fight for his second place in this event, and this alone made the race very entertaining to watch. Sid. Jones showed he had lost none of his form with a first and second, and Charlie Melchior proved that his working arm was in good throwing order and was well backed up by the evergreen George Powell. In the relay Sid. Jarlett just pipped Atkinson over the half-mile stage, but a bad take-over by Bowers lost some ground. The latter recovered himself in fine style and sent Stan. Botwright off in front to hand over a 10 yards lead to Len. Marchant. Len. "legged" it out in smashing style and try as his opponent did he could not reduce the gap, and so we won the final event of the afternoon. With the points scoring 5—3—1 for each event, the relay was a 3—0 affair. It will be seen that the Tyrian just won the match by reason of their securing the majority of first places. This was our first match of the season, however, and for our future fixtures we hope to have more of the "Poly." boys lending us a hand, but so long as we do our bit towards keeping the sport going then we are well satisfied. items.s: Match v.T.C.C. & U.L. Tyrian Report and results of the evening track match on 4 June 1941 against The Combined Clubs and U.L. Tyrian, won by Belgrave with 65 points; the text gives T.C.C. 30 points but the printed result line says 3 pts. Match v.T.C.C. & U.L. Tyrian Our return match, Wednesday evening, June 4th, with the Tyrian Club, and our first meeting with old friends The Combined Clubs, i.e., London A.C., South London H., and Blackheath H., resulted in a somewhat hollow victory for our lads. Both the other competing teams were not at full strength, however, the Tyrian lacking the services of most of their Medical students, while the T.O.C. seemed to miss that genial personality C. E. Jones, who is now in the Navy, although his successor E. G. Lymbery did his best to field a representative side, which included A. D. Holmes, of Essex Beagles, and A. V. Mortimer, that very promising young Finchley Harrier. Our side had been strengthened by the inclusion of Frank Close, the well known miler and International runner; also A. W. Lewis, a very fine Field Events performer, while R. H. Bryan came all the way from Eastleigh to run in the 2 miles, which is enthusiasm indeed. A. T. Liffen, a former Southern sprint champion, turned out again after a two years' absence from the track and gained third place for us in the 100 Yards, with M. J. Wright of the "Poly." fourth. B. Metcalfe, a very promising sprinter, and Wright gained us further points by finishing second and third in the 220 Yards. In the 440 Yards, Syd. Jarlett ran a splendid race to beat Holmes, with W. Watts gaining third placec for us. The 880 Yards was a very good race and Len. Marchant showed a return to last season's form to clock 2 m. 3.9 s., which was very good time on such a heavy track. The result of the 1 Mile was a foregone conclusion and Frank Close won easily, but S. J. Wooderson ran well to beat Les. Cohen, although the latter was just back from a week's holiday. The 2 Miles was a race between Tom Carter and R. H. Bryan, the Hants County runner, who has recently joined us. Bryan cut out the pace at the start and then when Tom went in front tried pluckily to hang on to his man, but with Carter running in that effortless fashion of his, Bryan had to be content with second place, and here again the time was very good considering the heavy track. The 1 Mile Medley Relay, which was the final running event, saw a very close race, and Jarlett gave us the lead over the half mile stage. Elliott, of the T.C.C., made up ground on Bowers and a bad take-over between the latter and Hayes saw Holmes send off the T.C.C. man in the lead for the final quarter. Len. Marchant strode out in fine style, however, and soon caught his man and carried on to give us yet another win. In the Field Events, Charlie Melchior gained us first place in the Javelin with George Powell second, and A. W. Lewis won both the Weight and the Discus. His effort of 132 ft. in the Discus was a really fine performance, and only 10 ft. short of the English Native record. Thus on the evening we came out winners with a total of 65 points, with the T.C.C. scoring 30 and U.L. Tyrian 22. Webb who also took the handicap, with Belgrave second to Woodford Green by one point in the team race. The Highgate " 20 " 17.5.41. There being no R.W.A. "20" this year, Highgate put on a race over the same distance, which was well supported. On paper it looked a snip for the "Bels." with Jack Bidgood, A. Webb, Syd. Roberts and Bob Readman. However, as in most long walks, things didn't work out as well as expected. Jack was let down by the "snob" and had to walk in old shoes which soon began to give him trouble, and Syd. Roberts, who had not fully recovered from a bad cold, slowed up over the last five miles. The surprise of the day was Webb's splendid win, beating A. Cotton by the wide margin of 2 minutes and completing the double by also winning the handicap. For well over ten miles, it looked as though it might be anybody's race, but with about five miles to go Webb forged ahead and had no difficulty in leaving the rest of the field behind. Bob Readman went through towards the end, but only managed to reach 6th place. Woodford Green, with 2nd and 3rd places, came out winers by 1 point. Standards were awarded to all completing the course inside 3 h. 30 m., and all our walkers qualified. RESULT. Scr. Team Race.—1. Woodford Green 22 Pts. 2. Belgrave H. 23 Pts. Individual Hcp.—A. items.label: June 1941
items.sum: Walking section news of members in the Forces and the Police, Percy Wright's Belgrave News Letter, A. H. Webb's and Syd. Roberts' Police championship wins and the summer walking programme, closing with praise for the Police walkers.
items.s: Walking section news of members in the Forces and the Police, Percy Wright's Belgrave News Letter, A. H. Webb's and Syd. Roberts' Police championship wins and the summer walking programme, closing with praise for the Police walkers. Since our last number, several more of our walkers have been drawn into the ranks of H.M. Forces, and our main support now rest with our Police members who are keeping the Club Colours well to the fore. It is difficult to get news of all our men in the Forces but as far as is known, Charlie Churcher is now out East, whilst Harry is still in the Isle of Man (not interned). Joe Coleman is shooting pictures in the air. Our Hon. Handicapper has worked himself into a soft number as chauffeur-batman, and Percy Wright is now at Newport. Anyway, from the latest available information, they are all doing their utmost to encourage sport in their respective circles, and we wish them luck and a safe and speedy return. Percy Wright has started a new venture, a sort of miniature mag. which he calls " Belgrave News Letter," through which he is endeavouring to keep in touch with the boys. Although production facilities are limited, his printing press being confined to a typewriter, he is circulating as many copies as possible with a request that when finished with, they be passed on to other members and so extend the circulation. Well done Percy ! Hope you will be able to keep it up. Congratulations to A. H. Webb on winning the Highgate "20" and following up a fortnight later with the Police "24." Syd. Roberts having won the Police "10" earlier in the season, both Police Championships are now held by our members. Good work. Harry Thaxter, who showed such good form last season, unfortunately cracked up in the blitz and was invalided out of the Police. He is now back in the country recuperating and we wish him a speedy recovery. Despite present conditions, a good programme of walking was held during the winter, although it started later than usual on account of the black-out. Our Open proved a great success. Joe Coleman turned up but left his shoes in his 'plane. Co-operation between the A.A.A. and the R.W.A. has resulted in a good summer programme of racing. The A.A.A. are promoting four Open 2-Miles in conjunction with their meetings, the R.W.A. are putting on two 5-Miles walks, as last year, and London Transport are also staging a 5-Miles. Dates of these fixtures have been well circulated and should be known by all. Mid-week club fixtures have also been arranged, and it is hoped to work in one or more club handicaps for the walkers. Our Police Walkers, despite their difficult work these days, and the few walkers to remain in civil life, still keep our stock high in the Walking world. We look to them to continue to do so while the rest of us are away; and when the Service men return and link up with their old time Police friends (together with the new recruits they will have found for us); Belgrave will again set the standard of performance and sportsmanship which is synonymous with the Club name. items.label: June 1941
items.h: THE HON. SECRETARY HAS THE LAST WORD !
items.sum: Message from the Hon. Secretary, serving in the West Country, thanking those keeping the club going at home and urging serving members to stay in touch and promote athletics in their units.
items.s: THE HON. SECRETARY HAS THE LAST WORD ! Message from the Hon. Secretary, serving in the West Country, thanking those keeping the club going at home and urging serving members to stay in touch and promote athletics in their units. THE HON. SECRETARY HAS THE LAST WORD ! Although on service in the "West Countrie" (and, I'm afraid as an Hon. Secretary, a name only), I have been privileged to see this magazine of ours in manuscript form. To me it brings back a host of memories of good friends, good racing, good times, good fellowship; and no doubt it will do so to many of you. And these times will come again if it is our will that they should. When we return we shall have lost a year or two's sport; gained in experience of other things. The racing careers of some of us will be finished; but that excellent friendly Belgrave spirit will live again in all its fullness. New men will repeat old successes and perhaps gain new ones; and we who have made our small contribution to the Club's record of success—and, more important, to its reputation for scrupulous sportsmanship—will share again the happy atmosphere of friendliness and sportsmanship from which we have been obliged to turn for a while to other things. It will be a grand day when we can all get back and start working for the Belgrave Harriers again; and place the Club in an unassailable position at the head of all that is best in Athletics—the sport we have followed in all its branches, and for which we have so much affection. And now, on behalf of all of those away from the Club, I would like to express our thanks to all who are carrying on with the good work and keeping the structure of the Club intact against our return. We realize the extra calls on the time of the civilian in these difficult days; and we are glad to think that the older members are doing all they can to have things ready for an immediate crescendo of activity as soon as our serving members return. There are many to whom we are indebted, and space permits only mention of a few. Our thanks, and hopes for a speedy recovery from his present indisposition go to our President, Frank Thomson, for his work on our behalf. Our Acting Hon. Secretary's and Hon. Treasurer's efforts also demand an expression of gratitude. And speaking for the serving members once again, what is our part? Keep in touch with Club headquarters, your letters will be shown to all attending members. Write your friends also serving and keep them posted with the latest Club news. Stir up some athlete's interest in your unit. I have been able to get Sports promoted and win a race which says little for the standard of performance! Frank Elston, Percy Wright, Charlie Smart, Bill Merryman have all created interest and have teams in the making. Why not you, also? Any such interest is bound to help Athletics generally and our own Club; and we may well experience a boom at the end of the War, as followed the last. To conclude :—We're separated by large distances; but not in our thoughts and friendships [illegible] Let's regard these present days as a passing phase; and let's be determined to keep together now in spirit that we may enjoy together all that is best in sport in the years that lay ahead. A. A. HARLEY. A. A. Harley A. A. HARLEY Hon. items.label: November 1941
items.sum: Opening piece by A. A. Harley on the Gazette as the link between scattered members, the Annual General Meeting and the Belgrave spirit in wartime.
items.s: PROLOGUE. Opening piece by A. A. Harley on the Gazette as the link between scattered members, the Annual General Meeting and the Belgrave spirit in wartime. Whilst we are necessarily compelled to be so far apart from one another, this Gazette of ours becomes our greatest link. We considered it an essential of our Club life in times of peace. How much more necessary is it now that we are scattered? How glad those of us serving in H.M. Forces are to receive "The Belgravian" and to read of current happenings. And perhaps of even more importance is the fact that it stimulates us to think of all the good times of the past; and, of still greater importance, of the good times we mean to have in the future. We owe a debt of gratitude to the Club officials responsible for the production of our journal. Feelingly, I could write much on the subject of the difficulties of presenting "The Belgravian" regularly to its readers; but in these days of increased costs, scarce paper, fewer contributors, and less leisure time for its production and distribution; it is little short of a miracle that we receive our journal at all. I know that those of us who are away do appreciate all that is being done; and I would suggest that a letter of thanks and of news to our Hon. Secretary is indicated. If you are in a position to add a small subscription to help carry on the Club, so much the better. If not, still write and give the latest news of yourself; and if you are lucky enough to get "seven days" and near enough to make for your accustomed haunts, don't forget to show yourself at the Club Headquarters. Our fellow-members who are still able to train and race will be found at Wimbledon throughout the winter, and they'll welcome you for a training spin. Incidentally, we're glad to see that a Belgrave team still takes plenty of beating when it comes to a race. Our main object must be to ensure that the War is only an interruption of our efforts and activities; and that when the interruption has passed, we can carry on where we previously left off. All those we know so well, we hope to see together again, supplemented by new friends; and then away to a programme of sport and sportsmanship and all that meant so much to us, and will do so again. May it be soon! It was my good fortune, at very short notice, to be able to attend the Annual General Meeting; and it was very encouraging to find such a goodly number of real enthusiasts present. It was good, too, to hear of the past year's achievements in the face of so many difficulties; and to sense the feeling that though wars may come and go, Belgrave will survive, its friendships endure, its atheletic triumphs multiply, its sportsmanship stand the test of all time. War, and everything that follows in its train, may act temporarily as a partial brake on our progress; but it cannot stay it. We have cause for self-congratulation in that we have a Committee in being which, with the infusion of some younger blood, will spring into action and see that our Club has its rightful place in the athletic world of post-war years. And, best of all, we have a wealth of goodwill, friendship, and community of interest—which we know as the Belgrave spirit—very much alive and evinced in the letters which pass between the members. They are more widespread than usual, covering all parts of the globe; but still with the mind's eye on a corner of Belgrave Hall at Wimbledon, and treasured memories of their training, racing and social affairs with those they are proud to know as friends. It is our fervent hope that we shall know these things again in the year that is almost upon us. A. A. HARLEY. A. A. Harley A. A. HARLEY Wimbledon Belgrave Hall

items.label: November 1941
items.sum: Club notes on the second wartime Annual General Meeting, officials' changes, members' honours and family news, new members and members called to the Services.
items.s: Club notes on the second wartime Annual General Meeting, officials' changes, members' honours and family news, new members and members called to the Services. The Second Annual General Meeting of the war period has come and gone. Thirty-six members were present, one less than last year. Our President, Mr. Frank Thomson, was unable to be present owing to ill-health. In a letter to the Hon. Secretary he said: "I am very depressed at being out of touch with the Club and its activities. It is most cheering to hear that the Club funds are still in a healthy condition, and that Bill Webb is doing such fine work in keeping things going. Please remember me to the A.G.M. and express my feeling towards the welfare of the Club, which I hope one day to materially help." In a brief resumé the Acting Hon. Secretary stated that there were 376 names on the Club Register. One hundred and twenty had notified him that they had joined the Forces. Twenty-two new members had been elected during the year, but only one resignation had been received. Despite the difficult times, the past season had been very successful, and thanks were due to the Polytechnic Harriers for their support, also to those members of other clubs who had helped to make the inter-club matches a success. * * * * There was consternation on the track when Frank Webb came along one evening and announced his "calling up." Our best wishes go with you, Frank, and our heartiest thanks for all the hard work you have put in as Team Organiser and Editor. You certainly will be missed. Harry Shields valiantly came forward and volunteered to carry on the good work, despite being "so blinking busy" these days. * * * * Our hearty congratulations to our Hon. Secretary, P. O. A. A. Harley, who was married at Ickenham on September 6th. May your "double" life be long and happy! * * * * Our congratulations to our old and esteemed member Jack Bidgood upon his re-election as Chairman to the Road Walking Association (Southern Committee). As Vice-Chairman he was the natural successor to the Chairman, Alf Harley, our Hon. Secretary, when he was called to the Colours. As a side line to walking (we hope) Jack seems to favour bowls, and recently appeared in the Wimbledon Police team who won the local Hospital Bowls Tournament. * * * * Congratulations to Jim Tosh and Tiny Jarlett, who have had awarded the British Empire Medal for bravery in air raids last winter. "F.M." is already the holder of the Police Medal for Bravery and has many "mentions" to his credit. He is perhaps our oldest police member, having joined in January, 1924. Was a very successful walker and a great team man. * * * * Congratulations to Jim Tosh and Tiny Jarlett, who have had additions to their families. May I yet couple Percy's name to this par? And Jimmy Belchamber tells me he will soon be a grandpa! * * * * We welcome the following new members, and wish them every success in the future:— Sydney Blandford, U. H. D. Broadbent, Ronald Durban. * * * * Since the last issue of the Gazette the undermentioned members have notified their call to the Services:— A. C. Ball, R.N. A. H. Beaumont, R.A. R. F. Boyce, R.A.S.C. items.label: November 1941
items.sum: News gathered from letters sent by members, mostly serving in the Forces, with short quoted letters about the Belgrave News Letter.
items.s: News gathered from letters sent by members, mostly serving in the Forces, with short quoted letters about the Belgrave News Letter. Many letters have been received from members, all of whom were pleased to hear from the Club. Most "moaned" because of the lack of atheletic news in the daily and weekly press. W. R. Laing, in the Middlesex Regt., received his gazette from his pal, his own copy having been returned through the post. J. H. Thomas is in the Pay Corps at Nottingham, where he found Jack Rutland. Also been doing some running and came to Tooting one Wednesday evening to try his paces. Len Coleman, who makes frequent journeys between Oxford and London, gets no thinner! Percy Wright, still in Wales and hard at work on the B.N.L. This is Percy's pet stunt to keep all walking members in touch with one another. "Doub", still in Exeter, and doing his bit with the Exeter Harriers, who have elected him Vice-Captain. Bill Merryman, at Lichfield, on the Sports Committee of his unit. Also doing some running, but no news yet as to whether he is amongst the prizes. Bill Lucas, nr. Bury St. Edmunds. Has transferred from fighters to bombers, and awaiting his initial trip over Germany. This was at the end of August, and no further news has been received, so we hope he is safe. Our old friend, Ken O'Kell, who is at a "shadow factory" in the Midlands, sends his kind regards to all the boys, especially Bert Footer. The Hon. Treas. was especially pleased when Ken's letter arrived. Frank Webb, who has been moved from Skegness to Northern Ireland, within a few miles of Dick Towndrow, who is still winning races. Won the N.I. 3 Miles Flat Championship and other open races, and is looking forward to the Irish C. C. season. Lieut. Ron Patience, who is trying to work up some enthusiasm in the Shetlands. Syd Ring, who is on work of national importance at Cowley, Oxon. Megaphone man, Cook. Keeping himself used to the "mike" by helping at local meetings down Gloucester way. Also training as a "red cap." By the way, Arthur, what's a "blue cap"? Norman Shrubb, in Scotland, had the Welsh International Corpl. Hier as Sports Officer. Has won two medals. Teddy Read, the sprinter, sent to Canada, and a letter is eagerly awaited. Lieut. Bradman, in Norfolk, where he has been showing a clean pair of heels in the Battalion Sports. Frank Elson, who has definitely got a big move on down in Wiltshire. Corpl. Dumbrill, in Hampshire, also met Joe Binks lecturing the troops. Albert Wattam, Lincolnshire and Brighton road fame, writes:—"My old place was practically destroyed by enemy action in November last." Our deepest sympathies, Albert, but we are very pleased that you are still standing up and smiling. Victor Reynolds, late of Brixton, now with the East Yorks, in the Middle East, sends his very best wishes to the Club and its members, and hopes to be with them in the near future. "Pidgeon" Bird, now at St. Annes-on-Sea, and enjoying himself. Stimpson, is in the Orkneys. Recovered from his broken leg, and is starting training again. Brian Rowe, who is at Aldershot with an Officers Cadet Training Battalion. P. N. Roberts, now in the R.A.F. in Salop. G. F. Long, in the Marines at Havant. Says he has had quite a successful time running, won 3 Miles Cross Country, 440, 880, and Mile, and in the winning relay team. Not all on the same day, though! Now a Corporal. Congrats! Also says he has visited our one and only Tommy Green, who is very busy with the Home Guard. We understand that Bill Orton is likely to proceed overseas any moment, and that Joe Daly and Les Bennett are on their way. News from Bill Jones in Yorkshire. "I am turning out once a week to do a mixed cross-country and road-running training, mainly to give the Club colours an airing. The village certainly sat up and took notice. The "Signals" had some Sports yesterday, and the 100 and 220 were won by Smith, a 'Belgravian.' Congrats, Smith—but which one are you? Unsolicited Testimonial. From a member "who is particularly interested in the Club, but one who has little time for active sport":— "I should like to congratulate you on the splendid idea of the Belgrave News Letter." C.R. Another. "If my name appears in the walking game again, I must blame your News Letter for bringing me out of retirement." C.S. From Aberystwyth. "I went for a 3½ miles spin and quite a lot of chaps came out to watch." "BILL." W. R. Laing W. R. Laing in the Middlesex Regt. J. H. Thomas J. H. items.sum: Report and results of the 21 June 1941 relay and field events match at Imber Court between the Royal Navy and Marines, 52nd Welsh Guards, Metropolitan Police and Belgrave Harriers.
items.s: At Imber Court. Report and results of the 21 June 1941 relay and field events match at Imber Court between the Royal Navy and Marines, 52nd Welsh Guards, Metropolitan Police and Belgrave Harriers. On Saturday, June 21st, 1941, in a match between the Royal Navy and Marines (Portsmouth), 52nd Batt. Welsh Guards, Metropolitan Police and Belgrave Harriers. Unfortunately, this meeting clashed with the Polytechnic at Chiswick, therefore we had some difficulty in arranging teams, as the events turned out to be on a relay system. As the afternoon went on we were able to fill in the vacant places by the following:— Aberton, Johnstone (Q.P.H.); W. Day (I.V.H.); L. Lewis (Epsom H.); and J. S. Rugman (Shaftesbury A.C.); which we greatly appreciate for their help. Among the notable performances for us was F. R. Webb's splendid half mile of 2 mins. 3 secs. in the 1½ Miles Relay (well ran, Frank!); J. S. Rugman's long jump, with a leap of 21ft. 2in.; Melchoir (Javelin) with a throw of 178ft. 4in.; and L. Lewis (Weight) with a putt of 37ft. 8¾in. The meeting was held under splendid conditions, and some keen racing was seen in all events. The Field events were also keenly contested, followed by a social evening, which was well patronised. The results of the meeting are as follows:— 4 × 110 Yards Relay.—1, M.P.; 2, Bels.; 3, R.N. & H. items.label: November 1941
items.sum: Report and results of the North of Thames v. South of Thames match at Tooting Bec Track on 16 July, won by the South 56 points to 55.
items.s: North v. South. Report and results of the North of Thames v. South of Thames match at Tooting Bec Track on 16 July, won by the South 56 points to 55. A very interesting match was held at Tooting Bec Track on Wednesday, 16th July. As our original fixture, which was with the Combined Clubs and Shaftesbury Harriers, had been cancelled by the former, who, as they put it, could not field a team to match our strength, our Running Hon. Sec. decided to ask the Shaftesbury Hon. Sec., A. J. C. Kendall, to raise a team representing the North of Thames, while our own boys, plus a few additions, made up the South of Thames side. The meeting proved a great success, and it was immediately decided to have a return match at Parliament Hill Track in a few weeks' time. The following clubs had members competing, so it can be truly said to be a representative affair. For the South:—Belgrave H., Mitcham A.C., Metropolitan Police A.C., London Paper Mills, and Eastleigh A.C.; while for the North:—Shaftesbury H., Polytechnic H., Woodford Green A.C., Essex Beagles, Thames Valley H., Southgate H., Enfield A.C., Finchley H., North London H., and Vale of Aylesbury A.C. An international flavour was also imparted by the presence of a Czecho-Slovakian who ran in the 2 miles, an Austrian in the Discus, and a Polish athlete in the high jump. Also competing were two schoolboy athletes—M. H. Broadbent, of Wallington County School, and J. L. Gowans, of the Whitgift Middle School—and they proved a tower of strength to the South side. Broadbent, who had gained second place in the Southern Junior 220 yards, ran extremely well to win both the 100 and the 220 yards match events, and his smooth style of running is very reminiscent of C. B. Holmes, and as Broadbent is only 16 years of age, he may well reach the very highest honours and looks an Olympic star in the making. W. H. Bowers, of our own club, also showed improved form to gain second place in the 100 yards, but our other runner in the 220, A. T. Liffen, unfortunately pulled a muscle and had to drop out of the race. The 880 yards was a very good race, and Len Marchant cut out a very fast pace and led at the bell in 57 seconds, a fact which told on him when it came to the finish, and W. Elliott came by him in the straight, while he also lost second place on the post to M. T. Forde, and thus the North gained the first two places. In the 440 yards Syd Jarlett was opposed by A. C. Pettit, who is a City of London policeman, and although the latter ran well, he could not get on terms with Jarlett, who led throughout. Third place was taken by W. H. Watts, a very persevering runner who is assisting us this season. The 2 miles was a very steady affair for the first mile, when Tom Carter led with the Czech runner at his shoulder. The pace then warmed up, and the Czech runner fell behind the leading bunch, which consisted of Carter, Worboys, Attryde, Fox, and Bettiss. With 200 yards to go, Attryde went into the lead with huge strides, with Worboys second, and Tom Carter striving to overtake the leading pair. He could not do it, however, and so the North gained yet another 8—1 victory. Points scored: 5—3—1 for the first three places in each event, with the Relay being a 3—0 affair. As the 2 miles was being run who should turn up but R. H. Bryan, who had come all the way from Southampton to run in this race. He very sportingly agreed to turn out in the 1 mile, which was later in the programme, and immediately his race was over, he left to catch his return train home, and so was at the meeting about half an hour only, and yet was willing to make the long journey just for the run, which to our mind shows the perfect sportsman and a true-blue amateur. He found the pace in the Mile a bit too fast for him, but finished a very creditable fourth, and G. Morris just held off Les Cohen to win a good race. H. Pascoe, who has had a very successful season in Open Mile Handicaps, having gained a place in each one held, finished third just in front of Bryan. Thus on the running events the North were slightly in front on points, but our Field event men, led by D. L. Grigg, pulled back the lost ground by a series of good performances. A. J. Ford won the High Jump with 5ft. 8in., a really fine jump, actually he went over this height and then called it a day. J. L. Gowans, who won the Southern Junior High Jump, was second with 5ft. 3in., and here again this lad shows wonderful possibilities. Charlie Melchoir won the Javelin Throw with 167 ft. and two more "Bels" were second and third, although the South scored the first two places only. D. L. Grigg, now a sergeant in the Metropolitan Police, and who was recently awarded the George Medal, was first in the Discus with a throw of 125ft. 6in., and he also gained second place in the Weight Putt being beaten by 1¾ins. for first place. J. H. Quarton, who had travelled up from Dartford, was third in the Weight and gained the same position for the Long Jump. Also in the programme was a 2 Miles Walk, and thanks to A. D. McSweeney, who is doing great work as Hon. Secretary and Treasurer of the Southern Committee of the Road Walking Association, a fine field of about 30 walkers turned out. All clubs were represented, and Jack Rutland obtained leave to be there, while S. D. Inspector Bidgood was also present, together with many other of our Police walkers. The race was won by M. J. Fisher, with H. D. Neilson second, and G. Lawson third, and the time was quite creditable. The 1 Mile Medley Relay resulted in an easy win for the North, and this was mainly due to D. G. Wilson, who ran the half-mile stage for them and gave his team a good lead. At this stage the South led by 55 points to 47, but when the result of the Long Jump was ascertained, giving the North an 8—1 win, the final score was South 56 and the North 55. Thus ended a most interesting and enjoyable meeting, and all taking part together with the officials present are to be thanked for their efforts. items.sum: Report and results of the 26 July track match at Southall in which a Belgrave-Poly. team finished second to the West Middlesex Triangle, ahead of the Metropolitan Police and Watford Harriers.
items.s: Match at Southall. Report and results of the 26 July track match at Southall in which a Belgrave-Poly. team finished second to the West Middlesex Triangle, ahead of the Metropolitan Police and Watford Harriers. On July 26th at Southall we met teams from the Metropolitan Police, Watford Harriers and the local club, the West Middlesex Triangle. There were no field events, it being a purely track meeting, and they had first and second string races with the 1 Mile and 3 Miles being run on the team principle. In the 100 Yards, Bill Bowers was third, with M. J. Wright taking fourth place, and in the first of the 220 Yards races Bowers finished second to Wigley of the Triangle, but in the second race Wright won, beating Littler of the home club. Watts ran a good race to finish second to Ensor in the first string 440 Yards, and Metcalfe put up a good performance in running beyond his usual distance, to finish second in the second race. W. R. Moody, of the Police, won the 880 Yards, with Len Marchant beating the present Police Champion, R. Ayton, to take second place. The 1 Mile saw A. J. Collyer the ex-A.A.A. Champion, making a welcome re-appearance on the track, but he was beaten by D. G. Wilson, the Poly. miler, in 4 min. 26 secs., with A. Hughes of the Triangle third. The team race resulted in a win for the Belgrave-Poly. boys. Les Cohen ran a splendid race in the 3 Miles to beat Maurice Bingham, who was running for the Triangle, and the latter won the team race. The 1 Mile Medley Relay resulted in a win for the Police, with our lads second and the Triangle third. Owing to the Watford boys arriving late, they were only able to take part in a few events, which accounts for their small score of points. We were beaten by the small margin of 3 points, but had a really enjoyable fixture, and that is what counts most!
