items.sum: Reports of the five Southern Counties C.C.A. team races of the season: Belgrave Hall (17 Oct., A and B teams 1st and 2nd), Ruislip (14 Nov., 2nd to Finchley), Epsom (12 Dec., won), Chingford (20 Feb., won, Herbert first) and Hayes (27 Mar., 2nd to the Fire Force, Hoath first); the first race lists 15 runners though it says only 14 members ran, and the last lists 13 though nine members turned up.
items.s: SOUTHERN COUNTIES C.C.A. Reports of the five Southern Counties C.C.A. team races of the season: Belgrave Hall (17 Oct., A and B teams 1st and 2nd), Ruislip (14 Nov., 2nd to Finchley), Epsom (12 Dec., won), Chingford (20 Feb., won, Herbert first) and Hayes (27 Mar., 2nd to the Fire Force, Hoath first); the first race lists 15 runners though it says only 14 members ran, and the last lists 13 though nine members turned up. Five team races were promoted by this Association during the season. The first from Belgrave Hall on October 17th, attracted an entry from 17 teams and 97 competitors started. The day was mild with a slight wind and the ground was rather dry and hard, and the usual 5 miles course was used. Three teams had been entered by the Club but only 14 members turned up to run. The individual race was won by Richards of Mitcham in 30.25, Carter being 2nd, 25 seconds behind. Cohen was 3rd, 31.45; Taylor 7th, 31.45; Speight 8th, 31.47; Walker 11th; 31.58; Tobin 13th, 32.7; Durrant 18th, 32.16; Jarlett 21st, 32.24; Morrell 22nd, 32.26; C. T. Beer 27th, 32.36; Shields 36th, 33.14; McDonald 47th, 34.17; Harding 50th, 34.26 Owen 75th, 35.56 and Woodard 76th, 36.0 However with 4 aside scoring we had the pleasure of finishing first and second in the team race, the "A" team scoring 20 points and the "B" team 79 points. * * * * The second race was held on November 14th at Ruislip over the Finchley Harriers 5 miles course, but which, on the clock, was under the scheduled distance. The large number of starters, 112, the best field to date, made the scoring more open, and the final tally found us beaten by the home club by 4 points, the scores being 35 to 39 for 4 aside. The "B" team were 5th with 99 points. Pat Parker made one of his rare appearances and although short of a little pep, finished 7th. Micky Walker ran well to gain 15th place and Jimmy Green was very pleased with himself and his 19th position. "Stimmo" and Beer, both on short leave, were, however, hardly fit enough for the fast course. Result: 1, Carter, 27.48; 3, Hoath (N.F.S.) 28.7; 7, Parker, 28.26; 15, Walker, 28.58; 16 Speaight, 28.59; 19, Green, 29.7; 25 Shaw, 29.36; 27, Shields, 29.43; 28, Morrell, 29.47; 40, Stimpson, 30.49; 41, Taylor, 30.50; 53, Beer, 31.3. * * * * The third race of the series was held at Epsom under the auspices of the Epsom Harriers on December 12th. The best entry to date had been received and 145 runners comprising 24 teams turned out. The estimated distance was 5 miles but the time of the winner (32m. 6s.) would make the distance perhaps nearer 5½ miles. The course was a good one, nearly all grassland and not very heavy, although wet on top. We welcomed the re-appearance of Len Herbert, Ted Stimpson, and Charlie Smart, all home on short leave, and also a newcomer Sam Beer, who in this his first cross-country race for a year or more, and without any serious training, finished 26th. Jimmy Green also ran very well after his recent illness. The team were very anxious to wipe out their defeat at Ruislip and did so by finishing the scoring four in the first 21 places, the scores being 43 points to 56 of the second team. Len Herbert and Tom Carter finished together in the third place in 32m. 46s., and in true Belgrave spirit Tom waived any claim to the 3rd medal and it was handed to Len who had not previously won a Southern medal. Other positions were 14th, Hoath, 33.44; 15, Tobin, 33.48; 21, Green, 33.59; 23, Speaight, 34.1; 26, S. J. Beer, 34.8; 27, Stimpson, 34.9; 28; Peck, 34.10; 40, Smart, 34.54; 47, Shaw, 35.25; 48, Shields, 35.28; 51, Taylor, 35.32; 61, Morrell, 36.0; 89, McDonald, 37.25; 91, Clarke Spencer, 37.27; 116, Woodward, 39.7. The "B" team were placed 8th with 161 points. * * * * The fourth race on February 20th found a merry party at Butlers Retreat, Chingford, and the 7½ miles course was mapped out into 3 laps of undulating grassland, and 15 members were amongst the 83 starters. Bill Speaight, having been on duty the previous night, was not up to the mark, and retired after the first lap, and Andy Gray twisted his ankle in the last lap and limped back home. At the end of the first lap Carter and Hoath were leading, but Carter appeared far from comfortable. Brickwood led in the next lap with Hoath still second, Herbert was 3rd and Carter had dropped back to 4th. The finish saw Herbert in front clocking 42.42; Hoath 2nd, 42.49; Carter 4th, 43.3; Tobin 15th, 44.44; Bryan 17th, 44.49; Cohen 18th, 45.4; Peck 21st, 45.15; Shields 25th, 45.34; Morrell 40th, 47.16; Spencer 55th, 49.25; White 63rd, 50.39 and Jannaway 70th, 53.30. The team were placed first, scoring 38 points. * * * * The last of these races was held over the Blackheath Harriers 7½ miles course at Hayes on 27th March. Owing to the "exigencies of the service" we were short of both service and civil members. However nine members (and Mrs. and Miss Morrell) turned up and saw a strong Fire Force team beat us with a score of 31 to 51 points. Congratulations, Firemen—it's not out of your turn. Fireman Hoath (also a Bel) won a splendid race, winning by 1¼ minutes, clocking 44.35. items.s: CLUB 3-MILES ROAD RACE HANDICAP. Report and result of the club 3 miles road race handicap round the Common, won by G. Durrant off 1.45 from 23 starters, with George Still, 65 next birthday, 7th off the limit mark. This race was, as usual, held the week following the opening run of our winter season, and a good field was seen out. George Still, that G.O.M. of our running section, who is 65 next birthday, was on the limit mark of 5m. 15s. and finished 7th in the race. The race was won by a very promising young runner, G. Durrant, who is a protege of Syd Jarlett's, and he made good use of his 1.45 start to work his way through the long markers and come home a good winner. Prominent among the back-markers were Tom Carter, R. H. Bryan who came up from Eastleigh, Les Cohen and Art Penny, and only a few seconds divided them when actual times were worked out. The scratch man, L. W. Herbert, was unable to be present, but a field of 23 starters must be considered very good in these rather difficult times. We used the old 3 mile course round the Common and by the Windmill, but lengthened the course by starting at the bottom of Lauriston Road, although finishing at the top of the Common, as was usual in the past. items.s: METROPOLITAN POLICE A.C. Reports of two matches with the Metropolitan Police A.C.: at Hayes, Kent on 28th November (with London Fire Services and Thames Valley Harriers), won by Belgrave with Tom Carter breaking the course record, and the return at Belgrave Hall on 30th January, won 115 to 185; the Hayes scores as printed (8 aside 73, 5 aside 35) do not match the positions listed. From their sports headquarters at Hayes, Kent, on Saturday, Nov. 28th, and in which the London Fire Services and Thames Valley Harriers participated. The course was the usual one used by the Police and is about 4¾ miles. Tom Carter, taking the lead from the start, went away all on his own and was never headed, to eventually finish in 25.40, knocking 15 seconds off the previous best time for the course. We were pleased to welcome George Murray home on 10 days leave, but very obviously short of training. Result: 1, Carter, 25.40; 5, Speaight; 6, Main; 10, Tobin; 12, Morrell; 13, Shaw; 14, Shields; 17, Taylor; 20, Murray. Scores: 8 aside. Belgrave, 73; L.F.S., 99; Police, 128. 5 aside. Secretary paid us the compliment of giving them perhaps the best and happiest run of the season. They turned up 15 competitors and several supporters, but being without their cracks were beaten with a score of 115 to 185 points, 12 aside scoring. The course was laid over the Club "7" and was very wet in consequence of heavy rains in the morning. Championship, won by Tom Carter from George Hoath, the Bels winning 89 to 121. At Belgrave Hall on 20th March, in which the British Workers combined their C.C. Championship. The Club 5 miles course was used, and nearly 40 runners faced the starter. The race resolved into a duel between Tom Carter and George Hoath, and on entering the finishing field both were fighting every inch, first Tom and then George in front, and Tom putting in a tremendous finish just landed home first by about 7 yards in 29.3. items.s: FINCHLEY "20." Report of the Finchley 20 miles road race at Ruislip on 10th April, where Mick Walker was a few yards behind Richards (Mitcham), who set a course record, and Walker, Ring and Mitchell took second team prizes. At Ruislip on 10th April. At about 7 miles Sid Ring had a substantial lead, but at about 15, Richards (Mitcham) with Mick Walker in attendance, were in front. Despite every effort, Mick was unable to pass Richards, but pushed him to a record for the course, Mick being a matter of a few yards behind in 2 hrs. 49 secs., a time which in previous years would have won the race. Ring was 7th in 2 hrs. 7 mins. 25 secs; Bert Mitchell 13th, 2 hrs. 14 mins. 16 secs.; and Fred White 23rd in 2hrs. 24 mins. Walker, Ring and Mitchell took second prizes in the team race. items.s: MIDDLESEX SENIOR C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP. Report of the Middlesex Senior C.C. Championship at Ruislip on January 2nd, where a depleted Cadogan A.C. team lost third place on time aggregate and David Mains was 3rd in the Junior Championship. So many members with a Middlesex qualification being in the Services and unable to obtain leave, a very depleted team had to do service for Cadogan A.C. at Ruislip on January 2nd. Although Tobin (8), Shields (13) and Taylor (14) scored equal points, 34, with Thames Valley Harriers, they lost third place on time aggregate. David Mains, running as a Belgravian, was placed 3rd in the Junior Championship, 35 secs. behind the winner. Tobin Tobin 8th, scoring for Cadogan A.C. Shields Shields 13th, scoring for Cadogan A.C. Taylor Taylor 14th, scoring for Cadogan A.C. David Mains David Mains 3rd in the Middlesex Junior Championship, 35 secs. behind the winner Middlesex Cross Country Championships Ruislip Cadogan A.C. items.label: May 1943
items.sum: Walking section notes by Syd. Robert on the winter season: new walkers recruited, open handicap successes, the Belgrave Open, inter-club matches with Highgate and Surrey A.C., the Highgate one-hour walk, the Surrey and Middlesex county walks, the B.W.S.A. 10 Miles, Bob Readman's Police 10 Miles win and Syd Roberts' Met. 15 win.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Walking section notes by Syd. Robert on the winter season: new walkers recruited, open handicap successes, the Belgrave Open, inter-club matches with Highgate and Surrey A.C., the Highgate one-hour walk, the Surrey and Middlesex county walks, the B.W.S.A. 10 Miles, Bob Readman's Police 10 Miles win and Syd Roberts' Met. 15 win. Since our last issue no fewer than twelve walkers have joined our ranks, eight of whom have been recruited from our old friends the Police, and for which our thanks are mainly due to Bob Readman. They also include Tommy Green's boy, who we have not yet had the pleasure of seeing on the road; L. Kennett and F. Joels, both youngsters; and J. Robins, who actually joined the Club in 1939, but has apparently not been active until just recently. Such progress in these difficult times is sure proof of the popularity both of the Club and the sport. Now is the time to start forming a nucleus of a strong post-war team, and the keenness which is being displayed by all concerned leaves no doubt whatever that when the regular championships are resumed, the Belgrave colours will be well to the fore. Our new members have already been giving good accounts of themselves in the Open handicaps, Norman Dyne getting a 1st and 2nd in the Highgate and Police Opens respectively, and J. Robins and H. Rouse 2nd and 3rd in our own open. Unfortunately in two instances the qualifying period of three months had not elapsed, and both Dyne and Rouse were, on different occasions, barred from inclusion in the team, thus robbing us of team handicap placings. Norman Dyne is certainly making rapid progress for his first season and looks like being one of our top liners. Our own Open gave us a chance of showing that we can still field a winning scratch team with really strong opposition. Jack Rutland was fitter than he has been for a long time, and finished 4th, young Mac walked well to finish 5th, and Harry Churcher, who has recently been posted nearer to London and got in some quick training, finished 7th, thus giving us three in the first seven, a little more like old times. As a war-time measure, to meet the wishes of the judges, who are now unable to provide their own transport, a new course was used, cutting out the long three-mile circuit round the hills. The entry 124 was one of the highest of the season and included 29 of our own club. Unfortunately, Charlie Redgrave was unable to get down and Frank Elson had to return to duty the day before the race. Nevertheless we were still able to field four teams. J. Robins, who has already received mention, being an unknown quantity, was not seriously considered for the handicap team, but surprised everyone, including the handicappers, by finishing second, only two seconds outside the winner's time. H. J. Rouse, another newcomer, also did very well to take 3rd handicap prize. A recurrence of the possibility of robbing ourselves of the scratch team race by an error in declaring the teams, was eliminated this year by the new arrangement of not declaring a scratch team, the first three men to finish of any club being counted for that purpose. Percy Wright still continues to do good work with the B.N.L., and now has another new idea, namely collecting Airgraphs, for which he has a market at 1/- a time. With the proceeds, which I understand are getting quite considerable, he hopes to acquire a cup, to be called the "Overseas Cup," for some sort of competition among club members. So if you get any Airgraphs don't forget to send them along to Percy. Opens having taken up such a large part of the winter programme, not much opportunity has been left for inter-club matches. Two matches, however, were arranged with Highgate Harriers and Surrey A.C. respectively. In November Highgate fielded quite a strong team, and although Eddie Staker did not compete, D. H. Christie-Murray (Second Claim) was able to assist our opponents. Charlie Redgrave was fortunately down that week-end, also E. Jury, both of whom walked well, and we came out winners by 103 points to 107. A Club Handicap was held in conjunction, and once again young Mac managed to pull it off, with Doub (walking again) 2nd and Stan Goold 3rd. In January Surrey A.C. came to Wimbledon with a strong team and just managed to beat us by one point, the score being 85 point to 86. Highgate Harriers organised a one-hour walk at Parliament Hill Fields in October on similar lines to the race put on by us a couple of years ago. Certificates were awarded to all those completing 6 miles or more in the hour, and ten of our walkers qualified, Syd Roberts and Bob Readman being the only two to cover more than seven miles, Jury, Goold and Halls being within a quarter of a mile. Our Surrey County team this year did not come up to expectations. R. McMullen, individual holder, had a bad time and dropped back over the last three miles to finish 5th, double honours being taken by Surrey A.C. with C. Morris 1st and a team score of 21 points to 22 of Surrey W.C. and ours of 36. A week later, our Middlesex walkers (Cadogan A.C.) met with no greater success. Highgate Harriers, who in addition to practically all their first claim men, also had the assistance of D. H. Christie-Murray (S.W.C.) and R. Andrews (Woodford Green) split their fast men into two teams and took 1st and 2nd team placings. We tied with Enfield for 3rd place, but as Enfield's aggregate time was 2 seconds less than ours, they were awarded third place medals. The following week we once again came into our own, when in the B.W.S.A. 10 Miles Open, we won our second scratch team race of the season. The longer distance apparently suited our walkers, the scoring three being Bod Readman, Syd Roberts and Bert Webb. All three showed considerable improvement over recent performances, and in addition to winning the scratch race, the same three comprised the 2nd Handicap Team, and Syd Roberts was placed 2nd in the individual handicap. Quite a successful day for the Club. Once again (the third time in the last four years) the Police 10 Miles Championship was won by one of our walkers, this time Bob Readman. Bob has always been well up in this race and has been placed on numerous occasions. His time, 80.49, is the second fastest for the course and under half a minute outside the record. Backing him up, in third place, was another of our walkers, Bert Webb. Perhaps the biggest surprise of the season was Syd Roberts' win in the Met. 15 at Regents Park on 17th April. After a very steady start over the first five miles, he went through the field, eventually taking the lead about a mile and a half from home to win quite comfortably by nearly a minute. With Bert Webb in third place and Bob Readman sixth, we took double honours in the scratch race. In addition Jack Bidgood was placed 2nd in the handicap and the Club 2nd in the Team Handicap. And so we come to the end of another winter season, one of our most successful since the outbreak of war, not only as regards the performances of our walkers, but also our increased membership. We hope that the small successes recorded here will hearten our members who are away from home and enable them to look forward to the time when, back with their clubmates, they too will help to carry the maroon and amber to even greater success. To all our walkers at home and abroad, we send greetings and a renewed wish for a safe and speedy return. Syd. Robert Syd. Robert byline printed "By Syd. Robert." items.sum: Short report of the Highgate Open 20 miles walk on 8/5/43, where Syd Roberts was second and Belgrave won the scratch team race for the fourth time in succession.
items.s: HIGHGATE OPEN 20: 8/5/43. Short report of the Highgate Open 20 miles walk on 8/5/43, where Syd Roberts was second and Belgrave won the scratch team race for the fourth time in succession. Syd Roberts, maintaining his recent return to form, walked a good race to finish second to Norman Burt (S.W.C.). Once again, our fourth in succession, we won the Scratch Team Race. Unfortunately, Bert Webb was unable to turn out, but his place was ably filled by Percy Wright, who was representing the Club for the first time in a distance race. With Roberts 2nd, Bob Readman 8th, Percy 11th, and Jack Bidgood 15th, we totalled 36 pts. to the 47 of Surrey W.C. In addition to the scoring four, Jack Rutland and Tug Wilson completed the course inside the time standard of 3 hours 20 minutes. items.label: May 1943
items.sum: Field events notes by T. C. Jones looking ahead to the coming season: the throwers and jumpers expected, Ron Jeal's move to Manchester A.C., Skelley's hoped-for return, juniors in the high and long jumps, A.A.A. field events handicaps and a junior high jump handicap.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP. Field events notes by T. C. Jones looking ahead to the coming season: the throwers and jumpers expected, Ron Jeal's move to Manchester A.C., Skelley's hoped-for return, juniors in the high and long jumps, A.A.A. field events handicaps and a junior high jump handicap. In the coming season it is hoped to have the help of most of the "boys" who did so well last season, including genial Pat Ridge for the Shot and Discus, Charlie Melchior, evergreen George Powell, and L. J. Higgins, the Javelin trio, and Jack Quanton from Dartford in the Long Jump, Shot and Discus. Unfortunately, we shall not have the services of Ron Jeal in the Javelin. He has been transferred and will be doing his stuff with the Manchester A.C. of which club he has become a second-claim member. He was at one time one of our trio of 160 footers at this event, and it is hoped he will be able to show the same form to the Northerners. It is believed that Skelley, who until he had a motor-cycle accident in 1939 had shown 22 feet in the Long Jump once or twice, hopes to be able to turn out again when his Forces duties permit. We shall certainly look forward to seeing him in the teams again. In the High Jump it seems that we shall still have to rely on the Juniors, but as there are a number who were showing promise last season, perhaps with more training and competition some of them will be able to reach 5ft. 6in. or even higher. The Long Jump is an event which our present Juniors seem to shun. Some of them, with some sprinting ability, should be able to do quite good performances with training and competition. In this event it is hoped we shall have the services of Frank Simmons and our Field Events Captain to back up Jack Quanton. The A.A.A. are again including a number of handicaps for Field Events men at the meetings on the following dates at which these events will take place. Our Fields Event Captain would be glad to meet any Juniors who are interested in Field Events, and will endeavour to help them. Don't forget, Juniors, we are holding a High Jump handicap for you during the season. See fixture list for the date. T. C. JONES. items.sum: Notice reminding members that the free magazine depends on prompt payment of the eight-shilling annual subscription.
items.s: £. S. D. Notice reminding members that the free magazine depends on prompt payment of the eight-shilling annual subscription. Yes, as previously hinted, the delicate question of subscriptions is now being brought up. For the Club to carry on with the good work recorded in this issue it is essential that our finances should be sound. Indeed, the production of the "Belgravian" presents our Hon. Treasurer with a tidy bill. The magazine is free to all members. It used to cost a few pence, but a few years ago the annual subscription was increased to eight shillings inclusive. Therefore the receipt of this magazine implies that the member is all-square with the Hon. Treasurer. Remember, then, that the present and future prospects of the Club depend in no small way on the prompt and regular payment of subscriptions.

items.label: May 1943
items.sum: Obituary of Lieutenant Frank William (Billy) Pritchard, killed in action in North Africa, with sympathies to members on family bereavements and a tribute to W. F. May of the London Vidarians W.C.
items.s: OBITUARY. Obituary of Lieutenant Frank William (Billy) Pritchard, killed in action in North Africa, with sympathies to members on family bereavements and a tribute to W. F. May of the London Vidarians W.C. It is with deep regret that we have to announce the death of Frank William (Billy) Pritchard. Billy was a Lieutenant in the Anti-Tank Regt. and was killed action in North Africa on November 26th. Billy will be remembered mostly by the track members, as he was a sprinter by merit. Although not outstanding, he was consistent and could always be relied upon to put up a good performance. * * * * Our sympathies are extended to our old and esteemed Charlie Cook upon the loss of his wife. To Stan Blundon, whose father was killed in a dockside accident, and to Frank Thomson, our late President, upon the loss of his wife after a long and tedious illness. Mr. W. F. May, who passed away in his sleep during January. Mr. May was the founder of the London Vidarians W.C. and a tower of strength in the walking world. Had a soft spot for Belgrave. Only a few days previous to his death, in thanking Alf Harley for the "Belgravian" wrote: "A dashed good number. I always read it from cover to cover. My congratulations." items.label: October 1943
items.sum: Editorial reviewing Belgrave's fourth war-time track season, explaining why members' letters and results fill the issue, and thanking the suppliers of news.
items.s: EDITORIAL. Editorial reviewing Belgrave's fourth war-time track season, explaining why members' letters and results fill the issue, and thanking the suppliers of news. The fourth war-time track season has seen Belgrave to the fore, and performances have, all things considered, maintained a very high level. Our mainstays have been first and foremost Club Matches, with Open and "Holidays at Home" Meetings providing handicap and scratch events. Many familiar names have disappeared or have appeared at long intervals in the results, but new names have taken their places, and we can be assured of a strong and keen nucleus for future teams. Many of our absent friends have written to us, and their news, so eagerly awaited and read by their Clubmates, occupies a large portion of this issue. Add to this the results, read and re-read by members thousands of miles from Tooting and Wimbledon, and we get little room for those witty and saucy articles which members used to write. It is hoped, therefore, that it will not read too much like a catalogue or time table. If it does, the only suggestion is to take it in small doses, the paper rationing allows of no sugar for the pill! Finally, a word of thanks to the chief supplier of "copy," Harry Parker, and to Ernie Duffett, Syd Roberts and Charlie Jones for the news from their respective sections. items.label: October 1943
items.sum: The Hon. Secretary's notes: thanks to officials, Polytechnic Harriers and the Supporters' Club, appeals for letters, vests and signing the attendance book, a letter from Canadian R. A. Abel, R.W.A. committee news and Charles Briggs's posting to North Africa.
items.s: THE HON. SECRETARY REPORTS. The Hon. Secretary's notes: thanks to officials, Polytechnic Harriers and the Supporters' Club, appeals for letters, vests and signing the attendance book, a letter from Canadian R. A. Abel, R.W.A. committee news and Charles Briggs's posting to North Africa. Thanks must be given to all of those members who gave their time to officiate at our meetings at Tooting during the season. I'm not going to mention any names in case I miss anybody. There are still many members serving in the Forces who have not written to the Club. The Hon. Secretary would welcome letters. News of others revives past pleasures and good times had with the Club, so just write a few odd lines. If you have not got the Hon. Secretary's address write to him at Belgrave Hall. The Attendance Book has been placed in Belgrave Hall for your benefit. It helps the sectional Hon. Secretaries to know who are turning up for training and also gives us a guide to the numbers using the Hall. Our ration allowance is not too big, and if proof of numbers can be given, perhaps a bigger allowance could be obtained. So don't forget to sign the Book. WANTED: Club vests. New ones are now unobtainable, so if you have a spare one don't let the moths eat it up, let the Hon. Secretary have it to pass on to one of our new members. Belgrave Hall will be open on Wednesday evenings. It is most essential that white clothing should be worn during black-out. We are most grateful to the Polytechnic Harriers for the help that their members have been to us during the Track Season, particularly Metcalfe and Maurice Wright. The services of Doug. Wilson were not always available owing to many calls on him by Jack Crump for representative matches. We hope to have the pleasure of the Poly C.C. runners and walkers at Belgrave Hall during the winter season. We have to record our most sincere thanks and appreciation for the continued success of the Supporters' Club. This is almost entirely due to the hard labours of Les Cohen; assisted by Mrs. Cohen. Between them they are largely responsible for a considerable portion of the Club's income. So thank you both, keep it going! A very interesting letter was recently received from R. A. Abel, who was with the Canadians when they visited us at Belgrave Hall in February, 1942. Abel was first man home for the Canadians, and was presented with a Club Spoon as a momento. In sending his regards to the Club, he wants a copy of the photograph taken that day. Can any member oblige? Members may also be interested to know that the Canadian Officer, Lt.-Col. La Blatt, who started the race, led the assault on the Casino in the Dieppe raid. At the A.G.M. of the R.W.A. Southern Committee, held in September, Syd Roberts was re-elected to the Committee. Frank Thomson, Alf Harley and Jack Bidgood are past Chairmen, so we are well represented. One of our walkers of a dozen or so years ago, Charles Briggs, has been sent to N. Africa on Police Administrative work with the rank of Colonel. Metcalfe Metcalfe helped Belgrave during the track season Maurice Wright Maurice Wright helped Belgrave during the track season Doug. items.sum: Club notes on school successes by younger members, members' representative honours, and Walton A.C.'s new Club Gazette.
items.s: Club notes on school successes by younger members, members' representative honours, and Walton A.C.'s new Club Gazette. Two of our younger members, from Sutton County School, have scored successes. Ken Cuff won the School C.C. Race, and Clifford Hopes the Under 15 Surrey Schools 440 Yards Championship. A number of our members have gained representative honours during the season both for Regional Teams, South, Midlands, Services Teams, and the A.A.A. Amongst those so honoured are Les Cohen, Charlie Smart, Stan Botwright, Len Marchant, Len Herbert, Tom Carter, Syd Jarlett, Charlie Melchoir, Wally Watts, T. R. Jover. Our good neighbours Walton A.C. have blossomed forth with a Club Gazette. Paper restrictions make it a concise record of the Club's fixtures, headed by a brief Editorial. It records a good year's work, including a C.C. win over a Belgrave Junior team. We wish their Gazette every success, and hope that they will soon be allowed more paper for a little convivial ink-slinging! Ken Cuff Ken Cuff won the Sutton County School C.C. items.label: October 1943
items.sum: Paragraph-by-paragraph news of members, many serving in the Forces overseas: postings, wounds, prisoners of war, marriages, races and letters home.
items.s: NEWS OF MEMBERS. Paragraph-by-paragraph news of members, many serving in the Forces overseas: postings, wounds, prisoners of war, marriages, races and letters home. Alf Harley, writing from Blackpool, says that he went for a five miles cross-country run with 15 others (out of 5,000). "The spirit was willing, but the flesh was very weak—not to say much too substantial; however, I enjoyed my plod." Ken O'Kell is keeping fit with cycling and climbing the Derbyshire Peaks—another cross-country man gone west! He writes: "The Gazette is such fine reading after the shallow dribble of the daily press." Thanks for the compliment, Ken! Frank Webb is now an L.A.C. and is "on tour" again. Having "done" Lincolnshire, he had a brief stay in Yorkshire, and is now in Worcestershire for re-grading. In the meantime he has turned gardener. Reg Shepherd. We learn with regret that he was reported missing from air reconnaissance over Europe during May. Further news is awaited. Dennis Rodaway, now a Lieutenant, R.A.N.S., and looking remarkably well, came along to the first meeting at Tooting in May. Dick Norton, our very promising junior sprinter, is suffering from acute synovitis, sustained whilst playing football, and has been ordered not to run again for some months. Hard lines, Dick, and best wishes for a quick and complete disappearance of your trouble. Charlie Warren, an old-time walker from Erith, sends his best wishes to all his Belgrave acquaintances. Harold King, a former Club and Kent County Walking Champion, has had an operation on his eyes (cataract). He is now back at work and hopes to be a competitor in the next Brighton Walk. Syd King, an old-timer, and when turning out salvage recently, passed his news-cuttings and records on to the Hon. Secretary, who found them very interesting and will in turn pass them on to the Club Historian. Others, please copy. Fred Clay, apart from his sprinting abilities, has gained the Higher National Certificate in Mechanical Engineering. Congrats, Fred! Fred Brunning, who is a cyclist as well as a walker, tried his hand at gymnastics recently. When cycling through Balham, he tried a hand-spring on the handlebars, but landed in the road on his neck—which he gave a crick! However, a week's rest in hospital, with the sister of Joe and Jack Flower to hold his hand, soon put him right again. Les Bennett. Mrs. Bennett informs us that she has heard from Les at a Prisoner of War Camp in Japan. We rejoice with her on having heard from him after such a trying period. Communication is difficult, and further news is awaited. Charlie Churcher. Still winning races out in the Middle East. In one race he missed the record by four seconds. By now he may have beaten it. Sends his regards to all his many Belgrave friends, and would eagerly swop a stretch of sand for some of the roads round Wimbledon Common. Harry Churcher, now nearer to London, but unable to fit in any regular training. Turned out for the R.A.F. at the Epsom Meeting, but was disqualified. Hard luck, Harry! Hope we'll be seeing you on the road this winter. Joe Coleman writes: "Keep the flag flying, and when we all get back home after this "do" we'll show our appreciation for the Bels at home who have kept dear old Belgrave alive." Thanks, Joe, we will! Joe himself has turned out in one or two track walks and given good performances. Len Coleman, on the move again, last heard of at Sierra Leone. Spent a week-end at a French resort to which the Plymouth meeting seemed "like a baby show." To quote him further: "Vive L'Entente Cordiale!" Ted Jackman, transferred to Portsmouth (N.F.S.). Has recently been up to town for an operation on his foot. Percy Wright, in addition to the B.N.L., organises sports meetings and walks in Monmouth. When he can, he pops up to town for a race. Can still do with more Airgraphs for the "Overseas Cup." If you have any, he will be pleased to accept them at 14 Chapel Farm, Terrace, Cwmcarn, Newport, Mon. (Stop Press: Is now a Corporal. Congrats, Percy.) Eddie Jury is helping to put walking on the map again down Portsmouth way. Nice work, Eddie. Keep it going! Frank Thomson has now recovered from his illness and operation, and has been seen at meetings, complete with the inevitable scoring-board, and is very pleased to be with us again. Bill Fish, recovering from a serious illness, and was at Tooting on June 12th for the match v. L.F.F. Was very pleased to see the "boys" again. We are all sorry to hear of his illness and we all wish him a speedy and complete recovery. Charlie Cook. Still running! and has run in Veteran's sprint handicaps, and thereby been in the limelight in what few sporting columns we get in the press nowadays. George Still, no doubt, will be showing some of the lads around the common again—and leaving some of them behind! (Stop Press: He has!) Jimmy Flatt, although very busy, finds time for an occasional spin. At his local "Holidays at Home" sports he had to yield to a trio of Polish Commandos in the Mile. Max Quackenbos, or just "Quack," ran sixth in the American Athletic Union 3,000 Metres Steeplechase Championship, won by Joe McCluskey. Regularly sends sporting news from the U.S.A. Bert Footer, when we all thought he was many miles away, turns up at Imber Court for the match with the Police. Said something about "Commando Training" and "Fitness," and went out for a spin on the roads. In the excitement of seeing all the lads, he forgot to black his face, and to put a tree in his hair! He came back, the same old Bert! Sid Ring, now working in Cambridgeshire, and has had the misfortune to injure his knee, which caused him to retire from the Poly Marathon. We all know his potentialities at this distance, and hope that it will disappear so that he can run to his next year's schedule and give us another first-class performance. Reg Shotter, news has trickled through that he is now a Captain and is in India. Jimmy Green, resting for a while owing to leg trouble, and was unable to run for us at Sandhurst in consequence. Colin Sutton, with R.A.F. in India, has been laid up with stomach trouble, otherwise he reports very fit, and hoping to get some local competition. Jack Field, now in the Army, has been doing some running, giving a good account of himself. Norman Graves contacted Len Marchant at Hereford and in an Inter-Station race beat Len into eighth place. Norman won his R.A.F. Group Championship and had the honour of presenting a bouquet to the Air Commodore's wife. Good luck, Norman! Bill Hewitt, in the R.A.M.C. and now with the B.N.A.F., writes that he is now married. (All the very best, Bill.) He says that he has a jog along the sea shore before sun-up just to keep in trim. Well Bill, we shall look for you at Wimbledon after this lot's over. Albert Chetland still enjoys a spin over the Common, and writes of the "Espirit de Corps" silently running through the Club. Len Marchant led his station to victory in an Inter-Allied meeting at Birmingham. He won the 440 and 880 and gave his team a good lead in the 880 yards leg of the relay. William P. Roberts, the deaf and dumb sprint champion, was knocked down by a lorry and sustained a compound fracture of the left leg. He is getting along splendidly, and hopes to be able to resume next Track Season. George Long, seeing the country with the Marines, hasn't been able to do any running, but eagerly follows the fortunes of the Bels in the press. Frank King, caught a packet in the desert, but is making good progress. David Laing was married recently. Congratulations, David. Met a crowd of the "boys" at Tooting when on leave. Is now up in the wilds of Scotland. Leonard Smith has gained a commission and is now a 2nd Lieut., R.A.S.C. Was best man at David Laing's wedding. Tells of seeing "herds" of Belgravians on the road near Tooting. Jimmy Kemp sends a short, chatty letter from Wrotham, Kent. Len Spooner, now a Lieutenant, is at present in Palestine, and recently had an operation for hernia. We hope to hear that he will soon be racing again. Wally Ives sends very lengthy letters from India. Has sent a scarf and a handkerchief with the Club badge embroidered to help the Club funds; they will be on show in the Hall. Has been promoted to Bombardier. Congrats, Wally. Fred Rickards is keeping fit for post-war racing by a weekly cycle ride to Slough to visit his family. Bill Sutton writes: "On landing in Pantellaria I espied on the beach a spherical object which to the best of my recollection looked like a shot. On closer inspection it was like the very thing. I've done a bit of putting and find I can do 33 to 34 feet." In a later letter he says: "No wisecracks now, but I've been awarded the French "Croix de Guerre." Congratulations, Bill. We're all eagerly awaiting to hear the details. Laurie Jackson (Jacko) writing from Bishop Auckland, says:—"I'm still keeping well and am looking forward to a return to activity with the Field Events Section." Arthur Beaumont, now recovered from a bomb splinter in his elbow, got in the North African campaign. After a sojourn in hospital in Cairo, is now back with his unit. Len Herbert was married on May 24th. Our best wishes to them both. Is still amongst the top-liners over 2 and 3 miles. Bob MacMullen, jnr., also recently married. (All the best to you both.) Has been resting from competition for a few weeks, but is back on the road again. The Patience Brothers. Dan has been wounded. (N. Africa) and is now recovering up in Ross-shire. Alec has also been wounded, but has returned to his unit. Capt. Rod, we believe, is still in Scotland. Arthur Beales (Pilot Officer). We learn with regret that he is missing from air operations over Germany. It has since been learned that he is a prisoner-of-war and is uninjured. Charlie Smart sends a suggestion for a war-time Club vest—a Claret and Gold dics after the style of the A.A.A. badge. He also suggests that we promote a Ten Miles Open Road Race, to become an annual affair. Gets a party of eight out training regularly at his station. Nice work, Charlie! George Durrant, having convalesced at Halifax, is back with his unit at Catterick. He won the Inter-Squadron One and Three Miles. Says he is training regularly for the Championship, the results of which are awaited. Tommy Clinton, one of our Irish Guards members, writes from hospital that he was wounded just before Christmas, whilst on a landing trip. He lost all his running kit. Can anyone help him out? Tommy Scrimshaw is back in England after his long sojourn in Scotland. It was pleasing to see him "having a go" at Imber Court, but he obviously wasn't fit and lacked his usual finish. Jack Edwards writes from Tripolitania and sends his thanks for the Xmas card which chased him from Wales to Scotland, thence on to Libya, to reach him in June. He says that it helped to recall some of the happy times he had with the Bels. The Censor stamped across part of his address. Can any member let me have it? Cyril Pateman is still out in Ceylon, and is looking forward to the day when he can once again have a trot across the Common with the boys. "Remember me to all members, and I wish them every success." Sid Jones, writing from the M.E.F., says that he has competed in an International Sports meeting with Britain, New Zealand and S. Africa, and was most surprised at not meeting any other members there. Competed in the Shot and Discus. Ken Sheail, still with the B.N.A.F. and, having seen active service, is enjoying a well-earned rest. Hopes to be back in England shortly to renew acquaintance with "some of the grandest lads I've met." "O.H.M.S. Ashcombe" Jones, who, despite his two score years, has been passed "A.1," and also his proficiency tests, is enjoying himself in Derbyshire, and goes out with Derby and County over the plough. And what plough! You want to hear what "W.C." says about it! James Faulkner sends his regards to all Belgravians from B.N.A.F. He is a trooper with the R.A.C., and handles tanks. Michael Broadbent, our Junior Champion Sprinter, is now in the R.N.A.S., and further news is awaited. Teddy Read, we understand from Lilian, is in the Bengal jungle, amongst snakes and alligators, looking for Japs—apparently enjoying himself. Norman Shrubb is still out in India, very busy but happy, and has no inclination for running. Has contacted Teddy Read. Peter George is out in Canada doing his R.A.F. training. He says that he is enjoying the life and the country, and had a quick glance at New York on the way. Allan Lomas, our chubby Rutlish member, is now with the R.A.F. in Canada. Had a good journey out, a very happy week in Massachussetts, where the Americans gave him a good time—iced beer which you can't knock back quickly; but New Brunswick, where he is stationed, is "dry"—one has to have a licence to get a drink! Has had no opportunity yet for any training, and has taken up photography to record his travels. Best wishes to all Belgravians. John Quinlan, one of Jarlett's school, is now in the R.N. and stationed in Scotland. He wants to hear a few more items of sports news. Jack Flower, now a Captain, writes from the M.E.F. that he has met Bill Snell whilst doing a spot of training on the sand. Sends his regards and best wishes to all his old team-mates. Megaphone Man Cook has paid us several visits when on leave, but seems to have forgotten how to use the Meg! Bob Boyden, writing from Redhill, wants us to know how "Submarine" Footer managed to get into the Marines. What'll he say when he knows "Our Bert" is a Commando? Bob says "our young champ" for 1963 is getting along fine—good for you, Bob! Joe Daly, from Malta G.C., writes: "Many thanks for the 'Mag. It's great; it revives memories of fellows who slapped the back of the last man home just as hard as the winners, of Socials—a little rough sometimes, but never lacking in spirit." Sends hearty greetings to all Belgravians, and wants to know if there's any truth in the rumour about putting the Club Badge on the African Star? Ben May, Audrey and the youngster, send greetings from Bournemouth. His secretary says he's so busy nowadays that he finds little time for anything else but work! Ho! Ho! You must be putting on weight, Ben! Stan Botwright, despite having settled in billets in Stafford with his wife, made the journey to Sandhurst for the inter-club. He has represented both the R.A.F. and Jack Crump's team during the season, and picked up one or two pots for the bottom drawer for use when he returns to Bromley. Bill Snell writes from the M.E.F.: "Thanks a million for the May Gazette which I have just received (Aug.). Also thanks for the Xmas Card which arrived in June. It's a source of great comfort to us out here to know that you chaps are doing your best to keep the Club's colours flying high." Charlie Redgrave—Percy's Printer (B.N.L.)—despite so many calls upon his services finds just that little extra time to run off a few on the duplicator. Thanks a lot, Charlie! Has recently taken to hockey, and enjoys it. Charlie Jones has put in a grand job of work in holding together the Field Events Section. He knows the capabilities of all his men, and what is more, where to find some spare ones when necessary. He is also responsible for "putting the Club across" in the local press. Thank you, Charlie. Harry Shields: We often wonder how he gets through it all. You ring his office and are told he's away in Manchester or some other such place and won't be back for several days. But the teams are always there. How does he do it? Why, instead of complaining he's "too busy," he gets on with the job. Bill Merryman, still in Staffs, brought a team to London for Joe Binks' Whit Monday meeting, and his C.O. was very pleased with their performance. Bill won his unit 3 Miles Championship, and was third in the 1 Mile, and in the winning Medley Relay Team. Wishes the boys all the best. Bill Jones, still keeping our colours flying in Yorkshire, finished 23rd in the Bradford Whitsun Walk (15½ miles) in 2h. 37m. 35s. Jack Rutland has recently been promoted to Bombardier. Congrats, Jack. Comes up from Wales whenever he can for a race with the lads. Always full of enthusiasm, and looks forward to his visits. Tommy Green recently won the Hants County Road Walk Championship. Shall we have the pleasure of seeing him on the road again at Wimbledon? Ron Bryan, another Hampshire member, together with a colleague, cornered the four County Cross Country Championships. Will Rispin, M.E.F., wishes to be remembered to all his old associates at Belgrave Hall and is eagerly looking forward to the next "Mag." Dick Towndrow, now stationed in one of England's front lines, has an O.C. who actually encourages sport. Now that is good news, as football is generally the utmost limit, and if you are a runner you are looked upon as a crock. Or, as our old friend Len Fletcher once said, if you talk of walking—well you are thought to be taking out Blondie in the A.T.S. Len Camin, a football member, regrets he will not be able to do any C.C. running as his team is busy getting points in league and cup games. items.label: October 1943
items.sum: Belgrave beat Metropolitan Police A.C. 42-27 at Tooting Bec on 22 May 1943; the opening report of Ernie Duffett's 'Track Results for 1943'.
items.s: TRACK RESULTS FOR 1943. Belgrave beat Metropolitan Police A.C. 42-27 at Tooting Bec on 22 May 1943; the opening report of Ernie Duffett's 'Track Results for 1943'. Sat. May 22nd. v. Metropolitan Police A.C. at Tooting Bec. Track. We scored a fairly comfortable win over our opponents, who had Frank Close, the English International running for them. Fred Clay ran well in the 100 Yards and also won the Long Jump for the Club, and we were pleased to see Tom Wiley out again. Les Cohen ran a good race in the 2 Miles, and Syd Jarlett and young Dave Main beat Moody, the Police Champion, in the 880 Yards. Eddie Pack also made a welcome reappearance, and we hope he will soon regain the form which took him into an A.A.A. Final and a place in the Empire Games Team which visited Australia. items.s: Sat. June 12th. v. London Fire Force S.A. at Tooting Bec Track. Belgrave, helped by three Poly men, beat the London Fire Force S.A. 53-22 at Tooting Bec on 12 June 1943, with a 2 Miles Walk added to the programme. We had a strong side out for this match and were strengthened by the inclusion of Doug. Wilson, M. J. Wright, and B. W. Metcalfe, of the Poly, who are again assisting us this season. We had the individual winner of every track event and Frank Abberton, who was on leave, ran well to win the 2 Miles. Doug. Wilson had an easy win in the 880 Yards and Syd Jarlett beat Norman Day in very good time for the 440 Yards. Young Clay scored a fine sprint double, and we were glad to see Willie Nankeville, our young Southern Junior Champion turning out again, although not over his usual distance. A 2 Miles Walk was included in the programme, and a very big field turned out for this, there being a Belgrave v. The Rest match, which J. Morris, the much improved Police walker, won from C. T. items.s: Saturday, July 10th. v. Walton A.C. at Tooting Bec Track. Belgrave beat Walton A.C. 53-27 at Tooting Bec on 10 July 1943 after Dartford Harriers and the Royal Norwegian Air Force cried off. This fixture was originally a match with Dartford Harriers, but they could not make the trip to Town, and the Royal Norwegian Air Force who were coming along in their place, were also forced to cancel at the last minute. We are very indebted to the Walton boys for coming along and making a match of it, althought being only a young club, they were rather outmatched. Stan Botwright, looking very fit in his R.A.F. uniform, came along to win the 100 Yards, and young John Brown scored a good double, winning the 880 Yards and 1 Mile. B. W. Metcalfe won the 220 Yards for us, while M. J. Wright sportingly ran for Walton in the sprints. Placings of our members are given hereunder:— 100 Yards—1 Botwright (B); 2 Metcalfe (B). items.s: Saturday, August 21st. v. West Middx. Triangle and Dartford H. at Tooting Bec Track. A weakened Belgrave side lost 34-32 to a combined West Middx. Triangle and Dartford team at Tooting Bec on 21 August 1943. Owing to Dartford only having a few men evailable, they combined forces with the Triangle and a very close match resulted. We were much below our usual strength owing to other fixtures on the same day, and so far as Athletics are concerned it would seem as if we are getting back to peace-time conditions with the A.A.A. matches taking the pick of club sides! Les Cohen ran a grand race to win the 1 Mile, while Tom Carter showed a return to his old form in winning the 2 Miles in the good time of 9m. 57s. Stan Blunden ran well to win the 220 Yards, and our representatives for the 440 were Alf Shaw and Les Cohen! George Powell had a field day in winning three field events, while young Hendry showed the results of Charlie Jones' careful coaching in clearing his highest jump of the season. items.s: Saturday, May 22nd. Juniors v. Whitgift Middle School at Tooting Bec Track. Belgrave Juniors, helped by Polytechnic Juniors, lost 26-25 to Whitgift Middle School at Tooting Bec on 22 May 1943. For this match we had the assistance of several Polytechnic Juniors and a very close match resulted. Grieve of the Whitgift scored a fine sprint double with Brant of the Poly second in both races. Quinlan set a rare pace in the 880 Yards only to be beaten down the straight, and he should improve with better racing tactics. Boddy ran well to finish second in the 1 Mile, while De Knop, the Middlesex Junior champion, won the 440 Yards and Long Jump. We also won the 4 x 220 Yards race, but when the points had been counted up we were 1 on the wrong side! items.s: Thursday, June 10th. Juniors v. Whitgift Middle School on the School Ground at Croydon. Belgrave Juniors lost 32-19 to Whitgift Middle School on the school ground at Croydon on 10 June 1943. Grieve, of the School, once again won both sprints, although young Peter Vine was a good runner-up in both races, and this finely-built young man should prove a good addition to our sprinting strength. John Brown also displayed fine form in winning the 1 Mile in impressive style, and is another Junior who should make a name for himself. Dick Norton, who owing to leg trouble has had to forego sprinting for the present, turned out in the Weight and won with a very good effort. Also in the High Jump a promising youngster named Stirling competed for us and later ran in the 880 Yards and showed quite good running ability. The School, however, were too strong for our lads, although they showed the School a thing or two later on at the supper table! We much appreciated the School's hospitality, and look forward to next year's meeting. Seniors please note! items.s: Saturday, August 21st. Juniors v. Dorking St. Paul's A.C. at Tooting Bec Track. Belgrave Juniors lost 32-22 to Dorking St. Paul's A.C. at Tooting Bec on 21 August 1943, with fast wins by John Brown and Heathfield. Once again we were under strength for this match with the sporting Dorking boys, but even so some of our lads put up some very fine performances. John Brown won the 880 Yards in the fine time of 2m. 5.5s., which beat the time of the Senior half on the same afternoon! Young Heathfield also ran a sterling race to win the 440 Yards in 55.4s., which also beat the Senior match time. Charlie Jones adopted Junior status for the afternoon and won two events, his Hop, Step & Jump effort being particularly good. Young "Rodney" Stone, a regular chip off the old block, competed in both sprint races, and although running very green, he showed plenty of "guts" and was credited with a place in each. items.sum: Belgrave's young runners and field-event men finished third behind R.A.F. Halton and the Surrey A.T.C. at Halton on 17 July 1943.
items.s: v. R.A.F. (Halton). 17th July. Belgrave's young runners and field-event men finished third behind R.A.F. Halton and the Surrey A.T.C. at Halton on 17 July 1943. A marvellous day, and those who made the long journey were unanimous that it was well worth it. The R.A.F. got together a good team, and a third team was made by the champions of the Surrey A.T.C. The fixture was well supported by the Field Events Section and the younger runners; the absence of the Seniors was a disappointment to our hosts. A good crowd had gathered, and the track was in very good trim. The 100 Yards, won in 10.1s., saw Peter Vine about a yard away with Hayes fourth. Peter stepped into the breach and tackled the quarter, and was a good third in 54.1. Alan Bishop having an "off" day was fifth. The quarter obviously upset Peter's running in the furlong, in which he was fifth, Hayes gaining third place. In between races Hayes had been tackling the Long Jump, and finding it not to his liking, left it to Charles Jones to jump 18ft. 6in. for third place, the winner doing 21ft. 9in. In the half Alan Bishop drew a blank. Charlie Jones and Hendry tackled the High Jump in which Hendry failed at 5ft. 2in., complaining of bruised heels. Melchoir, Powell and Jerry Thompson were doing good work and bringing home the points. The Shot was won by the A.T.C., using the 12lb. shot. Jerry, using the 16-pounder, was second with 35ft. 4in. In the Discus Melchoir was second with 100ft. 1in. and George Powell third with 97ft. 6in. Melchoir (160ft. 10in.) and Powell (147ft. 9in.) took the first two places in the Javelin. Vine, Jones, Bishop and Watts, although tired, ran a good third in the 4 x 110 Yards Relay. The One Mile, Two Miles and Hurdles had to be missed. Our best thanks to Flight-Lieut. Caddy for the welcome he gave our boys and for the much appreciated tea afterwards. Final scores were:— 1 Halton, 56; 2 A.T.C., 51; 3 Belgrave, 22. items.h: SOUTHERN JUNIOR CHAMPIONSHIPS.. POLTECHNIC STADIUM, JUNE 19th.
items.sum: Short report on Belgrave juniors at the Southern Junior Championships at the Polytechnic Stadium on 19 June.
items.s: SOUTHERN JUNIOR CHAMPIONSHIPS.. POLTECHNIC STADIUM, JUNE 19th. Short report on Belgrave juniors at the Southern Junior Championships at the Polytechnic Stadium on 19 June. In the 100 Yards Peter Vine won his heat in 11.7. but was unplaced in the second round. Later on he was unsuccessful in the 220 Yards. Nankeville won his heat in the 880 Yards in 2m. 10s., showing a fine action. In the Final he was beaten in the last few strides in 2m. 6.6s. In Quinlan's heat the runners ran in a bunch for three-quarters of the distance; John was fairly well boxed in, and in the final dash was fourth. Bates too was fourth in his heat. Bishop put up a good fight in the Quarter, but was unable to qualify. In the One Mile. John Brown ran almost faultlessly to win his heat in 4m. 51s. In the Final he dropped out when lying fourth. Joels and Kennett were our representatives in the One Mile Walk, but were unplaced, their respective mentors. Alan Robins and Joe Wilson will no doubt keep a fatherly eye on them on the road this winter. items.s: AROUND THE MEETINGS. Round-up of Belgrave members' performances at open meetings in summer 1943 (Epsom, Kingston, Walthamstow, White City, Acc and Tabb, Fulham A.R.P., Harrow C.D., Clapham A.T.C., Sutton, Banstead, Erith, Maidenhead), mostly two-mile team races and relays. Epsom, 2nd June. "Holidays at Home" in a thunderstorm! Three Miles Team Race—1 Cohen, 15.47; 2 Close (Epsom); 4 Beer; 6 Morrell; 8 Main; 12 Shaw; 13 Speaight; 14 Shields; 23 Jannaway; First team—28 points, 4 to score. Kingston (Whit Monday). Two Miles Team Race.—Tom Morrell was second, with Beer, Shaw and Speaight completing the team. Alan Robbins was third in the Two Miles Walk. Walthamstow (Whit Monday). Two Miles Team Race.—Cohen winning from Jimmy Green in 10m. 1s., with Carter fifth. David Main won the One Mile Handicap off 125 yards in 4.20. White City (Whit Monday). Len Herbert was beaten by the New Zealander, Johnson, in 9m. 34s. Stan Botwright was third in the Scratch 440 Yards. Acc and Tabb, 26th June. Truly a Belgrave meeting with Ernie Duffett the "big noise." On a downhill track Freddie Clay won his heat in the 100 Yards off 6¾ in 9.8. Peter Vine was beaten by an American by inches in 9.7. Clay proved a winner in the Final, and completed the "double" by winning the furlong off 15 in 22s., Jim Harding being second a few inches away. In the 880 Yards John Brown, off 68, won in 1m. 56s., with Main third, Blunden fourth, and Bishop sixth. In the Two Miles Team we turned out three teams, but Finchley had the measure of us, finishing 1.3 and 4 to win by 7 points (3 to score). Jimmy Green made a game effort and was beaten in the run in. Bert Shaw was 6th, Carter 7th, Beer 9th, Morrell 10th, Shields 16th, Walker 18th, Penny 21st, Tobin 22nd, Taylor 23rd, and Jannaway 29th. In the Closed Events, Syd Jarlett, Bill Speaight and Alf Bishop were amongst the prizewinners. Fulham A.R.P. 1st July, at Stamford Bridge. Two Miles Team Race.—1 J. Green; 2 Cohen; 8 Shaw. Time: 10m. 0.2s. Team Race: 1 Belgrave H. Harrow C.D. 3rd July. Clay, Watts and Blunden qualified for the 220 Yards Handicap Final. Clay was third. In the Invitation Scratch 880 Yards won by our Poly friend Doug. Wilson in 2m. 0.1s, Len Marchant was 4th and Syd Jarlett 5th. David Main off 110 won the Invitation One Mile Handicap in 4m. 16s. Jimmy Green was 2nd and Les Cohen 3rd. Syd Wooderson clocked 4m. 29s. off scratch. In the Three Miles Handicap Shields was 5th and Taylor 6th. We fielded two teams in the Scratch One Mile Medley Relay. "A" Team (Jarlett, Blunden, Clay and Marchant) were 3rd, and "B" Team (Simmonds, Watts, Main and White were 5th. The Poly won in 3.48. Clapham A.T.C. 7th July. Peter Dunn, one of Syd Jarlett's School, won the 220 in 28.2, the 440 in 64.5, the 880 in 2.32, 110 Hurdles in 18.9, and the Long Jump 16ft. He was also 3rd in the Shot Putt with 25ft. 3½in., and was in the winning team of the Relay. Truly a Victor Ludorum! Sutton, Surrey. July 10th. Two Miles Team.—2 Cohen; 3 Green; 6 Shaw; 7 Carter; 9 Main; 11 Shields; 12 Tobin; 13 Taylor; 22 Eeles. Winners' Time 10m. 2s. Team Result—1st, Belgrave "A," 11 pts; 3rd, Belgrave "B," 27 pts. George Weston, who has been amongst the prizewinners recently, won the 100 yards (over 40) from scratch. Banstead. July 17th. Two Miles Team Race.—1 Herbert; 4 Cohen; 5 Green; 7 Shaw; 10 Taylor; 20 Eeles. Time 9m. 46s. Erith. "Holidays at Home," 31st July. A hotbed of Belgravianism!! Shades of Bob Ricketts! Bob, who was working for Vickers during the last war made this same Recreation Gound his training home. Here he also found many members, some of whom were helping at this meeting. Amongst these were Charlie Warren, Harold King, T. Moore, Jacques and Luther, all of whom sent their best wishes to THE Club. A team comprising Jarlett, Clay, Brown and Jones, won the Mile Medley Relay from scratch in 3m. 50s. In the Two Miles Shaw (2nd), Taylor (3rd), and Carter (5th) won with a score of 10 points. The "B" Team (Beer 7th, Morrell 12th, and Shields 14th, were 4th. Eeles was 17th. Bert Shaw, on "his own dung heap," ran a remarkable race and made a desperate attempt to win. He was ably supported by Alf Taylor who showed a return to some of his old C.C. form. In the Two Miles Walk, Joe Wilson, who finished 5th, was presented with a medal given by J. A. Sullivan, South African A.A.A., for the individual competitor who, in the opinion of the referee (Wally Jewell) put up the best performance at the meeting. Walthamstow. August 1st. items.label: October 1943
items.sum: Syd Roberts's review of the Belgrave walkers' 1943 summer season, with results of walks from the L.F.F. Inter Sports Match to the L.C.C. 1 Mile Final at Parliament Hill.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Syd Roberts's review of the Belgrave walkers' 1943 summer season, with results of walks from the L.F.F. Inter Sports Match to the L.C.C. 1 Mile Final at Parliament Hill. The Summer Season, just finished, has been one of great activity, both on the track and the road, and in both sections our walkers have given a good account of themselves, despite their hard work during the winter. The season's laurels, however, go to our old friend Tommy Green for his win in the Hants County 10 Miles Championship. Eddie Jury, another of our Hants walkers, chose to walk in the Highgate 20 on the same day, otherwise we should most probably have had two in the first three. In the Two Miles Championship, however, he took third place, with Tommy Green fourth, and Junior Green fifth—quite a good Club performance. Our other walkers to distinguish themselves during the season are J. Robins, who has been placed in no fewer than six races, and A. Readman, who took second place in the Police Championship. Percy Wright, still going strong with his promotions in Wales, was no doubt very bucked to have Robins with him on two occasions. Percy still continues the good work with the B.N.L., and once again stresses the importance of passing it on as quickly as possible. News still comes in of the activity of our walkers abroad. They are certainly maintaining the high reputation of the Club, and we wish them every success. The following are the results of races held since our last issue:— L.F.F. INTER SPORTS MATCH. Paddington, 22/5/43. In this novel event the cyclists rode 24 miles, the runners covered 10 miles and the walkers 7 miles, the latter two teams being on different courses on the road. The cyclists won by an easy margin, the first four clocking 23 minutes faster than the runners. The difference between the runners and walkers, however, was much less, the former winning by the small margin of 19 seconds. Times of winners of each section were Cyclist 52-35. G. items.label: October 1943
items.sum: Charlie Jones's review of the Belgrave field events section's 1943 season and its members.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS NEWS. Charlie Jones's review of the Belgrave field events section's 1943 season and its members. The season which has just closed has shown that the Field Events men made a fine contribution to the Club's successes in the summer matches. We have been glad to welcome a few new members to the Section. Two of them, in "Jerry" Thompson, a heavyweight Shot Putter whose best effort of 39ft. 1in. when he won the A.A.A. Handicap at Tooting, was very good; and Guy Hendry, who shows promise of becoming a really good high jumper, have already shown their worth. Hendry is quite young. and by assiduously studying technique. looks as if he will master the "Western roll" very soon. Charlie Stirling and Roy Woodhead are also jumpers of promise. Charlie Melchoir and George Powell have again shown up well in the Javelin, and lent valuable assistance in the Shot and Discus events. Charlie has again been honoured by the A.A.A. in representative matches. His best effort of the season was over 170 feet. In the Long Jump we have had to rely upon Tom Wiley, who a number of times has reached 21 feet. He has been supported by Frank Simmons, Stan Blunden, and our Captain. Jack Quarton has also lent his assistance in this event in addition to the Shot and Discus. We have been pleased to have the help of A. W. Lewis, the Welsh International, in the Shot and Discus events in a number of matches. News has been received that Sid Jones, our Shot Putt Champion, who is a sapper in North Africa, was honoured by being selected to represent Great Britain in a match at Cairo against South Africa, New Zealand and Canada. He was fourth in the Shot with a putt of 36ft. 1½in. and third in the Discus with a throw of 110ft. 4in. News of another well-known member of the Section also in the Middle East, in Bill Sutton, will be found on another page, and also an obituary notice of the late Pat Ridge, one of our Shot and Discus men. items.label: October 1943
items.sum: Notes on Belgrave members' long-distance road races in 1943: the Kent 20, Red Cross Ten, Poly Marathon, Reading 10 and S.L.H. 30.
items.s: MARATHON NOTES. Notes on Belgrave members' long-distance road races in 1943: the Kent 20, Red Cross Ten, Poly Marathon, Reading 10 and S.L.H. 30. A few of our members have appeared in the long distance runs this year. In the "Kent 20", on May 8th, our team repeated their performance in the Finchley 20 by running S.L.H. a close second. Sid Ring was second to T. Richards (Mitcham A.C.). Mick Walker was 3rd, Dick Towndrow was 4th, and Bert Mitchell 20th. The Red Cross "Ten" Race, held simultaneously with a 24-miles cycle race and 7-miles road walk, was a unique race, and a good crowd saw the three races start at the same moment. Ten 1-mile laps were covered, and over one stretch the same road and path used by the walkers were used. Charlie Smart was third in 58m. 49s, Sid Ring 4th in 59.35, and Mick Walker 6th in 60.11. Doubleday was 15th, and Bert Mitchell 22nd. Scoring 3 a side on time aggregate, we recorded 2h. 58m. 35s. to win by over 2 minutes from Reading A.C., who totalled 3.1.18. L.F.F. were third with 3.1.47. Charlie Smart very sportingly passed his team prize to the first non-scoring member—the Hon. Editor. Many thanks, Charlie! In the Poly Marathon (26 miles 385 yds.), held on a four-lap course from Chiswick Stadium, Micky Walker, nursing a gammy leg, was 8th in 3h. 8m. Doubleday was 15th, just inside 3h. 18m. Sid Ring had to retire owing to trouble from a knee injury. One of our Police walkers, Jim Watson, made a plucky first effort, but retired at 22 miles. Our sole competitor in the Reading "10" was Fred White, who ran well to finish 11th in 65m. 10s. In the S.L.H. "30", held at Coulsdon on Sept. 25th, over four laps of 7½ miles, Doubleday finished 16th in 3h. 59m. 4s., and gained a time standard medal by finishing within 45 minutes of the winner, G. Humphreys, S.L.H. Mention must be made of the very good running of our Fire Force runner, George Hoath. He was first in the Red Cross Ten in 57.25, first in the Reading Ten, and, after leading at 20 miles, was third in the Poly Marathon. In addition, he has many good performances on the track to his credit. We all know what George can do over the country, and no doubt he will be the spearhead of the L.F.F. team this winter. items.label: October 1943
items.h: A FLIGHT OF FANCY INTO THE FUTURE.
items.sum: Imaginative piece written as a 1960 newspaper extract describing a grand future for Belgrave Harriers.
items.s: A FLIGHT OF FANCY INTO THE FUTURE. Imaginative piece written as a 1960 newspaper extract describing a grand future for Belgrave Harriers. EXTRACT FROM "THE DAILY PRESS" DATED APRIL, 1960. As I look down on the swirl of traffic which flows eastwards through Hyde Park towards the new Double Cross-over traffic bridge at Piccadilly Circus, my thoughts turn on this Spring morning through the years, and I ponder on the position the Belgrave Harriers have now attained when contrasted with their humble origins of nearly seventy-five years ago. I am sitting in one of the offices devoted to the production of "The Belgravian," lavishly illustrated these days and published weekly, and recognised as the leading authority on all matters concerning Athletics. These offices form part of the magnificent building in Knightsbridge, which houses the Club's Town Headquarters and preserves its associations with the City of Westminster, and from which training takes place most evenings over Rotten Row. At Wimbledon the Belgrave Harriers still have their week-end headquarters now situated on Common Side; and every Saturday throughout the winter hundreds of athletes in the familiar claret and gold enjoy their favourite sport on the neighbouring roads and common land. The Club still maintains its reputation for sportsmanship, athletic ability, and sociability and has consistently refused to allow wealth, or position, or influence to interfere with its principles. Some interesting customs continue; and the Club jealously safeguards its proud athletic reputation and does everything possible to ensure that Athletics is still its primary purpose. The Committee many years ago realised in its wisdom that the facilities the Club can offer, which are unrivalled anywhere in the world, might well attract a type of member who was merely interested in its restaurant, its billiard room, its luxurious lounges, with no interests in running, walking, or field events; and so all members are called upon during their first ten years of membership to make at least twenty appearances in athletic races or competions each year. The subscription remains at the humble few shillings which ruled at the commencement of the Second World War; and the frequent Social evenings are still a great feature of the Club life. The Club's history is a momumental example of loyalty to ideals. As far back as the 1920's, the Club's Committee had thoughts on acquiring its own Headquarters. These ideals were pursued by an increasing number of enthusiasts, until in 1936 the Club's first leasehold was purchased. Still the ideals gathered momentum, and whilst the War of 1939—1945 caused a slight slowing down of efforts owing to the presence of so many members in the Armed Forces, the years following Peace enabled the ideals of many hundreds of members to be crystallised into reality, in the form of handsome premises in Westminster and Wimbledon. It must be admitted that the Club hardly expected to be owners of such magnificent quarters in such a comparitively short time; but the new outlook towards Amateur sport which followed the winning of the War, plus a munificent grant from the Anglo-American Philantropic Association for the finest example of "self help" in the first half of the Twentieth Century, together with the funds accumulated by decades of enthusiastic Club members, made all things possible. Many of the Club's members have gained positions of considerable importance in our present-day world. A notable example is bluff Sir Harry Shields, Bart., whose contributions to the solution of post-War traffic problems are well known; and whose baronetcy derives mainly from the original and brilliant idea of bringing all London's Underground train services to the surface, and of directing all surface routes underground. He recently unveiled a marble tablet on the Water Tower at Colley Hill, commemorating an incident of his youth. Lord Parker, of New Malden, to whom much of the credit for the Belgrave Harriers' progress goes, was awarded his peerage in the Peace Honours List "for distinguished services to Amateur Athletics and the public." It is said that his constant and ever-increasing use of postcards represented all the difference between profit and loss in the Post Office accounts during the 1930—1940 decade. Tom Cotton, M.P. for the Battersea Park Division, is universally known for his fighting speeches in the House and his consummate command of language; and is ably supported from the back benches by A. W. Penny, whose rallying call of "Up, Surrey!" has often been heard in the House. The erstwhile cross-country champion, Bert Footer, now leads a quiet life in the bosom of his family as "Mine Host" at "The Spiked Shoe," Putney Heath. It will be remembered that on leaving the Royal Marines, Footer secretly married Miss "Fluffy" Blonde from the "Windmill" Theatre; and later became Minister for Cross-Country Running in the 1948 Administration; a position he later resigned on account of a broken blood vessel brought about by constantly throwing his papers to the ground and retrieving them at a rapid rate, when discussing the selection of the 1949 International Team. Gordon Doubleday is Managing Director of "Nutty Foods Limited"; and Tommy Green is Mayor of Eastleigh permanently. Charlie Churcher can be seen with his attractive wife at all the Club Social events, dancing with all his former grace to which is allied these days, an Egyptian mysticism. Percy Wright is leader of the Welsh Nationalist Party (how time brings changes!); Frank Webb remains a bachelor and pursues his sinuous course; and so on . . . One could continue for a long while following the careers of those who have carried the claret and gold vest with distinction on the road, cross-country, on the track, and in the field events; but space will not permit these interesting meanderings. To all who have contributed to the amazing success of the Belgrave Harriers in the past; to those who help to guide and maintain its traditions in our time; a great debt of gratitude is due from the World, for these amateur sportsmen have shown that ideals worth pursuing and fighting for can come to realisation. There is a message in their achievements for all of us. And so we wish the Belgrave Harriers continuing success. Success in the Athletic field and success in the wider field of sporting endeavour are certain to be theirs in increasing measure as the Club approaches its Centenary Year; and as the subsequent centuries succeed one another until the end of Time. items.label: October 1943
items.sum: Report of the Belgrave Harriers Annual General Meeting at Belgrave Hall on 9th October 1943, with the officers and committee elected.
items.s: THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING: Report of the Belgrave Harriers Annual General Meeting at Belgrave Hall on 9th October 1943, with the officers and committee elected. Belgrave Hall, 9th October. In the absence of the President, Harry Evans, who was unavoidably absent, Alf Harley took the Chair. The meeting opened with the company standing in silence in homage and remembrance of those members who had passed away since the last A.G.M. The Hon. Secretary, in his report, said that our runners and walkers had all given good accounts of themselves, not only at home, but in other parts of the country, and, indeed across the seas. One encouraging feature was the number of new members elected during the year—83. He praised the work done by Club officials, and thanked them for their support and co-operation. The Hon. Treasurer then presented his report, and began by thanking the Hon. Secretary for much valuable help during the year. He explained the details of the Balance Sheet, paying tribute to the excellent work done by the Building Fund Committee and Les Cohen. All things considered, our financial position was good. Before the adoption of the accounts was moved, the Chairman interposed with a few words in praise of our Hon. Auditor (Jimmy Belchamber) who had held this important office for 31 years. Tom Morrell, on behalf of the Committee, proposed that Les Cohen be made an Hon. Life Member. He spoke of the good work done by Les on behalf of the Building Fund, of his excellent performances over the country and on the track, and of his regular support of Club fixtures, and of his Club spirit. Percy Wright seconded, and Les was duly elected. Les modestly but thankfully accepted the honour the Club had bestowed on him. Next came the election of Officers. Harry Parker, with George Powell seconding, proposed that Harry Evans be re-elected as President for a second year of office. This was carried. The existing Vice-Presidents, with the exception of G. Harwood (deceased) and J. Sawyer (deceased) were re-elected en bloc. The other Officials were then elected (mostly re-elected!):— Hon. Secretary, H. Parker; Hon. Treasurer, W. G. Webb; Walking Hon. Secretary, S. C. Roberts; Running Hon. Secretary, E. A. Duffett; Field Eevents Hon. Secretary, T. C. Jones; Cross Country Captain, C. T. Carter; Track Captain, H. W. Shields; Walking Captain, A. Readman; Junior Captain, F. Clay; Starter, A. Fell; Timekeepers, C. Cook and J. Turner; Hon. Handicappers: Running, E. Duffett; Walking, S. C. Roberts; Hon. Auditor, J. B. Belchamber; Trustees, F. G. Thomson and E. Gordon. The following were elected to the Committee:— F. W. Brunning, L. J. Cohen, G. S. Doubleday, S. Jarlett, T. Morrell, G. H. Powell, R. J. Savage, A. R. Shaw, C. H. Speechley, and A. E. Taylor. Two proposals were then discussed and referred to the Committee. They were the possibility of organising Socials or Dances, and of promoting a Ten Miles Open Road Race. Before concluding the meeting the Chairman expressed his gratification at coming to such an enthusiastic gathering. He drew attention to the fact that when the Cross-Country and Road Walking Championships were held again, our winning teams of 1939 would be five, six or even ten years older!; and was pleased to see that we were developing our young new members into teams worthy of defending our role of dual champions. He then closed the meeting and a vote of thanks was passed to him for the able manner in which he had conducted the meeting.
